title: P0201 – Cylinder 1 Injector A Circuit/Open
text: P0201: Cylinder 1 Injector A Circuit/Open. P0201 reports an electrical fault, mainly an open circuit, in the injector circuit of cylinder 1. The engine module watches each injector output: GM flags an open circuit at an impedance of 200 kΩ or more – on direct injection and diesel engines in 10 of 20 or 5 of 10 samples and with the warning light in the first trip, on some port-injected engines only after two trips. Ford's port injection reads a fault bit from the driver chip that covers open, short to ground and short to voltage alike; Ford diesels report only the open circuit here and shorts as P0261/P0262. On direct injection the affected injector is switched off; the cylinder misfires. Common causes: Connector at the cylinder 1 injector loose, corroded or with a broken or pushed-back pin (high likelihood); Injector coil open (medium likelihood); Wire between module and injector open or chafed (heat, rodents) (medium likelihood); Injector supply missing (fuse, relay) – then usually several cylinders at once (low likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301; Loss of power, rough idle; Limp mode possible on diesel and direct injection. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P020A – Cylinder 1 Injection Timing
text: P020A: Cylinder 1 Injection Timing. P020A reports a fault in the injection timing of cylinder 1 on a diesel engine. Unlike P01CB/P01CC ('over retarded/advanced', the result of the injector learning routine in overrun), this code has no direction, and what it checks is up to the manufacturer. GM uses it as an electrical check on a four-cylinder diesel and on the 6.6 litre L5P Duramax V8: at every injection the engine module measures how long the injector current takes to reach its pull-in level of 13 A. If on the V8 that time is outside 60–150 µs in 10 of 20 samples, the code sets and the warning light comes on in the first trip. FCA lists it for the 3.0 litre EcoDiesel V6 together with the learning codes: check injector coding, charge air leaks and the injector clamp, reset the zero fuel calibration and repeat the learning drive; if the code returns, the injector is replaced. Common causes: Injector of cylinder 1 faulty (coil, armature, wear, deposits) (high likelihood); Injector wiring or connector: contact resistance, corrosion, chafing (medium likelihood); Engine software sets the code falsely (update available for some models) (medium likelihood); Injector driver stage or boost voltage in the engine module (low likelihood); Wrong injector code, contaminated fuel or loose injector clamp (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Rough running or misfire, rough idle; Loss of power, smoke or knocking possible. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0210 – Cylinder 10 Injector A Circuit/Open
text: P0210: Cylinder 10 Injector A Circuit/Open. P0210 reports an electrical fault, mainly an open circuit, in the injector circuit of cylinder 10. The engine module watches each injector output: GM flags an open circuit at an impedance of 200 kΩ or more – on direct injection and diesel engines in 10 of 20 or 5 of 10 samples and with the warning light in the first trip, on some port-injected engines only after two trips. Ford's port injection reads a fault bit from the driver chip that covers open, short to ground and short to voltage alike; Ford diesels report only the open circuit here and shorts as P0288/P0289. Cylinder 10 exists only on ten-cylinder engines; documented is Ford's 6.8 litre V10, whose check covers P0201 to P0210 with the warning light. Common causes: Connector at the cylinder 10 injector loose, corroded or with a broken or pushed-back pin (high likelihood); Injector coil open (medium likelihood); Wire between module and injector open or chafed (heat, rodents) (medium likelihood); Injector supply missing (fuse, relay) – then usually several cylinders at once (low likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0310; Loss of power, rough idle; Limp mode possible on diesel and direct injection. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0213 – Cold Start Injector 1
text: P0213: Cold Start Injector 1. A cold start injector is an additional injector in the intake manifold that sprays extra fuel for a few seconds while a cold engine is cranked. In classic Bosch systems a thermo-time switch on the block powers it directly, without the engine module – such systems cannot set a code at all. A code is only possible where the engine module drives the valve and monitors its circuit, as CARB requires for output components. From the 1990s the main injectors took over cold-start enrichment, so the code only fits early OBD II engines. P0213 concerns cold start injector 1. No manufacturer using it was found in GM, Ford or Saab documents. Common causes: Connector or wire corroded or open (high likelihood); Valve coil open or valve stuck (medium likelihood); Thermo-time switch or control relay faulty (medium likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Poor cold start, long cranking in cold weather; Leaking valve: hot-start problems, flooding, black smoke. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0215 – Engine Shutoff Solenoid
text: P0215: Engine Shutoff Solenoid. The engine shutoff solenoid is the electric stop valve on older diesel injection pumps, mainly distributor pumps. It is energised with the ignition on and lets fuel into the pump; with no current a spring closes it, the pump runs dry and the engine stops – also as a safety backup if the governor fails. P0215 reports a fault in this solenoid or its supply, typically a broken coil, a sticking plunger, a blown fuse or relay, or a wiring fault. The result is either an engine that will not start or dies, or one that keeps running after switch-off. Newer diesels stop through the injectors or a fuel shutoff valve with its own codes P0005–P0007. No manufacturer document describing P0215 was found; the description rests on CARB's requirements for output components and a Bosch patent on the valve. Common causes: Shutoff solenoid faulty (open coil, sticking plunger) (high likelihood); Relay or fuse in the supply circuit faulty (high likelihood); Broken wire, corrosion or ground fault at the pump connector (medium likelihood); Pump control module faulty (low likelihood); Engine module driver faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine does not start or stalls while driving; Engine keeps running after ignition off (solenoid stuck open); Check engine light on; Stumbling with a loose contact. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0216 – Injector/Injection Timing Control Circuit
text: P0216: Injector/Injection Timing Control Circuit. P0216 is a diesel code for the control of injection timing. On 1990s distributor pumps with an electronic timing advance it meant that actual injection timing missed its target; today manufacturers use it for the electronic injector control, with different meanings. GM's Duramax diesels compare, inside the engine module, the summed injection pulse widths from the hardware driver with those calculated by the software; a mismatch in 30 of 124 or 60 consecutive checks sets the code with the warning light in the first trip. On GM's 3.0 litre LM2 it appeared together with P0202 from a broken pin in the injector 2 connector. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel uses it for a fault in the separate injector power stage. The result can be loss of power, rough running, smoke and limp mode. Common causes: Injector harness or connector (broken pin) – common rail (medium likelihood); Engine module or injector power stage faulty internally (medium likelihood); Distributor pump electronics or timing advance faulty (medium likelihood); Low supply pressure on distributor pumps (lift pump, filter) (medium likelihood); Pump installed incorrectly, drive gear misaligned (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Loss of power, limp mode; Rough running, jerking; Hard starting or stalling (distributor pump), smoke. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0217 – Engine Coolant Over Temperature Condition
text: P0217: Engine Coolant Over Temperature Condition. P0217 is a condition code: the engine module reports that coolant temperature has passed a protection threshold. The limit and the reaction depend on the manufacturer – Saab's 2.2 diesel sets it at 120 °C for over 10 s, limits fuel quantity and suspends EGR and boost diagnostics until the temperature drops; heavy-duty diesels cut power sharply and may shut down; Ford petrol engines use their own code P1299 and cut fuel to individual cylinders. Whether the warning light comes on varies, because CARB exempts overheat protection that only engages once the gauge reads red. Usual causes are low coolant, a thermostat stuck closed, a failed fan or water pump – but Ford traced some cases to a faulty coolant sensor or harness. Common causes: Low coolant (leak, head gasket) (high likelihood); Thermostat stuck closed (high likelihood); Radiator fan, fan clutch or water pump faulty, radiator clogged (medium likelihood); Coolant temperature sensor or harness faulty (false reading) (medium likelihood); Extreme load (towing, gradient, heat) with an intact cooling system (low likelihood). Symptoms: Temperature gauge in the red, overheat warning; Loss of power, limp mode, cylinders possibly shut off; Air conditioning switches off; Steam or coolant smell, coolant loss. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0218 – Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Over Temperature Condition
text: P0218: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Over Temperature Condition. P0218 is a condition code: the transmission or engine module reports that transmission fluid temperature sensor A reads above an overheat limit. Saab's Aisin automatic sets it above 170 °C for more than 10 s, or above 140 °C for two minutes at high speed, shows a 'transmission overheating' warning and shifts less smoothly; afterwards a fluid change is advised because the additives are spent. Ford uses its own code on diesels and lists P0218 without the warning light on other models. Reactions include earlier torque converter lock-up, a modified shift pattern and sometimes reduced power. Causes are real overheating – towing, hills, low or old fluid, a clogged cooler – or a sensor reading wrongly. Common causes: High load (towing, hills, sustained full throttle, stop-and-go in heat) (high likelihood); Transmission fluid low or aged (medium likelihood); Fluid cooler, thermostat or lines clogged, weak cooling system (medium likelihood); Torque converter clutch slipping or internal damage (low likelihood); Temperature sensor or wiring reading wrongly (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission overheating warning; Changed or harsh shifting; Limp mode or reduced power possible; Burnt fluid smell. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0219 – Engine Overspeed Condition
text: P0219: Engine Overspeed Condition. P0219 is a condition code: engine speed has exceeded the overspeed limit even though the rev limiter already cuts fuel – so the engine was driven from outside, usually by downshifting at too high a road speed or descending in too low a gear, or the speed signal was wrong. Limits: Ford 6.7 litre diesel above 4,200 rpm, 3.0 litre above 4,800 rpm, after 0.1 s; GM/Saab 2.8 V6 petrol with manual gearbox above 7,000 rpm for 1 s; Saab 2.2 diesel above 6,200 rpm, although fuel is cut from 5,000 rpm. Many manufacturers store it without the warning light. Saab advises: together with a camshaft sensor code it was real overspeed, alone check the speed signal; after real overspeed inspect the engine for valve train damage. Common causes: Downshift at too high a road speed (manual gearbox) (high likelihood); Descending in too low a gear (medium likelihood); Fault in the speed signal (crankshaft sensor, wiring) (low likelihood); Diesel runaway (oil drawn into the intake) or sticking injection (low likelihood). Symptoms: Usually no lasting symptoms, only a stored code; Briefly very high revs, limiter intervening; Check engine light possible (manufacturer-dependent); After real overspeed: rattling, loss of power. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0220 – Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit
text: P0220: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit. With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. P0220 is the general circuit fault of sensor B without telling low from high. GM uses it in a special sense on 2015–2016 V8 engines: the signal lies outside 0.25–4.59 V only in the monitoring processor while the main processor sees it as valid; this sets immediately with the warning light. Newer GM and Ford engines report sensor B faults as P0222/P0223. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control. Common causes: Throttle body or sensor B faulty (worn track) (high likelihood); Wiring or connector at the throttle body (corrosion, break) (high likelihood); 5 V reference disturbed (short in another sensor on the same reference) (medium likelihood); Engine module input or monitoring processor faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light and throttle warning light; Reduced power, limp mode; Poor throttle response, jerking; Cruise control disabled. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0221 – Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0221: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Range/Performance. With electronic throttle control the throttle body carries two position sensors, A and B, usually with opposite or offset signals, and the engine module compares them (correlation code P2135). GM and Ford give the pedal sensors their own codes (P2120 ff), so B is in practice the second throttle sensor. Bosch ME9 engines (Saab) set it at a deviation of more than 9 %, older Ford systems at more than 7 degrees between the sensors without the warning light; many newer engines report this only as P2135. The module carries on with sensor A, limits throttle opening and power and switches off cruise control. title: P0225 – Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit
text: P0225: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit. Sensor C is a third throttle or pedal position sensor whose role depends on the manufacturer. Ford uses it for the sensor of the second throttle body on engines with two throttles and digital (SENT) sensors; with other makes it can be a further pedal or throttle channel. P0225 is the general circuit fault of sensor C without telling low from high (those are P0227/P0228). Ford sets it when the digital sensor of the second throttle body has been faulty for more than 4 s and switches on the warning light and the powertrain fault lamp; communication faults of the sensor line have their own codes. The result is reduced power. Common causes: Sensor C or second throttle body faulty (high likelihood); Wiring or connector (supply, signal line) (high likelihood); 5 V reference disturbed (medium likelihood); Engine module (low likelihood). title: P0227 – Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit Low

title: P022A – Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Circuit/Open
text: P022A: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Circuit/Open. The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P022A is the general circuit fault of the actuator drive, mainly an open circuit: the driver sees no current or an output voltage outside its window. The module then switches bypass control off and the flap stays in its rest position. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve. Common causes: Wire or connector at the bypass actuator open (high likelihood); Actuator or solenoid of the bypass flap faulty (coil, motor) (medium likelihood); Fuse or relay of the actuator supply (low likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Depending on the rest position: longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature with slight loss of power; Often nothing noticeable while driving. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0230 – Fuel Pump Primary Circuit
text: P0230: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit. The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0230 concerns the primary side. GM's output driver compares the commanded with the actual state of the relay control circuit and sets the code at 8 of 10 mismatches, after two trips; Ford checks for open or short circuits for 2–5 s. With a failed relay control the pump stays off and the engine will not start or dies; a short to voltage keeps the pump running and drains the battery. On Ford systems with a pump control module the code means its power relay circuit; on the Subaru-based Saab 9-2X it is the pump module's collective fault report. Common causes: Fuel pump relay faulty (coil open or shorted) (high likelihood); Control wire from module to relay open or shorted to ground or voltage (medium likelihood); Relay supply, ground or fuse missing (medium likelihood); With a pump control module: its supply, ground or the module itself (medium likelihood); Engine module driver faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start; Engine stalls while driving; Check engine light on; No pump prime noise at ignition on; with a short to voltage the pump runs on and drains the battery. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0231 – Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Low
text: P0231: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Low. The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0231 means the secondary side reads low, and the meaning differs by system. Ford's relay systems read the voltage in the pump power circuit through a monitor wire: if it is missing with the pump commanded on – relay contact not closing, fuse missing, wire open or shorted to ground – the code sets after 2–5 s. GM pumps with their own power module report a short to ground as overcurrent at 18 A or more, setting the warning light in the first trip and switching the output off. The pump gets no voltage, so the engine will not start or stalls. Common causes: Power wire from relay or module to pump shorted to ground (chafing at tank or underbody) (high likelihood); Relay contact not closing, fuse or battery feed to the relay missing (high likelihood); Pump motor jammed or shorted (high current) (medium likelihood); Connector at the tank flange corroded or burnt (medium likelihood); Pump control module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine cranks but does not start; Engine stalls while driving; Check engine light on; Blown fuel pump fuse. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0232 – Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit High
text: P0232: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit High. The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P0232 means there is voltage in the pump power circuit although the pump should be off – a welded relay contact or a power wire shorted to another supply. GM pump modules check this after switch-off or in the off phase of the PWM cycle; above about 4 V the code sets once per trip, with the warning light after two trips. Ford's relay systems see it through the pump monitor wire. Driving is usually unaffected, but the pump may keep running with the ignition off and drain the battery – and an emergency shutdown would not work. Common causes: Relay contact welded or sticking (high likelihood); Pump power wire shorted to another supply (medium likelihood); Pump control module output stage shorted (medium likelihood); Moisture or corrosion in the connector causing leakage current (low likelihood). Symptoms: Fuel pump keeps running after switch-off; Battery drained overnight; Check engine light on (GM after two trips); Often nothing noticeable while driving. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0233 – Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Intermittent
text: P0233: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit Intermittent. title: P0234 – Turbocharger/Supercharger A Overboost Condition
text: P0234: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Overboost Condition. P0234 is a function code, not a sensor fault: the engine module compares target and actual boost, and actual boost stays above target although the control is already lowering it (wastegate opened, variable vanes opened). GM petrol engines set it at 20–35 kPa over target with the warning light in the first trip; GM diesels with variable vanes at 7–10 kPa, after two trips; Ford EcoBoost at about 28 kPa (4 psi) over 5 s while the wastegate is already commanded fully open. Ford diesels instead use P0234 for exhaust back pressure above 4.0–4.5 bar. The engine limits boost or enters limp mode. Typical causes are a wastegate stuck closed, sooted variable vanes or a faulty control valve; Audi traced cases on the Q7 TDI to cracked exhaust parts jamming the turbo vanes. Check the boost sensor against barometric pressure first. Common causes: Wastegate stuck closed, actuator or linkage sticking, control hose off or blocked (high likelihood); Variable turbine vanes sooted or stuck closed (diesel) (high likelihood); Boost control valve or electric actuator faulty (medium likelihood); Boost or manifold sensor reading too high (drift) (medium likelihood); Software or calibration, tuning (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Limp mode with clear loss of power; Boost overshoots on acceleration, then power drops; Knocking under full load (petrol) or smoke (diesel). Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0235 – Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit
text: P0235: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit. Boost sensor A measures the absolute pressure between charge air cooler and throttle – GM calls it TIAP, Ford TIP – usually combined with an intake air temperature sensor; its voltage rises with pressure. With the ignition on and the engine stopped it must read the same as manifold and barometric pressure. P0235 is the general fault of sensor A's circuit or signal, for modules that do not split low, high and range. GM, Ford and Saab do not use it; Audi documents it on the Q7 TDI together with over- and underboost, so there it also marks an implausible boost value, for example from a charge air leak or jammed turbo vanes. No manufacturer threshold for this code was found. With a sensor fault boost control is switched off and only the base boost of the wastegate spring remains, with a clear loss of power. Common causes: Connector at the boost sensor corroded or loose, broken wire (high likelihood); Boost sensor faulty, often oily from crankcase ventilation (medium likelihood); Charge air leak or jammed turbo vanes causing an implausible value (medium likelihood); 5 V reference shorted by another sensor (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Clear loss of power, only base boost; Boost reading implausible in a scan tool. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0236 – Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance

title: P0239 – Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit
text: P0239: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Circuit. title: P023A – Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
text: P023A: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Control Circuit/Open. Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit, driven by an electric pump – GM uses this on supercharged V8s such as the LT4 (Camaro ZL1, Corvette Z06, CTS-V) and LT5 (Corvette ZR1). P023A means GM's driver diagnosis has found an open circuit (more than 200 kΩ between output and ground with the low-side driver off). Bundled conditions: main relay at least 11 V, ignition above 5 V; 50 of 63 samples set the code with the warning light in the first trip on 2018–2019 engines, older modules need two trips. Without the pump the charge air gets hot and boost is limited. Common causes: Wire or connector at the pump open (front area, corrosion) (high likelihood); Pump faulty (motor or electronics) (medium likelihood); Fuse, pump relay or supply missing (medium likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Loss of power under load or in heat (boost limited); Follow-up code P026A possible. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P023D – Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Correlation
text: P023D: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Correlation. P023D compares the manifold pressure sensor (after the throttle) with boost sensor A (before the throttle): with the engine stopped both must read the same ambient pressure. Saab's 2.8 V6 checks this once per trip with the ignition on before starting and sets the code at a difference of more than 12 kPa, with the warning light and limp mode limited to 170 Nm. The code does not say which sensor is wrong – barometric pressure as a third value decides. Electrical faults of either sensor (P0107/P0108, P0237/P0238) block the test and must be fixed first. GM and Ford run the same comparison but report it as P0236, P0106 or P2227. Common causes: Manifold or boost sensor drifting or dirty (high likelihood); Contact resistance at connector or ground of one sensor (medium likelihood); Pressure port or hose of one sensor blocked (oil sludge, ice) (medium likelihood); Engine module or reference voltage (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Limp mode, limited power; Otherwise often unremarkable. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P023E – Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Correlation
text: P023E: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Correlation. Boost sensor B is a second boost pressure sensor, for a second turbo or bank on parallel twin-turbo engines or a second stage on two-stage systems. title: P023F – Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit/Open
text: P023F: Fuel Pump Secondary Circuit/Open. The fuel pump circuit has two sides: the primary circuit is the engine module's output to the fuel pump relay coil (or to a pump control module), the secondary circuit is the power circuit from relay contact or module to the pump itself. P023F means the power circuit to the pump is open. GM pumps with their own power module, whose speed is controlled by rail pressure, measure the pump current: if it stays below 1 A (older modules 0.5 A) although the pump is commanded, the code sets with the warning light in the first trip, and fuel pressure diagnostics are suspended. The cause lies in the wire from module to pump or its return, the pump connector or the pump motor itself. The pump stops, so the engine will not start or dies – there is no limp mode. Common causes: Pump connector at tank flange or pump module open or corroded (high likelihood); Fuel pump open internally (brushes, winding) (high likelihood); Wire from module to pump or return wire open (medium likelihood); Pump control module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine does not start, no pump noise; Engine stalls while driving; Check engine light on. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0243 – Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A
text: P0243: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A. The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0243 is the general circuit fault of actuator A. GM uses it for an open circuit: with the driver off, more than 200 kΩ between output and ground in 10 of 20 samples sets it with the warning light in the first trip (older modules: two trips). Ford uses P0243 on its electric wastegates as the collective code for open and short circuits (0.4 s), together with P2ABD for driver overcurrent or overheating. Boost control is then switched off and only the spring-set base boost remains – less power, but no risk of overboost. Common causes: Connector at the wastegate valve or actuator loose, corroded or with spread contacts (high likelihood); Valve coil or electric actuator winding open (medium likelihood); Supply voltage to the valve missing (ignition, relay, fuse) (medium likelihood); Broken control wire between module and valve (medium likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Clearly less power, boost only at base level; Sluggish acceleration, turbo lag; Reduced engine power message possible. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0244 – Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A Range/Performance
text: P0244: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A Range/Performance. The wastegate lets exhaust bypass the turbine to limit boost; actuator A is either a pulse-width-modulated solenoid on a pneumatic wastegate can or an electric actuator with a position sensor. P0244 means the actuator does not respond as commanded although its circuit is electrically sound, and manufacturers implement it differently. Subaru engines (Saab 9-2X) set it when manifold pressure exceeds an altitude-dependent limit – about 220 kPa absolute at sea level – for over 2 s, with the warning light at once. Older GM modules (Saab LDK, LLU) however use P0244 for an open solenoid circuit; newer GM and Ford systems do not use it and monitor function under P0234/P0299 or P25B3/P25B4. Symptoms: Check engine light on; Lack of power or surging, too high boost; Limp mode with reduced power; Rattle or whistle at the turbo possible. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0245 – Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A Low
text: P0245: Turbocharger/Supercharger Wastegate Actuator A Low. title: P024A – Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Range/Performance
text: P024A: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Range/Performance. The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P024A is the functional fault: the bypass does not follow its command, judged from the position sensor or from the expected temperature effect – Bosch describes comparing the cooler's efficiency with the valve closed and open, using modelled air temperature before and measured temperature after the cooler. FCA documents P024A, together with P026E, on the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia and 2018 Stelvio with the 2.0 turbo and fixed it with an engine software update, so check the software level first. Common causes: Bypass flap sticking, coked or oily (oil from crankcase ventilation or turbo) (high likelihood); Actuator weak or vacuum line leaking (medium likelihood); Engine software (FCA 2.0 turbo) (medium likelihood); Position sensor inaccurate or connector corroded (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Longer warm-up or higher charge air temperature; Possibly less power from boost limitation. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P024B – Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Stuck
text: P024B: Charge Air Cooler Bypass Control A Stuck. The charge air cooler bypass is a flap or valve that routes compressed air around the charge air cooler, so the engine and exhaust warm up faster after a cold start; when warm it closes or opens partly to control intake air temperature. It is driven by an electric motor with a built-in position sensor or by a solenoid and vacuum can. P024B means the bypass flap does not move at all despite being commanded – the position signal stands still or the air temperature shows no reaction. Bosch's patent describes exactly the case of a valve stuck closed or a blocked bypass, which raises emissions during warm-up. Stuck open, the charge air gets hotter and power drops; stuck closed, warm-up takes longer. No manufacturer document using this code was found – GM and Ford do not use the bypass codes; the description rests on CARB's component monitoring requirement and a Bosch patent on the bypass valve. Common causes: Flap seized or coked (high likelihood); Actuator faulty (gear, motor) (medium likelihood); Vacuum supply missing (pneumatic type) (low likelihood); Position sensor reading constant (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Stuck open: higher charge air temperature, loss of power; Stuck closed: longer warm-up. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0251 – Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
text: P0251: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A (Cam/Rotor/Injector). These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump. On older distributor pumps it was a solenoid that set the injected quantity; on common rail it is usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that lets only as much fuel into the pumping elements as the rail needs, instead of spilling the excess through a pressure valve. Manufacturers use different codes for this part: Ford P0001–P0004, GM Duramax P0090–P0092. P0251 is the general circuit fault of actuator A. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel uses it for an open circuit of the pressure regulator on the high-pressure pump: if the control wire does not show the expected voltage with the driver off for more than 1 s, the code sets with the warning light at once. Depending on the system, rail pressure and power are then limited. Common causes: Metering actuator coil open (high likelihood); Connector at the actuator corroded or loose, broken wire (high likelihood); Supply voltage to the actuator missing (medium likelihood); Distributor pump: internal electronics or quantity valve faulty (medium likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Loss of power, limp mode; Rough idle or hunting; Hard starting or stalling. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0253 – Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
text: P0253: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector). title: P0254 – Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
text: P0254: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A High (Cam/Rotor/Injector). These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0254 means the actuator A circuit reads high or draws too much current – typically the control wire shorted to voltage. Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel sets it after 1 s with the warning light at once. On Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel a short to voltage of more than 0.31 s stops the engine, because a permanently energised valve can no longer control quantity and pressure. Ford's equivalent P0004 sets above 3.7 A; GM uses P0092. Common causes: Control wire shorted to voltage (high likelihood); Metering valve with shorted turns (overcurrent) (medium likelihood); Connector corrosion with leakage current (low likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Engine stalls or will not start (Saab 3.0 diesel); Limp mode, loss of power. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0255 – Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
text: P0255: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control A Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector). These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0255 reports brief open or short circuits in the actuator A circuit that come and go – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration. No manufacturer using it with exactly this meaning was found; a Ram 6.7 Cummins code list names it as a circuit performance fault instead. The description follows CARB's continuous circuit monitoring requirement and the documented A siblings. Common causes: Loose contact or corrosion at the metering actuator connector (high likelihood); Harness chafing intermittently (vibration) (medium likelihood); Actuator coil with a temperature-dependent fault (low likelihood); Engine module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light (often goes out again); Brief jerking or power dips; Occasional limp mode. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0256 – Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
text: P0256: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B (Cam/Rotor/Injector). These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. Actuator B is a second metering actuator, for example on pumps with two metering valves such as on Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel. P0256 is its general circuit fault, the counterpart of P0251. No manufacturer using P0256 was found – Saab reports its two valves under other codes; the description follows CARB's circuit monitoring requirement and the A siblings. Common causes: Metering valve B open (high likelihood); Connector or wire to valve B open (high likelihood); Engine module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Loss of power, limp mode. title: P0257 – Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
text: P0257: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Range/Performance (Cam/Rotor/Injector). These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0257 is the functional fault of actuator B: the metering does not achieve its target. It is documented on Mack and Volvo heavy-duty common-rail diesels of 2018–2020 together with rail pressure codes (P0087, P016F, P228F) and P2A17/P2A1F; the cause can lie outside the actuator, for example an electronic pressure relief valve stuck open, a leak or poor low-pressure supply, so those faults are fixed first. Engine power may be derated. Common causes: Rail pressure or metering target not reached (leak, relief valve open) (high likelihood); Poor low-pressure supply (filter, lift pump, air) (medium likelihood); Metering actuator or pumping element worn (medium likelihood); Software or diagnostic level (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Power derate; Hard starting, low rail pressure when cranking; Jerking under load. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0258 – Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
text: P0258: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Low (Cam/Rotor/Injector). These codes cover the electrically controlled fuel metering actuator on a diesel injection pump – on common rail usually an inlet metering valve on the high-pressure pump that sets how much fuel is compressed. P0258 means the actuator B circuit reads low. The only manufacturer found, Saab with its 3.0 V6 diesel of the early 2000s, uses it not for a second valve but for the shared supply of both metering valves: a short to ground or open for more than about 1 s triggers limp mode with limited pedal response and injection quantity, rail pressure capped at 60 MPa and idle raised to 1,000 rpm; the warning light comes on if it recurs on the next trip. Symptoms: Check engine light on (after the second trip); Loss of power, limp mode; Raised idle speed in limp mode. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0259 – Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B High (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
text: P0259: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B High (Cam/Rotor/Injector). Fuel metering actuator B is a second electrically controlled metering valve on a diesel injection pump; A has the codes P0251–P0255. P0259 means its circuit reads high or draws too much current – a short to voltage or a shorted turn. Saab's 3.0 V6 diesel, whose pump has two metering valves, uses it for an internal short in one of the valves lasting over 2.1 s: limp mode with limited pedal response, injection quantity and rail pressure (60 MPa), and the warning light if it recurs on the next trip. GM and Ford use other codes for this part (P0090–P0092, P0001–P0004). Common causes: Metering valve B shorted internally (high likelihood); Control wire to the valve shorted to voltage, chafing (medium likelihood); Connector at the valve corroded or wet (medium likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Limp mode with limited power and speed; Hard starting, engine may stall. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P025A – Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit/Open
text: P025A: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit/Open. On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025A means the control line from the engine module to pump module A is open or faulty. On Ford systems the pump module itself detects the bad command signal and reports it on the monitor line (11–16 V, 2–5 s); Ford uses P025A for the shared line to modules A and B. GM's pump module compares the enable line with the request on the data bus and sets P025A after about 1 s, with the warning light in the first trip; on some Ford vehicles the code does not light it. Common causes: Control line to the pump module open or shorted, often along the frame (high likelihood); Connector at the pump module corroded or wet (module often mounted on the frame) (high likelihood); Pump control module faulty (input) (medium likelihood); Module ground or supply poor (medium likelihood); Engine module output faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent); Hard or no start; Rough idle, surging; Lack of power from wrong fuel pressure. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P025B – Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P025B: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Range/Performance. On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. P025B means pump module A receives a signal, but an invalid command – the duty cycle is outside the valid window or implausible. Ford's module signals this with a 20 % (±4 %) duty cycle on its monitor line; the check runs continuously at 11–16 V over 2–5 s. Whether the warning light comes on depends on the vehicle. Typical causes are contact resistance in the control line or connector that distorts the duty cycle, a poor ground or a faulty module. Common causes: Contact resistance or corrosion in the control line or connector distorting the duty cycle (high likelihood); Pump control module faulty (medium likelihood); Interference or poor ground between engine module and pump module (medium likelihood); Engine module software or output (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent); Hard or no start; Rough idle, surging; Lack of power from wrong fuel pressure. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P025C – Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Low
text: P025C: Fuel Pump Module A Control Circuit Low. title: P025E – Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic
text: P025E: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic. Boost sensor A measures the pressure between charge air cooler and throttle (Ford TIP, GM TIAP). P025E counts brief excursions outside its valid voltage range that are each too short for the low or high code P0237/P0238 – Ford's limits are below 0.19 V and above 4.88 V. Ford counts these events continuously and sets P025E after 10 in one drive cycle. Boost control then runs on a substitute value or is switched off, leaving only base boost. Typical causes are a loose or corroded connector or a wire breaking under vibration and heat. Common causes: Loose contact or corrosion at the sensor connector (high likelihood); Wire or 5 V reference breaking from vibration or heat (medium likelihood); Sensor faulty internally (erratic signal) (medium likelihood); Shared 5 V reference disturbed by another sensor (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Occasional loss of power, boost limited; Jerking on acceleration. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P025F – Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Intermittent/Erratic

title: P0260 – Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector)
text: P0260: Injection Pump Fuel Metering Control B Intermittent (Cam/Rotor/Injector). P0260 reports brief dropouts or jumps in the circuit of fuel metering actuator B on a diesel injection pump that do not last long enough for the low or high code (P0258/P0259) – typically a loose contact or a wire breaking under vibration. title: P0261 – Cylinder 1 Injector A Circuit Low
text: P0261: Cylinder 1 Injector A Circuit Low. P0261 means the control wire of the cylinder 1 injector – the side the engine module switches to ground – is shorted to ground. GM detects this with the driver off: on direct injection at 1 V or less, on port injection and Duramax diesels at 0.5 Ω or less to ground. Ford's 6.7 diesel has its driver chip report the short within 0.3 s. Most systems switch the warning light on in the first trip (some GM port-injection engines and Saab's 2.0 turbo after two) and shut the affected injector off, so the cylinder misfires. Ford petrol engines report all injector circuit faults as P0201 ff instead. Common causes: Control wire of the cylinder 1 injector chafed to ground in the harness (high likelihood); Injector connector damp or corroded, leakage to ground (medium likelihood); Injector shorted to its housing internally (medium likelihood); Open control wire (on some GM port-injection drivers this also reads low; P020x sets too) (low likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0301; Loss of power, rough idle; Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0263 – Cylinder 1 Contribution/Balance
text: P0263: Cylinder 1 Contribution/Balance. P0263 comes from the cylinder balance control of common-rail diesels: the engine module measures the crankshaft acceleration of each cylinder's power stroke, compares it with the average and gives a deviating cylinder more or less fuel. The code sets when the correction for cylinder 1 reaches its limit and the cylinder still does not keep up – GM at 95 % of a limit of about ±12–17 mm³ for 30 s, Ford above 90 % of the allowed 3.5–15 mg per stroke for 7.5 s; GM needs two trips. The code does not say whether there is too much or too little fuel – the correction value for cylinder 1 shows the direction: strongly negative means a leaking injector, strongly positive a weak injector or low compression. VW and Ram traced some cases to over-sensitive software, so check for updates before replacing injectors. Common causes: Injector of cylinder 1 worn, coked or leaking (high likelihood); Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive (medium likelihood); Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement (medium likelihood); Low compression on cylinder 1 (valve, rings, injector seal) (medium likelihood); Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Rough idle, shaking or knocking; Loss of power or smoke; Higher consumption, poor cold start. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P026A – Charge Air Cooler Efficiency Below Threshold
text: P026A: Charge Air Cooler Efficiency Below Threshold. P026A means the charge air cooler is not cooling enough. The module compares the temperature drop across the cooler with the maximum possible (inlet minus ambient) or with a model: GM's 6.6 litre LML diesel sets it below 25 % efficiency, later GM diesels below 50 %, both after two trips; Ford's 6.7 and 3.0 diesels when the measured temperature is 18–35 °C (3.0: 35–65 °C) off the model over about 10 s. GM's 3.0 twin-turbo petrol with a coolant-cooled charge air cooler sets it in the first trip when manifold air exceeds 110 °C or boost has been limited for a long time. Hot intake air costs power and raises NOx and soot. Common causes: Charge air cooler clogged on the outside (insects, leaves, dirt) or fins damaged (high likelihood); Coolant-cooled cooler: pump faulty, air in the low-temperature circuit, low coolant (high likelihood); Charge air or ambient temperature sensor inaccurate (medium likelihood); Charge air cooler bypass stuck open (low likelihood); Software or calibration (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Loss of power under load or in heat; High intake air temperature in live data. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P026B – Injection Timing Performance
text: P026B: Injection Timing Performance. P026B is the engine-wide injection timing monitor: CARB requires diesels from 2010 to detect injection that is too early or too late overall, or a timing control at its limit. Unlike P020A ff (per cylinder) it concerns the engine as a whole. It is documented on the Ram 6.7 Cummins, together with the per-cylinder timing and balance codes; FCA describes it as set falsely by software and fixes it with an engine module update, without publishing thresholds. GM and Ford handle timing with per-cylinder codes instead (P01CB ff, P2B11 ff). Common causes: Engine module software (false setting) (high likelihood); Injectors coked or worn (changed start of injection) (medium likelihood); Rail pressure or fuel supply problems (pump, filter, fuel quality) (medium likelihood); Crankshaft or camshaft signal inaccurate (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Often nothing noticeable (false setting); Possibly knocking, rough running or more smoke. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P026C – Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected
text: P026C: Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected. From 2010, CARB requires diesel engines to detect when the commanded injection quantity is not delivered. The module estimates the fuel actually burned from airflow and the measured lambda (from the NOx or oxygen sensor) and corrects the quantity; if that correction passes a limit, the code sets. P026C means the engine gets less fuel than commanded. GM's 6.6 litre LML diesel checks it at idle with the vehicle stationary and the engine warm, setting it at a correction of −20 to −35 mm³ per stroke for 12 s; later GM diesels use the learned correction value (10 of 20 samples); both need two trips. FCA lists it with an injector cleaning procedure for deposits. Ford diesels do not use it. Typical causes are coked injectors, wrong airflow or lambda measurement and weak fuel supply. Common causes: Injectors coked or clogged (too little flow) (high likelihood); Airflow or boost measurement wrong, NOx sensor lambda inaccurate (medium likelihood); Weak low- or high-pressure supply (filter, pump, rail pressure) (medium likelihood); Fuel quality or contamination (low likelihood); Software (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Lack of power; Rough running or idle. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P026D – Fuel Injection Quantity A Higher Than Expected
text: P026D: Fuel Injection Quantity A Higher Than Expected. From 2010, CARB requires diesel engines to detect when the commanded injection quantity is not delivered. The module estimates the fuel actually burned from airflow and the measured lambda (from the NOx or oxygen sensor) and corrects the quantity; if that correction passes a limit, the code sets. P026D means the engine gets more fuel than commanded. GM's LML diesel sets it at idle at a correction of +16 to +35 mm³ per stroke for 12 s, two trips. Volvo trucks detect it as too little oxygen at the NOx sensors for the fuel flow and point to boost sensor, EGR valve and sensor, wrong injectors, turbo vanes and intake leaks. On GM's 2.8 litre diesel vans of 2020–2022 it could also be a software anomaly without driving problems. Symptoms are black smoke and more frequent filter regeneration. Common causes: Injector dripping or worn, or wrong injector type fitted (high likelihood); EGR valve not closing or EGR differential pressure sensor wrong (medium likelihood); Boost sensor or turbo vanes faulty, intake leak (medium likelihood); NOx or oxygen sensor reading wrong (medium likelihood); Software (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Black smoke, higher soot load, more frequent filter regeneration; Rough running or idle; Often nothing noticeable while driving. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P026E – Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Performance
text: P026E: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Pump A Performance. Some engines cool the charge air with a coolant-to-air cooler in its own low-temperature circuit with an electric pump. P026E means that pump is electrically sound but does not deliver as commanded – judged from feedback by the pump electronics or from the missing temperature drop. FCA documents it on the 2017 Alfa Romeo Giulia and 2018 Stelvio with the 2.0 turbo, together with P024A, and fixed it with a software update; thresholds are not published. Air in the circuit or low coolant lets the pump run dry; hot charge air then costs power. Common causes: Air in the low-temperature circuit or low coolant (pump runs dry) (high likelihood); Pump faulty internally (bearing, impeller, electronics) (high likelihood); Software or calibration (medium likelihood); Weak supply or ground, corroded connector (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Loss of power in heat or under load; Follow-up code P026A possible; Level in the auxiliary coolant tank drops. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P026F – Coolant Thermostat Performance
text: P026F: Coolant Thermostat Performance. P026F is a general functional code for the coolant thermostat. CARB requires that the coolant reaches the temperature needed for other diagnostics in the approved time and comes within 11 °C of the thermostat's regulating temperature; from model years 2019–2021 petrol engines must also detect it dropping back below that temperature, and electric pumps or valves controlling coolant flow are monitored like a thermostat. The module follows coolant temperature against a heat model. No manufacturer using P026F was found – GM and Ford report thermostat faults as P0128, P01F0 or P2181 – so the description rests on CARB and the thermostat's function. Common causes: Thermostat stuck open or opening too early (high likelihood); Thermostat stuck closed or opening too late (medium likelihood); Map-controlled thermostat: heating element or control faulty (medium likelihood); Coolant temperature sensor inaccurate (low likelihood); Low coolant or air in the system (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Slow warm-up, weak heating (stuck open); Low or fluctuating temperature gauge; Overheating (stuck closed). Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0270 – Cylinder 4 Injector A Circuit Low
text: P0270: Cylinder 4 Injector A Circuit Low. P0270 means the control wire of the cylinder 4 injector – the side the engine module switches to ground – is shorted to ground. GM detects this with the driver off: on direct injection at 1 V or less, on port injection and Duramax diesels at 0.5 Ω or less to ground. Ford's 6.7 diesel has its driver chip report the short within 0.3 s. Most systems switch the warning light on in the first trip (some GM port-injection engines and Saab's 2.0 turbo after two) and shut the affected injector off, so the cylinder misfires. Ford petrol engines report all injector circuit faults as P0201 ff instead. Common causes: Control wire of the cylinder 4 injector chafed to ground in the harness (high likelihood); Injector connector damp or corroded, leakage to ground (medium likelihood); Injector shorted to its housing internally (medium likelihood); Open control wire (on some GM port-injection drivers this also reads low; P020x sets too) (low likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Misfire and rough running, misfire code P0304; Loss of power, rough idle; Injector shut off, limp mode possible on diesels. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0272 – Cylinder 4 Contribution/Balance
text: P0272: Cylinder 4 Contribution/Balance. P0272 comes from the cylinder balance control of common-rail diesels: the engine module measures the crankshaft acceleration of each cylinder's power stroke, compares it with the average and gives a deviating cylinder more or less fuel. The code sets when the correction for cylinder 4 reaches its limit and the cylinder still does not keep up – GM at 95 % of a limit of about ±12–17 mm³ for 30 s, Ford above 90 % of the allowed 3.5–15 mg per stroke for 7.5 s; GM needs two trips. The code does not say whether there is too much or too little fuel – the correction value for cylinder 4 shows the direction: strongly negative means a leaking injector, strongly positive a weak injector or low compression. VW and Ram traced some cases to over-sensitive software, so check for updates before replacing injectors. Common causes: Injector of cylinder 4 worn, coked or leaking (high likelihood); Engine software outdated or diagnosis too sensitive (medium likelihood); Injector correction codes not or wrongly programmed after replacement (medium likelihood); Low compression on cylinder 4 (valve, rings, injector seal) (medium likelihood); Crankshaft sensor or tone wheel learning faulty, dual-mass flywheel (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Rough idle, shaking or knocking; Loss of power or smoke; Higher consumption, poor cold start. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P027A – Fuel Pump Module B Control Circuit/Open
text: P027A: Fuel Pump Module B Control Circuit/Open. On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. Module B is a second pump module, for example on dual-tank commercial vehicles. P027A is the counterpart of P025A: the control line from the engine module to pump module B is open or faulty. No manufacturer using P027A was found – Ford reports line faults of both modules together under P025A, GM only uses P025A; the description follows CARB's circuit monitoring requirement and Ford's module B check. If the second tank's pump gets no valid command, fuel may run short when running from that tank. Common causes: Control line to the pump module open or shorted, often along the frame (high likelihood); Connector at the pump module corroded or wet (module often mounted on the frame) (high likelihood); Pump control module faulty (input) (medium likelihood); Module ground or supply poor (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent); Fuel shortage when running from the second tank; Starting problems, surging. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P027B – Fuel Pump Module B Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P027B: Fuel Pump Module B Control Circuit Range/Performance. On demand-controlled fuel systems the engine module does not drive the pump itself but sends a pump control module the desired pump output on a separate control line, usually as a duty cycle; the module reports back on a monitor line or via CAN. Module B is a second pump module, for example on dual-tank commercial vehicles. P027B means pump module B receives an invalid command or its feedback does not match. Ford's module signals this with a 20 % (±4 %) duty cycle on its monitor line, checked continuously at 11–16 V over 2–5 s; on Ford commercial vehicles the module B monitor line runs via the smart relay module and CAN to the engine module. Whether the warning light comes on depends on the vehicle. Common causes: Contact resistance or corrosion in the control or monitor line to module B (high likelihood); Pump control module B faulty (medium likelihood); Ground problems (medium likelihood); Relay module or CAN forwarding disturbed (Ford commercial vehicles) (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light (vehicle-dependent); Fuel shortage when running from the second tank; Surging, lack of power. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P027E – Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected
text: P027E: Cold Start Fuel Injection Quantity A Lower Than Expected. P027E is the cold-start counterpart of P026C: during cold start the engine gets less fuel than commanded, for example because a catalyst-heating injection does not arrive. The check probably works as in warm running, from airflow and lambda against the commanded quantity. The code covers only phases with the cold-start emission strategy active (extra injections to heat the catalyst, raised idle): CARB requires faults of elements also monitored elsewhere to be reported separately during the cold-start strategy. No manufacturer using this code was found; the description follows CARB and the warm-running counterpart. Common causes: Injectors coked or clogged (medium likelihood); Rail pressure builds too slowly at cold start (filter, wax, pump) (medium likelihood); Airflow or lambda measurement inaccurate (medium likelihood); Software (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Poor cold start, rough running when cold; Longer warm-up. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P028A – Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Control Circuit/Open
text: P028A: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Control Circuit/Open. Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler; a Deere patent describes such a fan that the module switches and reverses to blow out dirt. P028A means the fan's control circuit is open or has a general fault, detected by the driver stage. Without the fan the charge air is cooled less at low speed or in heat, which can lead to P026A and boost limitation. No manufacturer document using P028A was found; the description rests on CARB's output component requirement. Common causes: Wire or connector to the fan open or corroded (high likelihood); Fan relay or fan control module faulty (medium likelihood); Fan motor open internally (medium likelihood); Fuse blown (low likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Fan does not run; Loss of power in heat or traffic; Follow-up code P026A possible. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P028B – Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Performance/Stuck Off
text: P028B: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Performance/Stuck Off. Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler, switched by the engine module; a Deere patent describes such a fan that is also reversed to blow out dirt. P028B means the module commands the fan on but sees no effect – no speed or current feedback from a fan control module, or the charge air does not cool – although the circuit is electrically sound (circuit faults are P028A, P028D and P028E). The charge air then gets hotter, which can limit boost and power. No manufacturer document using this code was found; the description rests on CARB's output component requirement. Common causes: Fan motor seized or worn (high likelihood); Fan blocked (debris, dirt, ice) (medium likelihood); Fan relay or fan control module without output (medium likelihood); Fan fuse or supply (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light (manufacturer-dependent); Loss of power in heat or at low speed; High charge air temperature, possibly P026A. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P028C – Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Stuck On
text: P028C: Charge Air Cooler Cooling Fan Stuck On. Some vehicles – mainly commercial and off-road machines, or cars with a separate cooler for a coolant-cooled charge air cooler – have their own fan for the charge air cooler, switched by the engine module; a Deere patent describes such a fan that is also reversed to blow out dirt. P028C means the fan runs although the module has switched it off – speed or current feedback, or the voltage at the output, does not match the off command. Typical causes are a welded relay contact or a shorted driver stage. The fan runs continuously and can drain the battery; the charge air tends to be too cold, which favours condensate. Symptoms: Fan runs all the time, even after switch-off; Battery drains; Warning light (manufacturer-dependent). Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0297 – Vehicle Overspeed Condition
text: P0297: Vehicle Overspeed Condition. P0297 is a condition code: the engine module detects that road speed – from the vehicle speed sensor or wheel and output shaft speed – exceeded the calibrated maximum. Electronic speed limiters cut fuel or throttle at that limit, and the event is stored. Ford uses the code on its petrol trucks and stores it without the warning light; no manufacturer publishes a threshold. Common triggers are descending with a trailer beyond the limiter speed, wheelspin on the driven axle, a wrongly programmed tyre size or axle ratio, or spikes in the speed signal. Unlike P0219 it concerns road speed, not engine speed. Common causes: Limiter speed genuinely exceeded (downhill, trailer) (high likelihood); Wrong tyre size or axle ratio programmed, larger wheels fitted (medium likelihood); Wheelspin on the driven axle (medium likelihood); Speed signal disturbed (loose contact, interference, tone wheel) (low likelihood). Symptoms: Usually no warning light, code only stored; Vehicle limits speed at its maximum; With a disturbed signal: jumping speedometer, odd shifting. Repair difficulty: easy.

citation.name: OBDex generic OBD-II code reference
citation.note: Generic SAE J2012 meaning; manufacturer-specific definitions can differ.

title: P0298 – Engine Oil Over Temperature
text: P0298: Engine Oil Over Temperature. P0298 is a protection code: engine oil temperature – from its own sensor, often combined with the oil level sensor, or modelled – has exceeded the protection limit. Saab's 3.0 diesel limits injection quantity when the oil stays at 135 °C or more for over 10 s, until it cools down; a heavy-duty bus engine warns in two stages and then derates. Ford stores the code without the warning light, in line with CARB's exemption for overheat protection. Usual causes are high load in heat, cooling problems, a clogged oil cooler or stuck oil thermostat, and occasionally a sensor reading too high. Common causes: High load in heat (trailer, mountain pass, stop-and-go) (high likelihood); Cooling or fan problem (clogged radiator, fan, thermostat, low coolant) (medium likelihood); Oil cooler clogged or oil thermostat stuck (medium likelihood); Oil temperature or level sensor reading too high (medium likelihood); Low oil level or wrong oil (low likelihood). Symptoms: Reduced power, quantity limited; Oil temperature warning; Usually no check engine light. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0299 – Turbocharger/Supercharger A Underboost Condition
text: P0299: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Underboost Condition. P0299 means actual boost stays below target for a period although the control already demands more. Thresholds: GM petrol 30–55 kPa below target with the warning light in the first trip; GM diesels 10–50 kPa, two trips; Ford EcoBoost more than 4 psi (about 28 kPa) for 5 s with the wastegate already commanded fully closed; Ford diesels 30–40 kPa for 10–15 s, with a further underboost code P2263. Typical causes from manufacturer bulletins: a charge air leak, a wastegate that lost its preload or whose rod came off, a leaking bypass valve, sticking turbo vanes on diesels, and ice in the charge air cooler in winter. A faulty boost sensor can also fake underboost. Many engines then limit power. title: P029A – Cylinder 1 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit
text: P029A: Cylinder 1 - Fuel Trim at Max Limit. These codes belong to an individual-cylinder fuel correction: a diesel's cylinder balance control measures each cylinder's crankshaft acceleration and adjusts its injection quantity; on petrol engines a cylinder-selective mixture control does the same. CARB requires the system to report when such a correction has used up its range or one cylinder causes an imbalance. P029A means the correction for cylinder 1 is at its upper limit: the module keeps giving this cylinder more fuel and still cannot even it out – a sign that the cylinder receives too little fuel or builds too little pressure. GM and Ford use other codes for this (P0263 ff, P219A ff); no manufacturer document describing this code with thresholds was found, so the description follows CARB and published patents. Common causes: Injector of cylinder 1 coked or partly clogged (high likelihood); Compression loss in this cylinder (valve, rings, leak at injector or glow plug) (medium likelihood); Injector circuit high-resistance or connector (medium likelihood); Petrol: false air at this cylinder's intake (manifold gasket) (medium likelihood); Injector correction code missing or wrong after replacement (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Rough idle, vibration; Lack of power, possibly misfire. Repair difficulty: medium.

These codes belong to an individual-cylinder fuel correction: a diesel's cylinder balance control measures each cylinder's crankshaft acceleration and adjusts its injection quantity; on petrol engines a cylinder-selective mixture control does the same. CARB requires the system to report when such a correction has used up its range or one cylinder causes an imbalance. P02B1 means the module detects fuel entering cylinder 6 outside the injection pulse – the injector is leaking or dripping. A BMW patent identifies such a leak by the fact that it persists with the injector switched off. A leaking diesel injector can dilute the oil or damage the piston, so act promptly. GM and Ford use other codes for this (P0263 ff, P219A ff); no manufacturer document describing this code with thresholds was found, so the description follows CARB and published patents. Common causes: Nozzle seat or needle of the cylinder 6 injector leaking (high likelihood); Deposits keeping the needle from closing fully (medium likelihood); Rail pressure too high (low likelihood); Wrong or wrongly coded injector (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Rough idle, vibration; Smoke, fuel smell, knocking. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P02C9 – Cylinder 12 - Injector Leaking
text: P02C9: Cylinder 12 - Injector Leaking. These codes belong to an individual-cylinder fuel correction: a diesel's cylinder balance control measures each cylinder's crankshaft acceleration and adjusts its injection quantity; on petrol engines a cylinder-selective mixture control does the same. CARB requires the system to report when such a correction has used up its range or one cylinder causes an imbalance. P02C9 means the module detects fuel entering cylinder 12 outside the injection pulse – the injector is leaking or dripping. A BMW patent identifies such a leak by the fact that it persists with the injector switched off. A leaking diesel injector can dilute the oil or damage the piston, so act promptly. Cylinder 12 only exists on engines with twelve or more cylinders. GM and Ford use other codes for this (P0263 ff, P219A ff); no manufacturer document describing this code with thresholds was found, so the description follows CARB and published patents. Common causes: Nozzle seat or needle of the cylinder 12 injector leaking (high likelihood); Deposits keeping the needle from closing fully (medium likelihood); Rail pressure too high (low likelihood); Wrong or wrongly coded injector (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Rough idle, vibration; Smoke, fuel smell, knocking. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P02CA – Turbocharger/Supercharger B Overboost Condition
text: P02CA: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Overboost Condition. Turbocharger B is a second, separately controlled turbo – on twin-turbo or two-stage systems, or one per bank. No manufacturer using the turbo B codes was found; twin-turbo engines such as GM's 3.0 V6 and Ford's 3.5 EcoBoost report boost faults under P0234/P0299 with a shared boost sensor, so the description follows CARB and the turbo A codes. P02CA means actual boost of turbo B stays above target although the control is already lowering it; for turbo A, GM petrol engines use 20–35 kPa, Ford EcoBoost more than 4 psi over 5 s. Boost is then limited. Common causes: Wastegate B stuck closed, linkage seized (high likelihood); Boost control valve or actuator B faulty, vacuum line swapped or leaking (medium likelihood); Boost sensor reading wrong (medium likelihood); Turbo B vanes sooted (diesel) (medium likelihood); Software or calibration, tuning (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light, reduced power, limp mode; Power cut under load; Possibly knocking (petrol). Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P02CC – Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit
text: P02CC: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit. The engine module learns a small-quantity correction for each injector: on overrun it gives one injector a tiny test injection (GM about 1.5 mm³), measures the resulting crankshaft acceleration and corrects the injector's activation time per rail pressure step. P02CC means the learned correction for cylinder 1 has reached its lower limit at at least one pressure step: the injector needs much less activation time than nominal – it delivers too much at small quantities or opens early. GM diesels set it at limits of roughly ±66–182 µs after two trips. It is documented on GM's 6.6 litre L5P and 2.8 litre diesels – on the 2.8 a worn drive belt caused it to return after injector replacement – and on Land Rover's 5.0 V8 petrol, where a software update is the first step. It differs from P01CC (over advanced), which some systems derive from the same learning. Common causes: Injector of cylinder 1 leaking or over-delivering at small quantities (high likelihood); Engine software (update available for some models) (medium likelihood); Injector correction code not or wrongly programmed after replacement (medium likelihood); Disturbed crankshaft signal (worn drive belt, tone wheel, dual-mass flywheel) (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Often nothing noticeable; possibly rough idle or knocking; Possibly smoke or higher consumption. Repair difficulty: hard.

text: P02DD: Cylinder 9 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Max Limit. The engine module learns a small-quantity correction for each injector: on overrun it gives one injector a tiny test injection (GM about 1.5 mm³), measures the resulting crankshaft acceleration and corrects the injector's activation time per rail pressure step. P02DD means the learned correction for cylinder 9 has reached its upper limit at at least one pressure step: the injector needs much more activation time than nominal – it delivers too little or opens late, for example from coking. Cylinder 9 exists only on ten-cylinder engines; no manufacturer using this code was found, so the description follows CARB and the documented codes for cylinders 1–8. It differs from P01DB (over retarded), which some systems derive from the same learning. Common causes: Injector of cylinder 9 coked or worn (delivers too little) (high likelihood); Engine software (update available for some models) (medium likelihood); Injector correction code not or wrongly programmed after replacement (medium likelihood); Disturbed crankshaft signal (worn drive belt, tone wheel, dual-mass flywheel) (low likelihood); Low compression on this cylinder (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Often nothing noticeable; possibly rough idle or knocking; Possibly smoke or loss of power. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P02E0 – Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit/Open
text: P02E0: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit/Open. The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back. P02E0 means the motor circuit is open – cable, connector or motor winding. GM diesels detect more than 200 kΩ with the driver off, after about 1.5 s (6.6 litre LML: 7 s), two trips. On a fault the valve is switched off and the spring opens it: driving is usually little affected, but EGR control is restricted and filter regeneration may be blocked. Common causes: Connector at the throttle corroded or loose (high likelihood); Broken motor wire (medium likelihood); Motor winding of the valve open (medium likelihood); Driver stage in the engine module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine light on; Often no noticeable change; Filter regeneration does not run, soot load rises; Shaking at switch-off. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P02E1 – Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Performance

title: P02E4 – Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Open
text: P02E4: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Open. The diesel intake air flow valve A is the throttle flap ahead of the intake manifold of a diesel engine: it creates the vacuum needed for high EGR rates, lowers airflow to heat the particulate filter and catalyst during regeneration and closes at switch-off against run-on shaking. A spring holds it open when unpowered; an electric motor positions it, with a position sensor reporting back. title: P02E5 – Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Closed
text: P02E5: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Closed.
