title: P07FE – Stuck in Gear Not Specified
text: P07FE: Stuck in Gear Not Specified. P07FE is the catch-all of the 'Stuck in Gear' family: the transmission stays in a gear it was commanded to leave, but the module cannot or does not name the gear. The gear-specific codes are P072B–P073C for reverse and gears 1–7, P07D7 for 8th, P07F8 for 9th and P07FB for 10th. No manufacturer document available to us uses P07FE; the gear-specific codes are documented on dual-clutch gearboxes such as Ford's DPS6 and Maserati's MC20, whose actuators move shift drums or forks. Typical causes are a sticking shift actuator or valve, low or unstable system pressure, mechanical damage, or a faulty position or speed signal. Common causes: Shift actuator or shift valve sticking (medium likelihood); System pressure low or unstable (medium likelihood); Mechanical damage in the gear train (medium likelihood); Position or speed sensor signal wrong (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission no longer shifts and stays in one gear; Limp mode, transmission warning. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P07FF – Cold Start Transmission Performance
text: P07FF: Cold Start Transmission Performance. P07FF means the transmission does not work as expected during the cold-start phase, shortly after starting with cold, thick fluid – for example a gear preselection or a clutch or valve response outside the expected window. The only documented user is Mercedes-Benz: its 2024 bulletin for the eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox 8G-DCT in the compact models (A-Class, CLA, GLA, GLB) names P07FF together with P0921, with reverse not available, a possible limp-home mode and the MIL; after switching off and on everything works again, and the fix was new control unit software. No thresholds or trip counts are published. It is not CARB's cold-start emission strategy, which concerns engine and catalyst heating (P050A ff), but a functional check of the transmission. Common causes: Transmission control module software misjudging the cold phase (high likelihood); Shift valve or hydraulics too slow with cold fluid (medium likelihood); Wrong or aged fluid, low level (low likelihood); Fluid temperature sensor reading wrong (low likelihood). Symptoms: Reverse not available (message in the cluster); Check engine lamp on; Limp-home mode shortly after a cold start; Normal again after switching off and on. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0800 – Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)
text: P0800: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request). P0800 works like P0700 for the transmission: the transfer case control module has detected a fault of its own that it rates as emissions-relevant and asks the engine control module to turn on the MIL. The engine module only stores P0800; the actual fault – often C, U or manufacturer codes – sits in the transfer case module and needs a scan tool that addresses it. CARB requires monitoring of an electronic transfer case only where it feeds other diagnostics, for example the 4WD-low signal that GM uses as an enable condition; this is why most transfer case modules never request the MIL and P0800 hardly appears in manufacturer documents. A GM bulletin for 2020–23 trucks with 'Service 4WD' and the MIL points to wiring and terminal contact at the transfer case. Common causes: Fault in the transfer case system stored in its module (shift motor, sensor, clutch) (high likelihood); Wiring or connector at the transfer case (terminal tension, corrosion) (medium likelihood); Transfer case module software (medium likelihood); Transfer case module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; 'Service 4WD' or similar warning; All-wheel drive or low range cannot be selected. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0801 – Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit/Open
text: P0801: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit/Open. On GM manual gearboxes (Tremec T56/TR6060 in Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V and ATS-V) the engine module drives a solenoid that blocks reverse while the car moves forward. P0801 means its control circuit is open. GM's tables describe the check: the low-side driver's internal diagnosis flags an open line with at least 9 V and the engine above 250 rpm, 20 failures in 25 samples of 250 ms – about 6 s; in 2006 a 5 s comparison of commanded and actual driver state. GM rates it type C, emissions-neutral and without MIL, from 2019 with a 'service vehicle soon' note. Depending on how it fails, reverse cannot be engaged or is no longer blocked. The title was updated to the current J2012 wording with '/Open'. Common causes: Connector at the reverse inhibit solenoid loose or corroded (high likelihood); Solenoid coil open (medium likelihood); Harness between engine module and gearbox damaged (medium likelihood); Engine module driver faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Reverse hard or impossible to engage; Reverse no longer blocked; Service note in the driver display, usually no MIL. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0802 – Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open
text: P0802: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open. On older vehicles with a separate transmission module and no MIL message on the CAN bus, the transmission module signals 'MIL on' over its own wire to the engine module. P0802 checks this wire for an open circuit. GM's Duramax tables of 2004 and 2005 (Allison 1000) describe it: at key-on the transmission module briefly pulls the line active like a bulb check; if the engine module sees no off-to-on transition between 0.125 and 7 s after ignition, the line is treated as open – type B, MIL after two trips. Only then is P0700 evaluated. The wire itself must be monitored because an open line would stop transmission emission faults from lighting the MIL. Newer vehicles send the request over CAN, where faults appear as U codes. Common causes: MIL request wire or connector between the modules open or corroded (high likelihood); Transmission module without power or ground (fuse, relay) (medium likelihood); Module output or input faulty (low likelihood); Wrong or retrofitted transmission module without this line (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Transmission faults no longer light the MIL; Usually no change in driving. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0803 – Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit
text: P0803: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit. GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid in the shifter housing that, at light load and low speed blocks the way from 1st into 2nd and 3rd so the driver shifts 1 to 4 – a measure for fuel economy ratings; the 1-4 lamp (P0804) shows it. P0803 means the solenoid control circuit is open. GM's tables check the low-side driver while it is off: too low a voltage or over 200 kΩ to ground, with at least 9 V and over 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms (2019 LT5: 20 of 25), type B with the MIL after two trips; shorts are P080C and P080D. An open circuit leaves the solenoid unpowered, so 1 to 2 always works. 'Skip-shift eliminators' with the wrong resistance are a frequent cause. Common causes: Solenoid unplugged or replaced by a skip-shift eliminator with the wrong resistance (high likelihood); Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded (high likelihood); Solenoid coil open (medium likelihood); Harness damaged (medium likelihood); Engine module driver faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp after two trips; 1-4 lockout no longer works (1-2 always possible); Otherwise no change in driving. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0804 – Upshift/Skip Shift Lamp Control Circuit
text: P0804: Upshift/Skip Shift Lamp Control Circuit. With GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes, a '1-4' lamp in the cluster tells the driver that the lockout is active and to shift from 1st directly into 4th. P0804 means the control circuit of this lamp is faulty – open, shorted, or the lamp does not follow its command. No GM table from 2004 to 2025 available to us contains it, because newer cars switch the indicator by a CAN message from the instrument cluster without a separate engine-module line check; the code therefore mainly concerns older vehicles with a lamp driven directly by the engine module. The lockout itself (P0803) keeps working, only the hint is missing; there is no limp mode, and the MIL behavior is not documented. Common causes: Bulb or LED in the cluster faulty (high likelihood); Wire or connector between engine module and cluster open or shorted (medium likelihood); Instrument cluster board faulty (medium likelihood); Engine module output faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: 1-4 lamp never lights or stays on; Possibly check engine lamp; Lockout works without the hint. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0805 – Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit
text: P0805: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit. The J2012 family 'Clutch Position Sensor A' (P0805 circuit, P0806 range/performance, P0807 low, P0808 high, P0809 intermittent, P080A not learned) covers the position of a clutch – the pedal of a manual gearbox, the clutch actuator of an automated or dual-clutch gearbox, or a clutch inside an automatic. P0805 is the general circuit fault. Uses differ: Nissan's 2022 Pathfinder with its nine-speed automatic stores it in the transmission module, lights the MIL and disables idle stop ('Idle Stop System Fault'), fixed with new software. Ford's DPS6 dual-clutch gearbox uses it for the module-internal chip that drives the clutch A motor, so a control unit fault rather than an outside sensor. GM reads its clutch pedal sensor under P0806–P0808 only. Common causes: Clutch position sensor faulty (pedal or actuator) (high likelihood); Connector or harness open, corroded or shorted (medium likelihood); Transmission module software (Nissan) (medium likelihood); Control unit internal fault (Ford DPS6: clutch motor driver) (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Idle stop disabled ('Idle Stop System Fault'); Jerky driving or harsh clutch engagement (dual clutch). Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0806 – Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0806: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance. The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0806 is the plausibility check. On GM's LT4 manual cars the pedal sensor is compared with gear detection: if it reports the clutch pressed while engine and output speed show a valid gear, a filtered position error above 4 % sets the code (above 5.6 mph, not in 4WD low), type A with the MIL after one trip. On Ford's DPS6 it reports a fault of the Hall sensors on the clutch A motor; Saab sets it for a frozen pedal signal and switches off cruise control. Common causes: Pedal sensor or Hall sensors of the clutch motor faulty (high likelihood); Pedal sensor misadjusted or not relearned after clutch work (medium likelihood); Harness or connector with contact resistance (medium likelihood); Clutch actuator motor faulty (DPS6) (medium likelihood); Master cylinder leaking, pedal does not fully return (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Cruise control and start-stop not working; Engine starts only with the pedal fully pressed, or not at all; Dual clutch: jerky take-off, limp mode. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0807 – Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low
text: P0807: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low. The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0807 means the signal is too low. GM's three-wire pedal sensor on a 5 V reference has dead bands at both ends: below 4 % of the reference counts as low or open, 200 of 250 samples of 12.5 ms (about 3 s), engine not cranking, over 9 V, type A with the MIL after one trip. Saab names an open circuit or short to ground. With the clutch position unknown, cruise control, start-stop and starter release by the sensor are blocked. Common causes: Signal wire open or shorted to ground (high likelihood); 5 V reference of the sensor missing (medium likelihood); Pedal sensor faulty internally (medium likelihood); Connector corroded or pins loose (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Cruise control not working; Start-stop disabled, possibly no engine start. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0808 – Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High
text: P0808: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High. The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0808 means the signal is too high. GM sets it above 96 % of the 5 V reference with the same 200 of 250 samples of 12.5 ms, type A with the MIL after one trip; Saab's 2012 9-3 above 4.8 V for longer than 0.6 s, with cruise control switched off. Typical causes are an open sensor ground or a signal wire shorted to the 5 V reference or battery voltage. Common causes: Sensor ground open (high likelihood); Signal shorted to 5 V or battery voltage (medium likelihood); Pedal sensor faulty (medium likelihood); Moisture or corrosion in the connector (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Cruise control not working; Start-stop disabled. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0809 – Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
text: P0809: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent. The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P0809 is documented only for Ford's DPS6 (Fiesta from 2011, Focus from 2012): the motor that operates clutch A carries three Hall sensors, one per phase, and while the motor turns they must produce a fixed sequence; a wrong sequence sets the code. The clutch B counterpart is P087E. The module then loses confidence in the clutch position, so clutch A with the odd gears 1, 3 and 5 is restricted. GM and Saab do not use P0809; Ford publishes no thresholds. Common causes: Clutch A actuator motor or its Hall sensors faulty (high likelihood); Loose contact at the actuator connector (medium likelihood); Transmission module Hall evaluation faulty (low likelihood); Supply voltage dips (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Jerky or judder take-off; Limp mode, odd gears missing. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P080A – Clutch Position Not Learned
text: P080A: Clutch Position Not Learned. The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same. Ford's DPS6 dual clutch uses the family for the electric motor of clutch A. P080A means the learned clutch position is missing or implausible. On GM manual cars the factory learns the pedal position 'clutch fully pressed', and the engine module then tracks it as the clutch wears; a learned value outside 9.0–36.0 % of travel sets the code (250 ms, type A, one trip), a factory counter keeps the MIL off during assembly. Saab clears it by relearning with the scan tool. A relearn is needed after replacing the pedal sensor, master cylinder, clutch or engine module. Common causes: Relearn not done after sensor, clutch or module replacement (high likelihood); Clutch badly worn or misadjusted (medium likelihood); Pedal sensor misadjusted or wrongly fitted (medium likelihood); Engine module reprogrammed or replaced (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Start-stop, cruise control or hill start assist disabled; Engine may start only with the pedal at the stop. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P080B – Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P080B: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance. GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080B would be the range or performance fault of this circuit: electrically plausible, but outside the expected range for the command – for example a coil resistance outside its window, a partial short or contact resistance. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM's tables from 2006 to 2019 check the solenoid only electrically (P0803 open, P080C short to ground, P080D short to positive). CARB requires a functional check of outputs where feasible. The lockout may then work unreliably. Common causes: Solenoid coil with shorted turns or resistance out of range (medium likelihood); Retrofitted skip-shift eliminator with the wrong value (medium likelihood); Corroded connector at the gearbox (contact resistance) (medium likelihood); Control module or software (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer); 1-4 lockout works not at all or only sometimes; Otherwise no change in driving. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P080C – Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Low
text: P080C: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Low. GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080C means the control line is shorted to ground: with the driver off it should sit at battery voltage through the coil but reads low (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to ground). GM checks it from 9 V (2015/16: 11–32 V) and above 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms, type B with the MIL after two trips; the 2019 LT5 uses 20 of 25 samples and type A, one trip. In the 2015/16 tables P080C also covers an open circuit. A low-side short keeps the solenoid energized, so the lockout may stay active. Common causes: Control wire chafed through to ground at gearbox or frame (high likelihood); Solenoid coil shorted to its housing (medium likelihood); Connector corroded or water ingress (medium likelihood); Older GM modules: circuit open or solenoid unplugged (medium likelihood); Engine module driver faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp; 1-4 lockout permanently active or not working; 1-4 lamp possibly unrelated to the lockout. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P080D – Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit High
text: P080D: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit High. GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid that, at light load, blocks the way from 1st into 2nd so the driver shifts 1 to 4; the 1-4 lamp shows it (P0804). The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit. P080D means the control line is shorted to positive: with the low-side driver on, the line should be pulled to ground but reads high (GM: 0.5 Ω or less to the supply). The solenoid cannot be energized and the driver is protected or switched off. GM checks it only with the driver on, from 9 V (2015/16: 11–32 V) and above 250 rpm, 5 of 6 samples of 250 ms, type B with the MIL after two trips in all tables from 2015 to 2019. Without power the solenoid does not lock, so 1 to 2 stays free. Common causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage (damaged harness) (high likelihood); Solenoid coil with shorted turns (resistance near zero) (medium likelihood); Substitute resistor ('eliminator') with too low a value (medium likelihood); Engine module driver faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp after two trips; 1-4 lockout not working; Otherwise no change in driving. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0810 – Clutch Position Control Error
text: P0810: Clutch Position Control Error. P0810 reports a control error of an electronically or hydraulically operated clutch: commanded and actual position differ too much or for too long. It is documented on Stellantis plug-in hybrids – Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe with the 8P75PH transmission – where it concerns the K0 disconnect clutch between engine and electric motor. According to the 2024 and 2025 bulletins the clutch adaptation ran at standstill or in electric mode, drive was lost until the next key cycle and the MIL came on; the cause was too tight setting parameters, fixed with new transmission software, partly together with P2885. On automated or dual-clutch gearboxes the same idea applies when the clutch actuator misses its target position. Common causes: Control unit software with too tight parameters (high likelihood); Clutch actuator or hydraulics (pressure, valve) faulty (medium likelihood); Clutch position sensor inaccurate (medium likelihood); Wrong or aged fluid, worn clutch (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Transmission warning message; Loss of drive until the next key cycle. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0811 – Excessive Clutch A Slippage
text: P0811: Excessive Clutch A Slippage. P0811 means clutch A slips too much while it should be closed – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 1 with the odd gears. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch; thresholds are not published. Audi's seven-speed S tronic DL382 (A4 to A7 and Q5, 2020–24) sets it intermittently together with P081E and input speed sensor codes, partly also clutch temperature too high; the cause was the transmission module calculating wrong slip, and the fix was a new module. Genuine slip from wear or overheating shows as flaring take-off and burnt fluid. The module limits torque, may lock out the affected half and go to limp mode. Common causes: Transmission module calculating wrong slip (speed capture) (high likelihood); Clutch worn or overheated (medium likelihood); Fluid burnt or wrong (wet clutch) (medium likelihood); Clutch pressure or actuator too low (medium likelihood); Input speed sensor faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission warning, limp mode; Engine flares, poor acceleration; Judder on take-off; Burning smell. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0812 – Reverse Input Circuit
text: P0812: Reverse Input Circuit. P0812 concerns the input 'reverse engaged' at the engine or transmission module – the reverse or back-up lamp switch on a manual gearbox, or the R contact of a selector. Modules check it for open or stuck states and against a second source such as a gear position sensor or the direction from speed sensors. A Honda patent describes this double detection: reverse counts only when switch and gear position sensor agree; if only one reports R, it is a fault and engine speed is limited. No manufacturer document with thresholds is available to us. Back-up lamps, reversing camera or parking aids may fail; on automated manual gearboxes reverse may be blocked. CARB lets such safety and comfort inputs run without the MIL. Common causes: Reverse or back-up lamp switch faulty or misadjusted (high likelihood); Connector loose or wire broken (e.g. after clutch work) (high likelihood); Back-up lamp circuit fuse blown (medium likelihood); Gear position sensor reporting the wrong position (low likelihood). Symptoms: Back-up lamps never or always on; Reversing camera or parking aid does not switch on; Usually no check engine lamp. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0813 – Reverse Output Circuit
text: P0813: Reverse Output Circuit. P0813 concerns a signal 'reverse active' that a module puts out – usually the transmission module, on manual cars the engine or body module – for example to the back-up lamp relay, the reversing camera or the body module. Like other driver outputs it is checked by comparing commanded and actual state, which reveals an open circuit or a short. Saab's 2012 transmission module reports a short to positive on its park/neutral output in the same way. No manufacturer document with thresholds for the reverse output is available to us. Back-up lamps, camera or mirror tilt may stop working; driving itself is not affected, and CARB allows such outputs without the MIL. Common causes: Wire from module to relay or body module open or shorted (high likelihood); Back-up lamp relay or connected load faulty (medium likelihood); Connector corroded (medium likelihood); Module output stage faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Back-up lamps not working; Reversing camera or parking beeper does not activate; Stored code without driving effects. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0814 – Transmission Range Display Circuit
text: P0814: Transmission Range Display Circuit. P0814 concerns the drive or data circuit of the range display – the PRNDL or PRNDM display or lighting on the selector, sometimes in the instrument cluster. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: the electronic shift module stores P0814 with the MIL on, the selector lighting flickers or goes dark, and in a 2020 bulletin the lever could be moved out of park during cranking so that the engine stalled. The cause was software in the shift module, fixed by reflashing; a 2022 bulletin adds P081C. A wrong or missing range display matters for safety because the driver cannot reliably see P, R or N. No thresholds are published. Common causes: Shift module software (Jeep Compass) (high likelihood); Connector or wire to the selector display or cluster (medium likelihood); Display LED or selector module faulty (medium likelihood); Range sensor or transmission module delivering an invalid range (low likelihood). Symptoms: Range display on the selector flickers or stays dark; Check engine lamp (Jeep); Lever can leave P during cranking, engine stalls (Jeep). Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0815 – Upshift Switch Circuit
text: P0815: Upshift Switch Circuit. Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch. P0815 is the upshift switch. GM's 2019 and 2025 tables set it when 'tap up' stays on for more than 1 s in P or N, or permanently in a drive range; the 2018 hybrid table uses 2 s in P/N and 655 s in drive; type C without MIL. Ford's 6R80 and 6F35 SelectShift report a switch closed in P, R or N without MIL. On Saab's 9-4X with the 6T70 a Hall switch feeds a resistor network on one wire: a short to positive sets P0815 or P0816, a short to ground or an open sets P0826. Manual shifting is then disabled. Common causes: Tap switch or paddle sticking or faulty (high likelihood); Signal wire shorted to positive (medium likelihood); Selector assembly (Hall sensor, resistor network) faulty (medium likelihood); Clockspring or steering wheel wiring (paddles) (low likelihood). Symptoms: Manual up shifting not working; Transmission stays in the normal automatic mode; No check engine lamp. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0816 – Downshift Switch Circuit
text: P0816: Downshift Switch Circuit. Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch. P0816 is the mirror of P0815 for the downshift switch. GM's 2025 table sets it when 'tap down' stays on for more than 1 s (100 ms raster, over 9 V), the 2018 hybrid table after 2 s in P/N or 655 s in drive, type C without MIL; Saab's 9-4X after 1 s in P/N or 10 minutes in a drive range; Ford's SelectShift when the switch is closed in P, R or N, without MIL. On selectors with a resistor network a short to positive in the downshift branch sets P0816. Manual shifting is disabled, automatic operation stays normal. Common causes: Downshift switch or paddle sticking or faulty (high likelihood); Signal wire shorted to positive (medium likelihood); Selector assembly faulty (medium likelihood); Body or transmission module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Manual down shifting not working; Transmission stays in the normal automatic mode; No check engine lamp. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0817 – Starter Disable Circuit/Open
text: P0817: Starter Disable Circuit/Open. The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P0817 is the general or open-circuit fault of this line. Saab sets it when the output reports 'start allowed' but the feedback shows 'off' for more than 100 ms, twice in a row, with 6–16 V and no limp mode; it rates the fault type D, without any lamp. The engine then cannot be started. Low and high are P081A and P081B; vehicles that send the start release over a bus often report similar faults as U codes or P0850. Common causes: Starter disable wire to the body module open or shorted (high likelihood); Connector corroded or pins pushed back (medium likelihood); Transmission module with built-in range switch faulty (medium likelihood); Body module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine does not crank in P or N; Start possible in only one of the two ranges; No check engine lamp. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0818 – Driveline Disconnect Switch Input Circuit
text: P0818: Driveline Disconnect Switch Input Circuit. P0818 concerns a switch input that reports whether the driveline is disconnected – on four-wheel-drive vehicles typically the neutral position of the transfer case or an axle disconnect, on hybrids a disconnect clutch between engine and transmission, as a Ford patent uses the term. It matters for OBD because in transfer case neutral the engine runs without load and wheel speed does not match the ratio, so misfire, ratio and vehicle speed monitors must know about it; CARB requires monitoring only then. The check would be a circuit or plausibility test against the speed ratio. No manufacturer document available to us uses P0818, and which of the two meanings applies cannot be proven. All-wheel drive or neutral may then be unavailable. Common causes: Neutral or disconnect switch at the transfer case or axle faulty (high likelihood); Underbody wiring or connector corroded or damaged (high likelihood); Transfer case actuator does not reach its end position (medium likelihood); Control module or software (low likelihood). Symptoms: All-wheel drive or neutral cannot be selected; 'Service 4WD' or similar warning; Possibly check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer). Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0819 – Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation
text: P0819: Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation. P0819 is the plausibility check between the tap-up and tap-down switches and the range sensor: a shift request may only appear in the manual gate or in drive. If a tap switch reports in P, R or N, or taps arrive without the manual gate being detected, the correlation is broken. GM's 2019 tables and Ford's 2012 SelectShift run exactly this check but assign the fault to the switch concerned as P0815 or P0816; no manufacturer with its own P0819 is documented. Manual shifting would be disabled while automatic operation stays normal, without the MIL. Causes are a sticking tap switch, a misadjusted range sensor or selector cable, or the selector wiring. Common causes: Tap switch sticking or faulty (high likelihood); Range sensor or selector sensor misadjusted or faulty (medium likelihood); Selector cable misadjusted (medium likelihood); Selector wiring or connectors (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Tap or manual mode not working; Range display partly wrong; No check engine lamp. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P081A – Starter Disable Circuit Low
text: P081A: Starter Disable Circuit Low. The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P081A means the start release line is too low – the output is shorted to ground or open. Saab's 2012 9-3 transmission module checks it in D, where the output must have a defined state, with 9–18 V, not in limp mode and continuously; no time threshold is published. Because the engine module then sees no 'P/N', the engine may not start. Common causes: P/N line to the engine module shorted to ground (high likelihood); Line or connector open (high likelihood); Connector oxidized or pins pushed back (medium likelihood); Transmission module output stage faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine does not start or only sometimes; Starter does not crank in P or N; No check engine lamp. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P081B – Starter Disable Circuit High
text: P081B: Starter Disable Circuit High. The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V). P081B means the start release line stays at positive, so the 'P/N' level is present in a drive range. Saab's 2012 9-3 checks it only outside P and N, with 9–18 V and not in limp mode. A short to positive could in principle allow a start in gear; the diagnosis catches it, and Saab names as the effect that the engine may not start because the release is refused. Common causes: P/N line shorted to positive (chafed against a supply wire) (high likelihood); Moisture or corrosion in the connector (medium likelihood); Transmission module output stage faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine does not start or starts unreliably; Start release in the wrong range possible (safety risk); No check engine lamp. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P081C – Park Input Circuit
text: P081C: Park Input Circuit. P081C concerns the input 'park position' – the P contact of the selector or shift module, or the park pawl feedback – which controls switching off the ignition, key release, starter release and the 'not in park' warning. It is documented on the 2017–22 Jeep Compass with the nine-speed automatic: a 2022 bulletin lists P081C with the MIL on, with 'Vehicle not in Park' shown although P is engaged; the car cannot be switched off, modules stay awake and the battery drains. The cause was shift module software, fixed by reflashing. The check is a circuit or plausibility test of the P signal against the range sensor; no thresholds are published. Common causes: Shift module software (Jeep Compass) (high likelihood); P contact or selector switch faulty or misadjusted (medium likelihood); Selector cable misadjusted (medium likelihood); Wire or connector (medium likelihood). Symptoms: 'Not in park' message although P is engaged; Ignition cannot be switched off, battery drains; Check engine lamp (Jeep). Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P081D – Neutral Input Circuit
text: P081D: Neutral Input Circuit. P081D concerns the input 'neutral' – the N contact of the selector or range switch, on manual cars a neutral switch or sensor for start-stop. Neutral serves for starter release, idle control without load, start-stop release and enabling other diagnostics. The check would be a circuit or plausibility test against the range sensor or speed ratio. No manufacturer document available to us uses P081D; its sister P081C is documented on the Jeep Compass, and Saab's range switch shows that P and N are the two start positions. The engine may then not start in N, start-stop is disabled and idle diagnostics may be suspended. Common causes: Neutral contact, range switch or neutral sensor faulty or misadjusted (high likelihood); Selector or shift cable misadjusted (medium likelihood); Wire or connector (medium likelihood); Control module or software (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine does not start in N (only in P); Start-stop not working; Range display does not show N. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P081E – Excessive Clutch B Slippage
text: P081E: Excessive Clutch B Slippage. P081E is the counterpart to P0811 for clutch B – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 2 with the even gears and reverse, which Audi calls 'clutch 2'. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch and flags slip above its limit. Audi's DL382 S tronic (2020–24) sets it intermittently with P0811 and input speed codes; the bulletins report a transmission malfunction and 'reverse gear unavailable', and the fix was a new transmission module with improved parts from late 2023. A failed clutch 2 typically means no reverse and no even gears. Common causes: Transmission module speed capture faulty (high likelihood); Clutch 2 worn or overheated (medium likelihood); Fluid or pressure (medium likelihood); Input speed sensor B faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission warning, limp mode; Reverse or even gears not available; Engine flares on gear changes. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P081F – Brake Transmission Shift Interlock (BTSI) Signal Correlation
text: P081F: Brake Transmission Shift Interlock (BTSI) Signal Correlation. The brake transmission shift interlock (BTSI) is a solenoid or actuator that locks the selector in park until the brake pedal is pressed, as US rule FMVSS 114 requires. 'Signal correlation' is the plausibility check between the interlock command or feedback and its input signals – brake switch and selector position: for example the lock released without a brake signal, or still active although the brake is pressed. The selector then cannot leave park, or it moves without the brake and the safety function is missing. Electrical faults of the lock solenoid have their own codes P0928–P0931. No manufacturer document with P081F is available to us; a GM service update for the 2016 Malibu and 2016–17 Volt explains the part and the 'won't shift out of park' complaint. CARB may exempt such safety parts from monitoring. Common causes: Brake lamp switch misadjusted or faulty (high likelihood); Interlock solenoid or locking mechanism sticking (medium likelihood); Wire or connector to the selector (medium likelihood); Selector module, control unit or software (low likelihood). Symptoms: Selector cannot be moved out of P; Selector moves out of P without the brake; Warning about brake or range. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0820 – Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Circuit
text: P0820: Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Circuit. Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0820 is the umbrella code: the module does not tell X from Y, or sees an invalid combination of both axes that matches no gate position. The only documented user is Mitsubishi's 2022 Outlander PHEV, which names it 'shift lever position (main) circuit malfunction' and sets it for an impossible lever position, without published thresholds. GM reads its X/Y sensors under P082A–P082F instead. Range selection may be blocked and the vehicle stays in P or N. Common causes: Wire or connector between selector and module open or shorted (high likelihood); Position sensor in the selector assembly faulty (high likelihood); Sensor supply (5 V reference) or ground faulty (medium likelihood); Transmission, hybrid or selector module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Range cannot be selected or only partly; Vehicle stays in P or N, or limp mode; Transmission warning, range display flashes or missing. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0821 – Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit
text: P0821: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit. Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0821 is the general circuit fault of X sensor 1 – an open or invalid signal – for modules that do not report low and high separately. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM reports the same axis in finer steps as P082A, P082B and P082C. A GM patent describes checking each sensor's x value separately: an invalid value makes that sensor unusable, and with a redundant sensor 2 the car can usually go on. Common causes: X position sensor in the selector assembly faulty (high likelihood); Signal wire or connector open or corroded (high likelihood); Liquid or dirt in the center console (medium likelihood); Control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission warning in the cluster; Ranges partly not selectable; With both sensors failed the vehicle stays in P or N. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0822 – Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit
text: P0822: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit. Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0822 is the same for the Y axis – the second direction of movement, on an H-gate the select gate. No manufacturer document available to us uses it; GM reports the Y axis as P082D, P082E and P082F. A failed Y sensor can hide a gate change, for example into the manual gate or the reverse gate. Common causes: Y position sensor in the selector assembly faulty (high likelihood); Signal wire or connector open or corroded (high likelihood); Liquid or dirt in the center console (medium likelihood); Control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission warning in the cluster; Manual gate or reverse not selectable; With both sensors failed the vehicle stays in P or N. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0823 – Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0823: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. P0823 watches X sensor 1 for short dropouts and jumps – a signal that changes faster than the lever can move, or briefly disappears. Such checks typically count jumps within a time window; no manufacturer publishes thresholds. GM folds a disturbed X signal (a frequency error of the PWM signal) into P082A, and its patent rejects a value at once if it was faulty before and differs from its partner. Common causes: Loose contact at the selector connector (high likelihood); Chafed or broken wire in the harness to the console (medium likelihood); Sensor worn (potentiometer track) or Hall sensor disturbed (medium likelihood); Interference or ground fault (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission warning comes and goes; Selected range occasionally not accepted; Occasional limp-mode reaction. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0825 – Gear Lever Push-Pull Switch (Shift Anticipate)
text: P0825: Gear Lever Push-Pull Switch (Shift Anticipate). P0825 concerns a switch on the selector that reports pushing or pulling the lever – sequential + and – shifting – or the start of a shift movement, hence 'shift anticipate'. Its purpose: the control unit of an automated manual gearbox can prepare clutch and engine torque before the actual gear change is detected; a LuK patent describes such shift-intent detection, which reports intent when the lever signal exceeds a filtered, load-dependent reference and cancels on a reversal. A fault is typically a switch reporting 'pressed' without lever movement or never, implausible against the X/Y sensors. No manufacturer document with P0825 is available to us. Shift-intent detection is then off, gear changes are slower or sequential shifting is disabled. Common causes: Switch in the selector faulty or sticking (high likelihood); Wire or connector to the selector assembly (medium likelihood); Liquid or dirt in the shift gate (medium likelihood); Control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Delayed or jerky gear changes (automated manual); Sequential tapping not working; Transmission warning in the cluster. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0826 – Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit
text: P0826: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit. Many selectors read tap-up and tap-down over one shared wire with voltage steps or a resistor network; P0826–P0828 cover this shared circuit, P0815/P0816 the single directions. P0826 is the general fault of the shared circuit. GM (6L80 in 2011, 2019, 2025, hybrids) sets it when the circuit shows an invalid voltage for at least 60 s with 8.6–32 V and 400–7500 rpm, without MIL. On Saab's 9-4X with the 6T70 a short to ground or an open sets P0826. Saab's 2003–04 9-3 Sentronic reports below 0.2 V or above 6.7 V for over 30 s under P0826 with a fault-type byte, lights 'Check gearbox' and locks the lever in P/N. Ram's 2025 heavy-duty trucks set it with P0827 and P085F and the MIL, fixed with transmission software. Manual shifting is then disabled. Common causes: Wire or connector between selector and module open or shorted (high likelihood); Selector assembly (Hall switch, resistor network, module) faulty (high likelihood); Transmission module software (Ram) (medium likelihood); Clockspring or steering wheel wiring (paddles) (low likelihood). Symptoms: Tap or manual shifting not working; Transmission runs only in automatic mode; Transmission warning; lever locked in P/N (Saab 9-3). Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0827 – Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Low

title: P0829 – 5-6 Shift
text: P0829: 5-6 Shift. Shift codes check the gear change itself: the module compares the commanded change with the speed trace and flags a shift that takes too long, does not happen, flares or binds up two clutches. P0829 covers the change between 5th and 6th gear in either direction; J2012 placed it here because P0785 ff were already taken, between P0781 '1-2 Shift' to P0784 '4-5 Shift' and P07DA/P07DB for 6-7 and 7-8. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: Ford's Diesel summary checks shift completion without a gear-specific code (speed must drop by more than 30 rpm on an upshift, flare above 300 rpm), Ford's automatics feed the solenoid function codes and GM the clutch valve codes. It exists only on transmissions with at least six gears; MIL and trip count follow the manufacturer. Common causes: Fluid low or aged (high likelihood); Shift or clutch pressure valve for 5-6 sticking (medium likelihood); Clutch or brake of 6th gear worn (medium likelihood); Adaptives or software (medium likelihood); Input or output speed sensor delivering wrong values (low likelihood). Symptoms: Harsh, delayed or missing 5-6 shift; Engine speed flares during the shift; Limp mode in a fixed gear, possibly MIL. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P082A – Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance
text: P082A: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance. Gear lever X and Y position sensors detect a selector's position in two directions: on an H-gate shift and select direction (a LuK patent uses two sensors about 90° apart), on a shift-by-wire lever its two axes. P0820 covers the whole X-Y circuit, P0821–P0824 and P082A–P082F sensor 1, P089A–P08A3 a redundant sensor 2. GM uses P082A–P082F on its electronic range selector (2019 tables, Cadillac XT4, 2025): a Hall sensor delivers a PWM signal, measured as duty cycle. P082A sets when the measured X position lies outside the lever's path (5.5 % duty cycle equals about 100 N of side force), the PWM signal has a frequency error, or X sensors 1 and 2 differ by more than 12 %; 3 of 4 samples in 2019, 10 of 12 in 2025 with an added angle check. Type B, MIL after two trips; the other sensor takes over. Common causes: Selector assembly faulty (Hall sensor, magnet, worn mechanism) (high likelihood); Connector or wire with resistance or interference (frequency error) (medium likelihood); Lever mechanically blocked (object in the console) (medium likelihood); Engine or selector module software (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp after two trips (GM); 'Shift to park' message or transmission warning; Range selection restricted; with both sensors failed the vehicle goes to park. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0830 – Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit
text: P0830: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit. Clutch pedal switches A and B are digital inputs of manual gearboxes: they release the starter only with the pedal pressed, switch off cruise control and tell start-stop whether the clutch is open. Which switch is A or B is up to each manufacturer – FCA calls the pedal-up switch A. Ford's 2020–23 summary checks a dual switch over more than 40 pedal applications and reports a stuck switch without MIL (P0830 stuck high, P0833 stuck low, comparison P0704). P0830 is the general fault of switch A. On Ford it means the switch is stuck high. On a 2012–13 Jeep Wrangler with the six-speed manual, Chrysler reprogrammed the engine module for unwanted cruise control cut-outs with P0830; an FCA tip notes that a driver resting a foot on the pedal keeps the pedal-up switch on and sets the code. The MIL depends on the manufacturer. Common causes: Switch faulty or misadjusted (high likelihood); Foot resting on the clutch pedal keeps the switch actuated (medium likelihood); Software misjudgment (reprogramming) (medium likelihood); Wiring, connector or remote-start bypass (low likelihood). Symptoms: Cruise control switches off or cannot be activated; Start-stop disabled; Engine may not crank (starter interlock). Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0836 – Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit
text: P0836: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit. The four-wheel-drive switch tells the engine module which transfer case range is engaged. 4WD low changes the ratio of engine to road speed by about 2.7:1 on GM trucks, so GM uses 'not in 4WD low' as an enable condition for idle speed and clutch pedal checks; that is why CARB requires monitoring such inputs. P0836 is the general circuit fault of this switch – an open or an invalid state. No manufacturer document available to us uses it: GM reports the same part from 2006 to 2025 as P2771 '4WD Low Switch Circuit', comparing the switch position with the measured transfer case ratio while driving (from 15 mph, diesel 5 mph, 2–7 s), without MIL on gasoline and type B on diesel. Ford has no such code. The 4WD indicator may flash and dependent diagnostics may be suspended. Common causes: Position switch or sensor at the transfer case faulty (high likelihood); Wire or connector at the transfer case corroded or torn (high likelihood); Selector switch in the cabin faulty (medium likelihood); Control module or software (low likelihood). Symptoms: 4WD indicator flashes or stays off; 4WD range cannot be selected or display wrong; Possibly check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer). Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0837 – Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0837: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit Range/Performance. P0837 means the signal is electrically valid but implausible: the reported position does not fit the driving state, or a multiplexed resistor switch sits between its position windows. GM runs this check on the same part under P2771: switch 'not low' while the transfer case ratio is 2.6–2.8, or 'low' at 0.9–1.1 (diesel windows 5.7–8.0 and 0.7–1.55), under load and in gear. title: P0839 – Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit High
text: P0839: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit High. The four-wheel-drive switch tells the engine module which transfer case range is engaged. 4WD low changes the ratio of engine to road speed by about 2.7:1 on GM trucks, so GM uses 'not in 4WD low' as an enable condition for idle speed and clutch pedal checks; that is why CARB requires monitoring such inputs. P0839 means the switch signal is above its valid range – a short to positive or, with a pull-up circuit, an open in wire, switch or ground. GM describes the open for its 4WD low switch as 'continuous open (stuck off)': the module sees 'not in 4WD low' although low is engaged (ratio 2.6–2.8, diesel 5.7–8.0). No manufacturer document available to us uses P0839. Dependent diagnostics could then run wrongly in low range, so modules suspend them or use a substitute value. Common causes: Switch signal or ground wire open, connector unplugged (high likelihood); Signal wire shorted to positive (medium likelihood); Switch or sensor open internally (medium likelihood); Control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: 4WD indicator flashes or stays off; 4WD range cannot be selected or display wrong; Possibly check engine lamp (depends on manufacturer). Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P083A – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch G Circuit

title: P083F – Clutch Pedal Switch A/B Correlation
text: P083F: Clutch Pedal Switch A/B Correlation. Manual cars often carry two clutch pedal switches: one near the top of the pedal travel for cruise control and start-stop, one near the floor that releases the starter. Pressing the pedal must switch them in a sensible order; P083F means their states contradict each other. Stellantis documents it for the 2025 Jeep Wrangler manual: the engine does not crank and start-stop is blocked, caused by corroded contacts in the clutch interlock switch, which is replaced. Ford checks the same pair over more than 40 pedal applications but reports it as P0704, without MIL. Common causes: One clutch switch faulty or corroded (high likelihood); Switch misadjusted or not seated after clutch or pedal work (medium likelihood); Open circuit or contact resistance in harness or connector (medium likelihood); Pedal does not fully return (stop, hydraulics) (low likelihood). Symptoms: Start-stop not working; Engine does not crank although the clutch is pressed; Cruise control cannot be set. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P0840 – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit
text: P0840: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch A Circuit. Transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch A and B are inputs inside the automatic gearbox. A switch only reports pressure present or absent, a sensor reports a value. The letter is the maker's choice: Allison 1000 uses A and B for the switches on shift valves S1 and S2, GM's CVT for the primary and secondary pulley sensors, GM's 2025 8-speed A for the lube pressure sensor; Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes instead. P0840 is the general circuit fault. GM documents it for the 2006 Allison: the module compares the commanded position of valve S1 with the switch feedback and retries the valve if they disagree; it then tells an electrical, mechanical or sporadic case apart. Type A, MIL after one trip. From 2007 Allison reports the same test under P0842/P0843. Common causes: Pressure switch or sensor A faulty or stuck (high likelihood); Sticking shift valve or dirt in the valve body (medium likelihood); Harness or connector at the gearbox: fluid wicking, corrosion, chafing (medium likelihood); Fluid level low or fluid contaminated (medium likelihood); Transmission control module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning lamp on; Limp mode with a fixed gear, harsh or missing shifts; Torque converter clutch stays open, higher fuel use. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P084A – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit
text: P084A: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch H Circuit. Transmission fluid pressure sensor/switch H is the last of up to eight pressure inputs (A to H) in SAE J2012; the letter is the maker's choice. Documented uses are rare: Mitsubishi sets P084A on its Jatco CVT8 (F1CJC/W1CJC) and Ford P084B on the 2020–23 Explorer 3.3 full hybrid. Mitsubishi uses P084A as a function check of the primary pulley pressure sensor: the module compares primary with secondary pressure and sets the code after 5 s outside the map at a steady ratio of 0.5 to 1.0. title: P084F – Park/Neutral Switch Output Circuit
text: P084F: Park/Neutral Switch Output Circuit. P084F concerns an output: a gearbox, hybrid or selector module passes the park/neutral status as a switched signal to other modules, for example for start release. The module watches its own driver for open circuits and shorts. Stellantis names the code for the 2019 Pacifica plug-in hybrid, where it came with a software fault that drained the 12 V battery; a hybrid control update fixes it. Saab's gearbox module reports the same kind of P/N output to the engine module under P081A/P081B. Strategy and MIL status are not published. Common causes: P/N output line or connector open or shorted (high likelihood); Module software misjudging the output (medium likelihood); Output driver in the module faulty (low likelihood); Receiving module pulls the line wrongly (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine or ready mode does not start in P/N; 12 V battery drains while parked; Warning about gear or park position. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0850 – Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit
text: P0850: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit. The park/neutral input tells the engine control module whether the automatic is in P or N, or a manual gearbox in neutral. It releases the starter, prepares idle control for the load of an engaged gear and enables cruise control and other monitors. All documented makers check it for plausibility against driving state or a second source such as the gearbox module. On GM's 6T70 and Subaru the switch pulls the line to ground in P/N. P0850 is the general fault. Ford's 2023 diesels check the switch for plausibility at start-up and set the code after 1 s. On GM's 6T70, as in the Saab 9-4X, the module sees P/N while the range switch reports a gear for 0.2 s above 10 km/h and 75 Nm, type C without MIL; it then uses the range switch for start release. title: P0851 – Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit Low
text: P0851: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit Low. The park/neutral input tells the engine control module whether the automatic is in P or N, or a manual gearbox in neutral. It releases the starter, prepares idle control for the load of an engaged gear and enables cruise control and other monitors. All documented makers check it for plausibility against driving state or a second source such as the gearbox module. On GM's 6T70 and Subaru the switch pulls the line to ground in P/N. P0851 means the input wrongly reports P/N while the car drives under load. Subaru's manual sets it when the neutral switch stays on while the car goes from idle at standstill to at least 64 km/h three times, MIL after two trips, cruise control blocked. GM's LML Duramax compares it with the gearbox module above 24 km/h and 120 Nm, type B; GM petrol engines use type C. Common causes: Inhibitor or neutral switch faulty or misadjusted, stays closed (high likelihood); Signal wire shorted to ground (medium likelihood); Selector cable misadjusted (medium likelihood); Gearbox module status wrong where it is the reference (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on (GM diesel, Subaru after two trips); Cruise control not working; Rough idle when stopping. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0856 – Traction Control Input Signal
text: P0856: Traction Control Input Signal. The traction control input carries the request of the ABS/stability module to the engine module to cut torque when wheels spin. Older cars used a wire with a voltage or duty-cycle signal, hence the low and high variants; today it is a CAN message, where pure loss of communication sets U0121 or U0415 instead. California's OBD rule counts traction control as a safety-only system that may be exempted, so these codes normally carry no MIL. GM checks the CAN torque request from the brake module: a wrong protection value or rolling count in 6 of 10 messages, or three changes of request type within 200 ms, set it, type C without MIL. On the Saab 9-4X the brake module then switches traction and stability control off for the key cycle and stores C0242. Common causes: Fault in the engine module that prevents torque reduction, often with other engine codes (high likelihood); Software of engine or brake module, module faulty (medium likelihood); CAN fault, connector or ground at the brake or engine module (medium likelihood); Low supply voltage (low likelihood). Symptoms: Traction or stability control lamp on, system switched off; No torque reduction when wheels spin; Usually no check engine lamp; C0242 or similar in the brake module. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P085A – Gear Shift Control Module B Communication Circuit
text: P085A: Gear Shift Control Module B Communication Circuit. Gear shift control modules A and B are selector modules of shift-by-wire systems, such as Audi's selector lever J587 or Stellantis' rotary shift module. The codes cover a dedicated link to the gearbox module and the module's plausibility. If the selected range cannot be transferred reliably, the gearbox holds its range, goes to P at standstill or into limp mode. Modules on CAN report lost communication as U0103 or invalid data as U0404 instead; GM uses its own codes. P085A is the general fault of the link to module B: no or no valid frames. No maker documents it; California's rule requires missing communication of digital inputs to be stored separately. Common causes: Wire or connector between selector module and gearbox module: open, chafed, moisture in the console (high likelihood); Power or ground of the selector module (medium likelihood); Software of selector or gearbox module (medium likelihood); Selector module faulty (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Selector or gearbox warning in the instrument cluster; Range cannot be selected or only with delay, car stays in P/N; Gearbox limp mode. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0863 – TCM Communication Circuit
text: P0863: TCM Communication Circuit. The TCM communication circuit is a direct link between gearbox and engine module outside the CAN bus. Subaru's 2005 WRX, sold as Saab 9-2X, uses a single 'AT diagnosis' wire: about once a second the gearbox module sends a frame with a start pulse of 40 ms low and 20 ms high, carrying among other things its request for the MIL. On CAN cars, loss of the gearbox module sets U0101 or U0402 instead. P0863 is the general fault of this link without telling range, low or high apart. No maker documents it on its own. Without the link the engine module receives no gearbox status, and a MIL request from the gearbox gets lost. Common causes: Wire or connector between engine and gearbox module open or corroded (high likelihood); Gearbox module without power or ground (medium likelihood); Gearbox module faulty (medium likelihood); Input of the engine module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine lamp on; Gearbox warning or limp mode possible; Gearbox faults not passed to the engine module. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0867 – Transmission Fluid Pressure
text: P0867: Transmission Fluid Pressure. P0867 to P0869 cover the system or line pressure of the gearbox as a whole: a pressure sensor measures it and the control module compares it with the pressure it commands. Faults of the sensor circuit itself have their own codes (Chrysler 68RFE P0932 ff), the single switches A to H have theirs (P0840 ff). Thresholds are not published; the codes are documented in bulletins for the Ram 68RFE and for the Tremec dual clutch of Corvette C8 and Maserati MC20. P0867 is the general pressure fault. GM's Corvette bulletin reads it as 'no system pressure': the pump delivers nothing or the fluid is almost gone, so valve cleaning is pointless and the gearbox needs a mechanical check. The car may lose drive completely. Common causes: Fluid level extremely low or leak (high likelihood); Fluid pump or its drive faulty (medium likelihood); Pressure regulator or relief valve sticking (medium likelihood); System pressure sensor faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission warning lamp or MIL on; Weak or no drive; Limp mode, car may be stranded. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0870 – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit
text: P0870: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch C Circuit. Transmission fluid pressure switches C and D report whether a clutch circuit is pressurised. Ford reports pressure faults under its solenoid codes. P0870 is the general fault. Allison's 2006 table uses it for the switch on valve S3: if it reports pressure for more than 20 ms with the valve at rest, the valve is retried twice and the case classed as electrical, mechanical or sporadic, type A. Ram corrected false P0870 'hydraulic pressure tests' on the 2019 68RFE with a software update. Common causes: Pressure switch C faulty (sticking, seal leaking) (high likelihood); Sticking shift valve or worn valve body bore (medium likelihood); Wiring or connector at the gearbox (medium likelihood); Control module software (Ram 68RFE) (low likelihood); Low fluid level (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL or transmission warning lamp on; Limp mode with a fixed gear; Harsh or missing shifts. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P087A – Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit
text: P087A: Clutch Position Sensor B Circuit. Clutch position sensor B reports the position of the second clutch or its actuator, the counterpart of sensor A (P0805 ff). The only documented user is Ford's dry DPS6 dual clutch in Fiesta and Focus: clutch B, for reverse and the even gears, is moved by a three-phase motor whose Hall sensors give its position, and the gearbox module drives it through an internal motor driver. Ford sets P087A for a fault in that internal driver; wiring faults of the motor have their own codes (P090A, P090C, P090D). Ford's warranty extension 19N07 covers replacing the gearbox module when it is the cause, which is common here. Clutch B can then no longer be controlled safely. Common causes: Gearbox module faulty internally (motor driver) (high likelihood); Water or corrosion at the gearbox module connector (medium likelihood); Clutch B motor or its wiring faulty (medium likelihood); Weak supply to the gearbox module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL or transmission warning on; Jerky take-off or shifts; Reverse or even gears missing, limp mode. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0880 – TCM Power Input Signal
text: P0880: TCM Power Input Signal. The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0880 is the general fault. Hyundai's 2017–19 six-speed automatics set it when the solenoid supply drops below 7 V or rises above 22 V: MIL on, limp mode in 4th gear. Hyundai's bulletin points to the valve body harness and the TCU fuses and expressly not to the gearbox. Common causes: Harness or connector between module and valve body damaged or corroded (high likelihood); TCU fuse or transmission relay faulty (medium likelihood); Weak battery, charging fault, poor ground (medium likelihood); Gearbox module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on; Limp mode in a fixed gear, no shifting; Harsh engagement into D or R. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0883 – TCM Power Input Signal High
text: P0883: TCM Power Input Signal High. The TCM power input codes watch the supply voltage of the gearbox module or of its solenoid supply. Without a proper supply all solenoids go dead and the gearbox falls back to its hydraulic emergency gear with maximum line pressure: a fixed gear, harsh engagement, no shifting. Ford's external gearbox modules check a window of 9 to 16 V; GM reports the same under P0562/P0563. P0883 means the supply is too high: Ford sets it above 16 V, continuously and with MIL; GM's counterpart P0563 sets at 18 V. Typical triggers are a failed alternator regulator or a jump start with 24 V. Overvoltage endangers the output stages, so the module may switch the solenoids off. Common causes: Alternator voltage regulator faulty (overcharging) (high likelihood); Jump start with 24 V or charger in boost mode (medium likelihood); Poor battery ground, regulator measures wrongly (medium likelihood); Module measurement faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on; Charging warning or unusually bright lights; Overvoltage codes in other modules. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0884 – TCM Power Input Signal Intermittent

title: P0885 – TCM Power Relay Control Circuit/Open
text: P0885: TCM Power Relay Control Circuit/Open. Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. title: P088A – Transmission Fluid Filter Deteriorated
text: P088A: Transmission Fluid Filter Deteriorated. Allison's 'Prognostics' in its fourth and fifth generation controls (1000 to 4000 series, buses and trucks, from 2009) has no fluid quality sensor: the gearbox module calculates. No car maker is known to use these codes. Its filter life monitor judges the pressure drop across the filter circuit; in Allison's patent a differential pressure valve operates a switch with temperature-dependent time limits. P088A, called 'filter maintenance alert' by Allison, is the early warning: the wrench symbol flashes. A faulty main valve body in some 3000/4000 units triggered it early (field action 2019FA07). After a filter change the monitor is reset by a selector sequence. Common causes: Filter change interval reached (high likelihood); Heavy contamination from clutch wear (medium likelihood); Filter changed without resetting the monitor (medium likelihood); Faulty main valve body (Allison serial range) (low likelihood). Symptoms: Wrench or TRANS SERVICE indicator flashing; Usually no change in driving behaviour. Repair difficulty: easy.

title: P088C – Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit Low
text: P088C: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit Low. The reverse inhibit solenoid on GM's six-speed manual gearboxes (Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V, ATS-V) blocks reverse while driving forward and is released by the engine module. A low-side driver with built-in diagnosis watches the control line: above 9 V and 250 rpm, 20 faults in 25 samples of 250 ms (about 6 s) set the code. GM rates it type C without MIL; from 2019 a service message appears. P0801 is the open circuit. P088C means the control line is shorted to ground, so the solenoid is energised unintentionally or can no longer be switched off. Common causes: Wire between engine module and gearbox chafed to ground (tunnel, near exhaust) (high likelihood); Solenoid coil shorted to ground (medium likelihood); Water or corrosion in the gearbox connector (medium likelihood); Engine module driver faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Reverse cannot be engaged or is no longer blocked; Service message (GM from 2019), no MIL. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P088E – Planetary Gear Set Failure
text: P088E: Planetary Gear Set Failure. P088E means the module has found that a planetary gear set no longer keeps the fixed speed relation between its sun, carrier and ring gear, for example through broken planet gears, seized planet pins or stripped teeth. No maker's table or bulletin documents the code. It suits power-split hybrid transmissions, which measure speeds at several members: a Toyota patent compares the road speed calculated from engine, generator speed and planetary ratio with the measured one, flags a deviation of about 10 km/h for about 1 s and then drives electrically only. In stepped automatics such damage usually shows as ratio or slip codes. Common causes: Planet gears or pins seized or broken (lubrication, overheating) (high likelihood); Tooth damage on sun or ring gear (medium likelihood); Speed sensor (engine, motor-generator, output) reading wrong (medium likelihood); Low or worn fluid (low likelihood). Symptoms: Grinding or whining from the gearbox; Power loss, limp mode (hybrids drive electrically only); Possibly no drive. Repair difficulty: hard.

text: P0890: TCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low. Some gearboxes draw their power through a relay, such as the transmission control relay in Chrysler's fuse box that feeds the solenoids. title: P0893 – Multiple Gears Engaged
text: P0893: Multiple Gears Engaged. P0893 means more shift elements are applied than the commanded gear allows, so the gearbox binds up. It is detected through speeds, when the ratio matches no valid gear and input speed collapses, or through commanded clutch capacities: a GM patent flags capacities above their limits for longer than roughly 200 to 500 ms and reacts by downshifting or falling back to the hydraulic limp mode. Nissan's 2020–22 Frontier and Titan nine-speed set it with all ratio codes and MIL; Land Rover cured P0893 on the ZF 9HP48 Evoque with gearbox software. Common causes: Gearbox module software or calibration (high likelihood); Shift or pressure valve sticking (dirt), control valve body faulty (medium likelihood); Clutch plates stuck or welded (low likelihood); Speed sensor false signal (low likelihood). Symptoms: Gearbox or engine warning lamp; Sudden limp mode, harsh jolts or judder; Strong braking or locking feeling during a shift. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0894 – Transmission Component Slipping
text: P0894: Transmission Component Slipping. P0894 reports slip of a gearbox component, found by comparing speeds. GM's 4L60-E applies it to the torque converter clutch: with lock-up commanded, slip between 100 and 550 rpm for 12.75 s on the third attempt in 4th gear sets it, type B with MIL after two trips; the module first freezes adaptation and raises line pressure. Lexus (Aisin AB60F) and Allison 1000 use it for a slipping shift element or low pressure and name the fluid level first. On the 4L60-E a cracked converter clutch PWM solenoid is a known cause. Common causes: Low, wrong or worn fluid (high likelihood); Converter clutch PWM solenoid cracked or regulator bore worn (GM 4L60-E) (high likelihood); Worn clutch plates or converter clutch lining (medium likelihood); Pump not priming, cracked suction filter (Allison) (medium likelihood); Control module software (low likelihood). Symptoms: Engine speed rises without matching acceleration, mostly when warm; Shudder during lock-up; Harsh shifts from maximum pressure, limp mode possible. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0895 – Shift Time Too Short
text: P0895: Shift Time Too Short. Shift time is the duration of the speed transition from the old to the new ratio, measured from input and output speed. Gearbox modules adapt fill time and pressure to keep it in a calibrated window; the code sets when adaptation is at its limit and the time is still outside. No maker could be found using these generic codes; Saab's 1994 900 automatic monitored the same with its own code P1832, a window of 0.3 to 1.3 s and a limp program. P0895 means the shift completes faster than the window: clutch pressure too high or applied too early, giving a harsh shift. Common causes: Pressure control valve stuck towards high pressure or line pressure too high (high likelihood); Shift adaptation faulty or reset, wrong software (medium likelihood); Valve body: sticking spool, faulty damper or accumulator (medium likelihood); Wrong fluid or level (low likelihood). Symptoms: Harsh, jerky shifts; Transmission warning lamp; Limp mode possible. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0898 – Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit Low
text: P0898: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit Low. The MIL request circuit is a dedicated wire over which the gearbox module asks the engine module to switch on the MIL. Today that request travels over CAN and shows as P0700 in the engine module; older Subarus, also sold as Saab 9-2X, used a single serial wire with its own codes P0864 to P0866. P0898 means the request wire stays at ground: a short to ground or, with active-high logic, a gearbox module without power. The engine module can then not tell a real request from a wiring fault. No maker documents the code; Subaru's P0865 is the closest documented equivalent. Common causes: MIL request wire shorted to ground (high likelihood); Engine or gearbox module connector corroded (medium likelihood); Gearbox module output faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on; Gearbox faults may not be indicated correctly. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P089A – Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit
text: P089A: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 2 Circuit. Gear lever position sensor 2 is the redundant second sensor of an electronic selector lever, next to sensor 1 (P0821 ff), for the X or Y axis. The only documented user is GM's electronic range selection with PWM Hall sensors, as in the Cadillac XT4, and only for range, low and high. Following GM's patent, an invalid sensor is dropped and the other carries on; with both invalid the module can request park. P089A, the general circuit fault of X sensor 2, is used by no maker found; GM reports circuit faults through duty-cycle low or high and frequency errors under P089B. Common causes: Wire or connector at the selector module open (high likelihood); Sensor 2 in the selector faulty (medium likelihood); Spilled liquid in the centre console (low likelihood). Symptoms: Gearbox or selector warning in the cluster; Range selection delayed or limited; Usually still drivable, sensor 1 takes over. Repair difficulty: medium.
