title: P0942 – Hydraulic Pressure Unit
text: P0942: Hydraulic Pressure Unit. General fault of the unit that generates and stores hydraulic pressure for an automated gearbox or its auxiliary oil supply: motor-driven pump, accumulator and pressure control. Toyota sets P0942 on the 2001 to 2005 MR2 Spyder sequential gearbox together with the SMT warning light and a buzzing pump, or with gears that can no longer be changed; fluid seeping from the reservoir cap or the seal of the hydraulic power unit is a known cause, fixed with new seal rings. Ferrari reads P0942 on its DCT differently, as system pressure command signal too low. CARB requires functional checks of transmission outputs. P0943 and P0944 are the cycling and pressure-loss faults, P0945 to P0948 the pump control circuit. Common causes: Fluid loss at the reservoir cap or hydraulic power unit seals (high likelihood); Worn pump motor or faulty pump relay (medium likelihood); Damaged wiring, connectors or power supply of the pump (medium likelihood); Transmission control module fault (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission or gearbox warning light on; Pump buzzing or running for long periods; Gears cannot be changed or shifts are delayed; Auto stop-start disabled or engine restarts immediately. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0943 – Hydraulic Pressure Unit Cycling Period Too Short
text: P0943: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Cycling Period Too Short. In a hydraulic pressure unit the pump charges an accumulator up to a cut-out pressure and switches off until pressure falls to the cut-in point. By J2012 wording this code means the pump switches on again too soon, so the interval between charging cycles is shorter than expected. Typical reasons are internal leakage across valves or seals, or an accumulator that has lost its gas precharge and stores too little oil. Audi patents describe such accumulator and leakage checks based on charging switch-over times and pressure decay. No manufacturer documents this exact meaning publicly; Ferrari uses P0943 on its DCT for a system pressure command signal that is too high. CARB requires functional checks of transmission outputs. P0942 is the general fault, P0944 the loss of pressure. Common causes: Accumulator has lost its gas precharge (high likelihood); Internal leakage at valves, seals or actuator cylinders (high likelihood); Faulty pressure switch or pressure sensor giving wrong cut-in point (medium likelihood); Low or aerated hydraulic fluid (low likelihood). Symptoms: Pump can be heard switching on unusually often; Warning light on; Slower or harsher gear changes. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0944 – Hydraulic Pressure Unit Loss of Pressure
text: P0944: Hydraulic Pressure Unit Loss of Pressure. The pump runs but the expected hydraulic pressure does not build or collapses. Stellantis names it Loss of Hydraulic Pump Prime: a 2023 STAR case lists it with P0868 and a slow engagement after the vehicle has stood, both set as the only transmission codes with the MIL on, and the fix was a new transmission; an FCA defect file from 2015 also shows it beside line pressure low. Mercedes uses P0944 on the 722.9 automatic with electric auxiliary oil pump for stop-start, as internal fault of that pump; stop-start stops working, and a leaking check valve between converter housing and pump is one cause. Ferrari reads it on its DCT as no system pressure signal with pressure loss. P0943 covers short cycles, P0868 low fluid pressure. Common causes: Pump loses prime (air drawn in through filter, seal or strainer pipe) (high likelihood); Blocked oil strainer or suction tube (medium likelihood); Worn or failed pump (mechanical or electric) (medium likelihood); Leaking check valve or internal leak in the valve body (low likelihood). Symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on; Slow engagement after the vehicle has been parked; Auto stop-start not available or engine restarts at once; Slipping, no drive or limp mode. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0945 – Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit/Open
text: P0945: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit/Open. The control module drives the motor of the hydraulic pump through a relay or a direct output. This code reports a general circuit fault or an open in that control path, so the pump cannot be switched reliably. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The layout is shown by a ZF patent for an automated gearbox, in which a motor-driven pump draws oil from a reservoir and charges a pressure accumulator behind a one-way valve, with shut-off valves feeding the shift cylinders. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission outputs. P0946 is the plausibility fault, P0947 and P0948 low and high; P094E covers the pump supply instead of the control side. Without the pump the gearbox soon runs out of pressure. Common causes: Pump relay coil open or relay not seated (high likelihood); Open control wire or loose terminal between module and relay (medium likelihood); Failed output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light on; Pump does not run, pressure is not built; Gears cannot be changed or auto stop-start disabled. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0946 – Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0946: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit Range/Performance. The pump control circuit is electrically intact, but its behaviour does not match the command, for example a pump that keeps running after being switched off, or one that switches but is not followed by the expected feedback. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. In the hydraulic unit of an automated gearbox, as shown in a ZF patent, the pump only has to run until the accumulator is charged; a relay that sticks or switches late upsets that cycle. CARB requires functional checks on transmission outputs. P0945 is the general circuit or open fault, P0947 and P0948 the low and high faults, P094B a pump stuck on regardless of the relay. A pump that never stops drains the battery and wears quickly. Common causes: Relay contacts welded or sticking (high likelihood); Pump supply or control wire shorted to battery voltage (medium likelihood); Faulty pump state feedback or control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Pump keeps running after switch-off; Warning light on; Auto stop-start not available; Battery discharged after parking. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0947 – Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit Low
text: P0947: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit Low. The voltage on the control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver is lower than the module expects for the commanded state. Usually the line is shorted to ground or the relay coil is shorted, so the output may be overloaded and the pump runs when it should not, or the driver shuts down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The hydraulic unit it belongs to, a motor-driven pump that charges an accumulator for the shift and clutch cylinders of an automated gearbox, is described in a ZF patent. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission outputs. P0948 is the high counterpart, P0945 the open fault, P0946 plausibility. Pressure supply for shifting may fail. Common causes: Relay control wire chafed and shorted to ground (high likelihood); Shorted relay coil (medium likelihood); Damaged output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light on; Pump runs continuously or not at all; Gearbox in limp mode or stop-start disabled. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0948 – Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit High
text: P0948: Hydraulic Pump Relay/Control Circuit High. The control line of the hydraulic pump relay or driver shows a higher voltage than expected, typically because it is shorted to battery voltage or the relay coil is open on a low-side driver. The pump then cannot be switched on, or the module sees it as active when it is not. J2012 places this code with the pump control circuit; Ferrari however reads P0948 on its DCT as no signal from the system pressure output, an unrelated use. The pump and accumulator unit of an automated gearbox is described in a ZF patent. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission outputs. P0947 is the low counterpart, P0945 the open fault and P0946 the plausibility fault. Expect a warning and possible loss of pump pressure. Common causes: Relay control wire shorted to battery voltage (high likelihood); Open relay coil seen as high level by the driver (medium likelihood); Control module fault (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light on; Pump does not start; Gear changes not possible or stop-start disabled. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0949 – Auto Shift Manual Adaptive Learning Not Complete
text: P0949: Auto Shift Manual Adaptive Learning Not Complete. Status code for an automatically shifted manual gearbox: the control unit has not yet finished learning its adaptation values, above all the clutch touch point and the end positions of the shift actuators. Such learning runs after a new control unit, clutch or actuator, after a software update and sometimes after the battery was disconnected; Hyundai and Kia patents show how the touch point is found and corrected from shaft speed changes. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The code is a reminder rather than a hardware fault; launch and shifts may be jerky until learning is done. P0950 to P0954 cover the manual control circuit, P0806 to P0808 the clutch position sensor. MIL use depends on the maker. Common causes: Relearn not run after clutch, actuator or control unit replacement (high likelihood); Adaptation values erased by software update or battery disconnection (medium likelihood); Learning aborted by low voltage or worn clutch outside the learn window (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Jerky launch or rough shifts; Gearbox warning or message to perform teach-in; Restricted gear selection until learning completes. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P094A – Hydraulic Pump Driver Performance
text: P094A: Hydraulic Pump Driver Performance. Concerns the electronic driver that powers the motor of a hydraulic or electric oil pump, often a separate pump controller. The driver reports, or the module infers, that it cannot deliver the commanded speed or current although the circuit is not open or shorted. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Hyundai shows what such a driver monitors on its wet 8-speed DCT pumps: overcurrent, current and Hall sensor faults and internal faults, filed under its own P193D and P1C2E codes. Mercedes reports an internal fault of the 722.9 auxiliary oil pump under P0944 instead. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094B and P094C are stuck pump faults, P094D overheating, P094E supply; P0C29 is the equivalent for auxiliary fluid pumps of automatics. Common causes: Internal fault of the pump controller or driver stage (high likelihood); Pump motor drawing excess current (worn bearings, fluid in motor) (medium likelihood); High resistance in supply or ground of the driver (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light on; Auto stop-start disabled; Delayed engagement or slower shifts. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P094B – Hydraulic Pump Stuck On
text: P094B: Hydraulic Pump Stuck On. The hydraulic pump keeps running although the module has switched it off, or it never reaches its cut-out point. Causes are a welded relay or shorted driver, or a pump that cannot reach cut-out pressure because of leakage. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. In the pump and accumulator unit of an automated gearbox, described in a ZF patent, the pump should rest once the accumulator is charged. Toyota links a constantly buzzing pump on the MR2 sequential gearbox to fluid loss at the hydraulic power unit, reported under P0942. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094C is the opposite fault, P0946 the relay plausibility fault, P0943 the too-short cycle. Battery drain and pump wear follow. Common causes: Pump relay contacts welded closed (high likelihood); Leakage or lost accumulator charge keeps pressure below cut-out (medium likelihood); Shorted driver stage or supply wire shorted to battery voltage (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Pump audible after the vehicle is switched off; Discharged battery; Warning light on. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P094C – Hydraulic Pump Performance/Stuck Off
text: P094C: Hydraulic Pump Performance/Stuck Off. The pump is commanded on but does not deliver: it does not turn, turns too slowly or produces too little pressure. The module judges this from pressure or speed feedback. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Mercedes reports a comparable condition of the electric auxiliary oil pump on the 722.9 automatic under P0944; its test plan checks connector and fuse, supply voltage, CAN lines and software, then a check valve in the converter housing, before the pump is replaced. Hyundai lists a stuck high-flow pump on its 8-speed DCT as P193E71. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094B is the opposite fault, P094A the driver, P0944 the pressure loss of the whole unit. Common causes: Air in the pump after service or a suction leak (high likelihood); Seized or failed pump motor (medium likelihood); Blocked strainer or leaking check valve (medium likelihood); Supply or relay fault stopping the pump (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light on; Engine restarts at once or stop-start not available; Delayed engagement or lost drive. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P094D – Hydraulic Pump Over Temperature
text: P094D: Hydraulic Pump Over Temperature. The hydraulic or electric oil pump, or its integrated controller, has become too hot. The temperature is usually measured on the controller board and the pump is derated or switched off to protect it. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Hyundai lists the same condition for the high-flow pump of its wet 8-speed DCT as P193D4B, over temperature, and P1C2E92 for the high-pressure pump motor control. Kia recalled stop-start oil pump controllers in 2023 because a damaged capacitor could short and overheat the board, harness and connector. CARB requires functional checks on outputs. P094A is the driver fault, P094B a pump that never stops, a common reason for heat build-up. Common causes: Pump running too long because of leakage or a stuck relay (high likelihood); Defective pump controller board (medium likelihood); Very hot transmission fluid or blocked cooling (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light on; Stop-start temporarily disabled; Burning smell near the pump in severe cases. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P094E – Hydraulic Pump Supply Voltage Circuit/Open
text: P094E: Hydraulic Pump Supply Voltage Circuit/Open. Fault in the power feed of the hydraulic or electric oil pump: fuse, supply wire, connector or relay output. The module sees missing or implausible supply at the pump or its controller. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Mercedes shows the checks that belong to it on the electric auxiliary oil pump of the 722.9 automatic, although it reports that pump under P0944: connector and fuse first, then supply voltage and CAN lines. Hyundai lists an open circuit of its DCT high-flow pump as P193D13. CARB requires circuit checks on outputs. P0945 to P0948 concern the control side, P094A the driver, P0562 general low system voltage. Without supply the pump stops and stop-start is usually blocked. Common causes: Blown pump fuse (high likelihood); Open or corroded supply wire or connector (medium likelihood); Weak battery or poor main ground lowering pump supply voltage (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light on; Pump does not run; Stop-start disabled or gearbox in limp mode. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0950 – Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit
text: P0950: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit. General electrical fault in the circuit that carries the driver's manual up and down requests to the transmission control, as used by tip-shift gates on automatics and by automated manual gearboxes. A Chrysler patent shows the classic design: a transverse gate beside the drive positions with a proximity switch that signals upshift on one side and downshift on the other. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. The module typically checks the switch signals for states that cannot occur. P0951 to P0954 are the range, low, high and intermittent faults, P0955 onward the mode select circuit. Usually manual shifting is disabled while normal automatic driving remains available; MIL use varies. Common causes: Failed up/down switch or sensor in the selector lever or paddles (high likelihood); Damaged wiring or corroded connector at the shifter (e.g. after spilled liquid) (medium likelihood); Clockspring or steering column wiring fault on paddle-shift vehicles (low likelihood). Symptoms: Manual or tip shifting does not respond; Gear display or warning message; Automatic mode still works normally. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0951 – Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0951: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Range/Performance. Plausibility fault in the circuit that reports the driver's manual upshift and downshift requests, typically the tip gate of an automatic selector lever or steering wheel paddles. The signal is electrically valid but makes no sense, for example both requests active together or a request held far longer than any tap. A Volkswagen patent explains that the Hall elements in such tip gates are hard to diagnose and proposes checking all sensors and lines while the lever sits in P or R. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0950 is the general circuit fault, P0952 to P0954 the low, high and intermittent faults. Usually only manual shifting is disabled. Common causes: Sticking or worn up/down tip switch, request signal stays active (high likelihood); Displaced magnet or damaged Hall sensor board in the selector lever (medium likelihood); Spilled liquid or dirt in the shifter causing cross-talk between contacts (medium likelihood); Faulty input stage in the transmission or shifter control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Tip shifting or paddles do not respond or respond erratically; Unwanted gear changes in manual mode; Warning message, automatic mode keeps working. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0952 – Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Low
text: P0952: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Low. The control unit sees the voltage on the manual up/down request circuit below its expected window, typically a signal wire shorted to ground or a switch stuck in the grounded state. In many tip gates the moving contact switches to ground, as a Nissan patent shows, so a short to ground can mimic a permanently held request; a Volkswagen patent describes checking the Hall tip sensors for shorts and breaks while the lever is in P or R. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0953 is the high counterpart, P0950 the general and P0951 the plausibility fault. In practice manual shifting is locked out while D keeps shifting automatically. Common causes: Signal wire of the up/down circuit chafed through and shorted to ground (high likelihood); Tip switch stuck in the closed position (medium likelihood); Moisture or spilled drink in the shifter creating a leakage path to ground (medium likelihood); Low supply voltage to a Hall-type tip sensor (low likelihood). Symptoms: Manual tip shifting inoperative; Gear indicator shows no manual gear or a warning message; Normal automatic driving in D still possible. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0953 – Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit High
text: P0953: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit High. Voltage on the manual up/down request circuit lies above its expected window. Common reasons are a signal wire shorted to battery voltage or, where the input is pulled up internally, a broken wire or a switch that never closes. A Volkswagen patent names a short to plus and a line break as faults its tip-gate diagnosis detects with the lever in P or R; a Chrysler patent shows the classic AutoStick-style gate with one switch for up and one for down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0952 covers the low side, P0954 dropouts, P0950 the general fault. Manual shifting is usually disabled, automatic mode remains. Common causes: Signal wire shorted to a voltage-carrying wire in the shifter harness (high likelihood); Broken wire or unplugged connector on a pulled-up input (medium likelihood); Missing ground of the tip switch or Hall sensor (medium likelihood); Faulty input stage in the transmission control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Tip gate or paddles have no effect; Warning or message about manual mode; Automatic shifting continues normally. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0954 – Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Intermittent
text: P0954: Auto Shift Manual Control Circuit Intermittent. The manual up/down request signal drops out or flickers for short moments, so a single tap may arrive twice, late or not at all. Unlike P0952 and P0953 the voltage is not stuck outside its window; it jumps between states without a matching lever movement. Typical triggers are loose pins in the shifter connector, worn contacts or a harness that flexes with the lever. A Chrysler patent shows how simple contact switches in the gate signal each request, a Volkswagen patent how Hall tip sensors and their lines are checked. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks. P0950 is the general fault. The driver notices missed or doubled manual shifts. Common causes: Loose or spread pins in the selector lever connector (high likelihood); Harness broken internally where it moves with the lever or steering column (medium likelihood); Worn or oxidised tip switch contacts (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Manual shifts occasionally ignored or executed twice; Fault comes and goes, often over bumps; Manual mode temporarily switched off. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0955 – Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit
text: P0955: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit. Fault in the circuit that tells the transmission control whether the driver has moved the selector lever from D into the manual gate. A Nissan patent shows a dedicated manual mode switch with two contacts on separate inputs, so a break or a short to ground can be told apart; a Hyundai patent uses a microswitch on the lever. Genesis bulletins for 2017-18 G80 and G90 automatics list Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit for the cable-shift version, with a check engine light and a part from the shift lever group as repair, though the table prints the code as P0995 and P095500. So at least Hyundai uses ASM for the manual mode of a torque converter automatic. P0956 to P0959 are the detailed variants, P0950 the up/down request circuit. Common causes: Failed manual mode switch or microswitch in the selector lever (high likelihood); Corroded or loose connector at the selector lever assembly (medium likelihood); Damaged wiring between selector lever and transmission control module (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Manual mode cannot be selected or is not displayed; Check engine or transmission warning light on; Driving in D remains possible. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0956 – Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0956: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Range/Performance. The manual mode signal is electrically valid but contradicts other information, for example manual mode reported while the range sensor reads P, R or N, or the mode switch never changing although the up/down requests arrive. A Hyundai patent uses a microswitch with two opposing contacts and treats identical or missing signals on both inputs as a defect; a Nissan patent likewise compares two contacts of the manual mode switch. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly, and Hyundai's mode circuit fault is only documented as the general code P0955. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P0957 to P0959 cover low, high and intermittent faults. Manual mode is usually blocked. Common causes: Mode switch or its actuating foot misaligned on the lever (high likelihood); Worn switch contacts giving contradictory states on both inputs (medium likelihood); Transmission range sensor out of adjustment, disagrees with the mode signal (medium likelihood); Worn selector lever bushings allowing side play (low likelihood). Symptoms: Manual mode drops out or will not engage; Display shows manual mode while lever is in D, or the reverse; Warning lamp depending on manufacturer. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0957 – Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Low
text: P0957: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Low. Voltage in the manual mode circuit, the signal that reports the selector lever in the manual gate, is below the expected range. Mostly the signal line has a short to ground or the switch contact hangs in its grounded position. A Nissan patent describes a manual mode switch whose moving contact is grounded and explains how the control unit spots a contact shorted to earth from its two inputs. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; Hyundai's mode circuit fault appears in Genesis bulletins only as the general code. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0958 is the high counterpart, P0955 the general and P0956 the plausibility fault. Expect manual mode to be unavailable or stuck on. Common causes: Mode signal wire chafed and shorted to ground (high likelihood); Mode switch stuck in the grounded position (medium likelihood); Liquid or dirt in the selector lever housing (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Manual mode not available or permanently indicated; Warning lamp depending on manufacturer; Automatic driving in D unaffected. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0958 – Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit High
text: P0958: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit High. The manual mode signal from the selector lever reads above its expected range. Possible causes are a short to supply voltage or, with an internally pulled-up input, an open circuit or missing switch ground that keeps the line high. A Nissan patent explains how two separately wired contacts let the control unit recognise a break in the manual mode switch, and a Hyundai patent shows the lever microswitch that reports the change from D to M. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; Hyundai's mode fault is only documented as P0955. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P0957 is the low side, P0959 the intermittent variant. Usually the gearbox stays in automatic mode. Common causes: Broken mode signal wire or disconnected shifter plug (high likelihood); Missing ground at the mode switch (medium likelihood); Mode signal shorted to a voltage-carrying wire (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Manual gate has no effect, gearbox stays in automatic mode; Warning lamp depending on manufacturer; No manual gear shown on the display. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0959 – Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Intermittent
text: P0959: Auto Shift Manual Mode Circuit Intermittent. The signal reporting the selector lever in the manual gate drops out or toggles briefly while the lever is not moved, so the transmission control switches between manual and automatic mode on its own. The voltage is not stuck out of range as with P0957 or P0958 but jumps. Loose connector pins at the lever, a harness that flexes with the shifter or a worn microswitch are typical. A Hyundai patent shows such a microswitch actuated by the lever's sideways movement, a Nissan patent the two-contact mode switch. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; CARB requires circuit checks. P0955 is the general fault, P0954 the intermittent fault of the up/down circuit. Common causes: Loose pins in the selector lever connector (high likelihood); Worn or bouncing mode microswitch (medium likelihood); Harness damaged where it moves with the lever (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Manual mode switches on or off by itself; Gear display flickers between D and manual gear; Fault often appears on rough roads. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P095A – Gear Shift Position Circuit C
text: P095A: Gear Shift Position Circuit C. Circuit C is a third channel reporting the shift position inside an automated manual gearbox, for example a further sensor track or a sensor on another shift rail or selector shaft. This general circuit code sets on an electrical fault of that signal that fits none of the more specific C variants. No manufacturer documents the code publicly, and which sensor carries the letter C depends on the design. A Nissan/Aichi patent describes shift stroke sensors as the feedback for engaging gears, an Aisin AI patent the fallback when a stroke sensor fails. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P095B to P095D are the C siblings, P0914 and P091A the same signal on circuits A and B. Shifting may be restricted. Common causes: Loose or corroded connector at shift position sensor C (high likelihood); Damaged signal, supply or ground wire of sensor circuit C (medium likelihood); Faulty shift position sensor C (medium likelihood); Faulty sensor input in the transmission control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on; Slower or restricted gear changes in fallback mode; Gearbox may hold a gear or stay in neutral. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P095B – Gear Shift Position Circuit C Range/Performance
text: P095B: Gear Shift Position Circuit C Range/Performance. Plausibility fault of the shift position signal on circuit C of an automated manual gearbox. The voltage is electrically acceptable, but the value does not fit: it contradicts the other position channels, stays put while the shift actuator moves, or misses the learned gear positions. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent points out that sensor mountings on shift parts can give way under vibration and distort the reading; an Aisin AI patent explains how control carries on when a stroke sensor can no longer be trusted. CARB requires rationality checks on such inputs. P095A, P095C and P095D are the electrical faults of circuit C, P0915 and P091B the same check on A and B. Common causes: Worn or drifting shift position sensor C disagreeing with the other channels (high likelihood); Bent sensor bracket or displaced magnet on the shift rail (medium likelihood); Gear positions not relearned after actuator or module replacement (medium likelihood); Increased contact resistance in the sensor circuit (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission warning light on; Harsh or aborted gear changes; Fallback mode with fewer available gears. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P095C – Gear Shift Position Circuit C Low
text: P095C: Gear Shift Position Circuit C Low. The signal of shift position sensor C in an automated manual gearbox lies below its permitted voltage window. Typical reasons are a signal wire shorted to ground, a lost sensor supply or a sensor with an internal fault pulling its output down. Because the value is physically impossible, the control unit can flag it quickly without comparing it to other channels. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent shows shift stroke sensors as the position feedback for gear engagement, an Aisin AI patent the fallback strategy when such a sensor drops out. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P095D is the high counterpart, P095A the general and P095B the plausibility fault; P0916 and P091C are the low faults of A and B. Common causes: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to ground (high likelihood); Open or shorted 5 V supply of the sensor (medium likelihood); Internally failed shift position sensor C (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on; Fallback mode with restricted gears; Gearbox may refuse to leave neutral. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P095D – Gear Shift Position Circuit C High
text: P095D: Gear Shift Position Circuit C High. Shift position sensor C of an automated manual gearbox delivers a voltage above its permitted window. This usually points to a signal wire shorted to the supply, a broken sensor ground or, with a pulled-up input, an interrupted signal line. Since no real shift position produces such a value, the module can set the code without cross-checking other channels. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. A Nissan/Aichi patent describes shift stroke sensors as feedback for gear engagement, an Aisin AI patent how control continues when one of them fails. CARB requires circuit checks on such inputs. P095C is the low counterpart, P095A the general and P095B the plausibility fault; P0917 and P091D are the high faults of A and B. Common causes: Signal wire of sensor C shorted to the 5 V supply or battery voltage (high likelihood); Open ground circuit of the sensor (medium likelihood); Internally failed shift position sensor C (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission or engine warning light on; Fallback mode with restricted gears; Jerky or aborted gear changes. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0960 – Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open
text: P0960: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open. Open-circuit fault in the driver circuit of pressure control solenoid A: the module measures an impedance far above the coil value, as if a wire, pin or winding were broken. Which solenoid carries the letter A depends on the gearbox. Ford uses it for the line pressure (EPC) solenoid; GM's 8-speed for clutch 1 (CB1278R), the 9- and 10-speeds for clutch CB123456(R), Allison 1000 for main modulation (line) pressure and GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the odd-clutch valve. GM flags more than 200 kOhm for 0.3 s (Type A), Allison 173 kOhm or more after an intrusive test. GM six-speeds report an open under P0963 instead. Low and high are P0962/P0963, performance P0961. Expect maximum line pressure, harsh shifts or a fixed limp gear. Common causes: Open solenoid coil inside the valve body or solenoid assembly (high likelihood); Loose, corroded or pushed-back pin at the transmission connector or pass-through (medium likelihood); Broken wire between module and solenoid (medium likelihood); Faulty output stage in the transmission control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Transmission warning or MIL on, fault message in the cluster; Very firm or harsh shifts due to maximum line pressure; Transmission stays in a fixed limp gear. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0961 – Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0961: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance. Performance fault of pressure control solenoid A: the circuit is electrically intact, but the solenoid does not behave as commanded. On GM's six-speeds, where A is the line pressure solenoid, the Saab 9-4X 6T70 sets it when measured and commanded current differ for 5 s, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s; both Type B, two trips. Allison 1000 flags a current error of 0.5 A or more in 40 of 80 samples (Type A). Ford's 2023 diesel summary lists it as a PC A current range fault. In GM's CVT, A feeds the secondary pulley: a pressure error above 500 kPa steady or 1,500 kPa transient, confirmed by a ratio error, sets it after 5 s. Electrical faults are P0960, P0962 and P0963. The module usually commands maximum line pressure and freezes adaptations. Common causes: Solenoid with internal electrical or mechanical fault, current no longer follows the command (high likelihood); Debris or varnish in the fluid sticking the solenoid or regulator valve (medium likelihood); High resistance at connector or pass-through distorting the current (medium likelihood); Low fluid level causing pressure errors (CVT pulley monitor) (low likelihood). Symptoms: Harsh or erratic shifts; MIL or transmission warning after the second drive; Slipping or ratio flare on CVT applications. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0962 – Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
text: P0962: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit Low. Pressure control solenoid A circuit low: the driver sees a short to ground. Ford tests its line pressure (EPC) solenoid this way; a short there opens a high-side switch that cuts power to the shift solenoids and leaves park, reverse, neutral and one fixed forward gear at maximum line pressure. On GM's six-speeds and the Saab 9-4X 6T70, A is the line pressure solenoid; the fault matures in 1.5 to 2 s and is Type A, with reverse and 5th gear only, no converter lock-up and maximum line pressure. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use A for a clutch solenoid and treat less than 0.5 ohm as a short, Allison 1000 for main modulation pressure (125 ms). Siblings: P0960 open, P0963 high, P0961 performance. Common causes: Control wire chafed through and touching ground (high likelihood); Internally shorted solenoid coil (medium likelihood); Transmission fluid or water in the connector bridging pins (medium likelihood); Faulty output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and transmission warning on immediately; Limp mode with only one forward gear and reverse; Harsh engagements, poor acceleration from standstill. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0963 – Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit High
text: P0963: Pressure Control Solenoid A Control Circuit High. Pressure control solenoid A circuit high: the driver detects a short to voltage, and on GM's six-speeds also an open circuit, since those units have no separate open code. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (line pressure solenoid) sets it after 5 s as Type B, GM's 2018 table after 4.4 of 5 s over two trips; the module then commands maximum line pressure and freezes adaptations. Ford tests its line pressure (EPC) solenoid for short to power and, in some applications, keeps P0963 like P0960 without MIL because maximum line pressure does not raise emissions. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds and Allison 1000 (power short within 75 ms) use A for a clutch or main modulation solenoid. Expect firm, harsh shifts rather than slipping. Siblings: P0960, P0961, P0962. Common causes: Open coil or high-resistance connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds) (high likelihood); Control wire shorted to a supply voltage (medium likelihood); Damaged or contaminated connector at the transmission (medium likelihood); Faulty output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Firm or harsh shifts at maximum line pressure; Warning light, on some vehicles only after two drives or not at all; Shift adaptation no longer improves. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0964 – Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit/Open
text: P0964: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit/Open. Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid B. What B controls differs by gearbox: GM's 8-speed uses it for clutch 2 (CB12345R), the 9-speed for CB29 and the 10-speed for CB128910R, Allison 1000 for pressure control solenoid 2, and GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the even-clutch pressure valve. GM sets it at more than 200 kOhm for 0.3 s (Type A, one trip), Allison at 173 kOhm or more after an intrusive test, the dual-clutch unit after 150 ms. GM six-speeds do not use P0964; an open in their 3-5-reverse solenoid shows up as P0967. Ford's OBD summaries list no B or C codes. Depending on the clutch involved, gears are lost or the unit drops into a fixed limp gear. Siblings: P0965, P0966, P0967. Common causes: Open solenoid coil (high likelihood); Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness (medium likelihood); Broken control wire (medium likelihood); Faulty output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and transmission warning on; Certain gears missing or limp mode; Dual-clutch gearbox drives on one sub-gearbox only. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0965 – Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0965: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance. Performance fault of pressure control solenoid B: wiring is intact, but current or resulting pressure does not match the command. In the Saab 9-4X 6T70, solenoid 2 feeds the 3-5-reverse clutch; a current mismatch for 5 s sets a Type C code without MIL and freezes that clutch's adaptations, and GM's 2016 six-speed table also lists it without MIL. Allison 1000 checks for a current error of 0.5 A or more within 250 ms windows (Type A). In GM's CVT, B controls the primary pulley: a pressure error above 500 kPa steady or 1,500 kPa transient, confirmed by a ratio error for 5 s, sets a Type A code. Electrical faults of B are P0964, P0966 and P0967. Symptoms range from none to rough 3rd, 5th or reverse, or CVT ratio problems. Common causes: Worn or internally faulty solenoid, current no longer matches the command (high likelihood); Debris sticking the solenoid or its regulator valve (medium likelihood); Internal leak in the CVT primary pulley circuit (medium likelihood); High resistance in connector or pass-through (low likelihood). Symptoms: Rough or delayed 3rd, 5th or reverse engagement; CVT ratio fluctuates, engine speed flares; Often no warning light on six-speed applications. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0966 – Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Low
text: P0966: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit Low. Pressure control solenoid B circuit low, meaning a short to ground in the driver circuit. On GM's six-speeds and the Saab 9-4X 6T70, B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch; a short lasting 0.3 s (GM 2018 table) or 1 s (Saab) sets a Type A code with a fixed limp mode: reverse and 5th gear, maximum line pressure, converter clutch off. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use B for a clutch solenoid and treat less than 0.5 ohm as a short; Allison 1000 uses it for pressure control solenoid 2 with ground-short detection in 125 ms. Ford does not use the B codes. Siblings are P0964 open, P0967 high and P0965 performance; solenoids A and C follow the same scheme. Common causes: Chafed control wire touching ground (high likelihood); Internally shorted solenoid in the valve body assembly (medium likelihood); Fluid or moisture in the connector (medium likelihood); Faulty output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on immediately; Limp mode with reverse and one forward gear; No torque converter lock-up, higher fuel consumption. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0967 – Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit High
text: P0967: Pressure Control Solenoid B Control Circuit High. Pressure control solenoid B circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, since they have no P0964. For the Saab 9-4X 6T70, where B is clutch pressure solenoid 2 for the 3-5-reverse clutch, the module needs 1 s, stores a Type A code and limits the transmission to reverse and 3rd gear at maximum line pressure; GM's 2018 six-speed table uses 0.3 s and one trip. GM's 8-speed (clutch 2), the 9- and 10-speeds, Allison 1000 (power short within 75 ms) and GM's dual-clutch gearbox (even-clutch valve) report the same fault on their solenoid B. Ford does not use it. Siblings: P0964 open, P0966 low, P0965 performance. Repairs usually involve the solenoid body or valve body module. Common causes: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds) (high likelihood); Control wire shorted to a supply voltage (medium likelihood); Damaged or contaminated transmission connector (medium likelihood); Faulty output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, limp mode in a fixed gear; Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure; Dual-clutch gearbox loses the even gears. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0968 – Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open
text: P0968: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open. Open circuit in the driver of pressure control solenoid C. GM's 8-speed assigns C to clutch 3 (C13567), the 9-speed to CB38 and the 10-speed to C23457910; an impedance above 200 kOhm for 0.3 s counts as open and sets a Type A code after one trip. In GM's dual-clutch gearbox, C is the redundant shutdown valve of the odd clutch, checked for open load while its output is switched off and confirmed after 150 ms. GM six-speeds report an open C solenoid as P0971, and neither Ford's summaries nor the Allison 1000 tables list C codes. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission output components. Low and high are P0970/P0971, performance P0969; the usual result is a lost gear range or limp mode. Common causes: Open solenoid coil (high likelihood); Poor contact at the transmission connector or internal harness (medium likelihood); Broken control wire (medium likelihood); Faulty output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and transmission warning on; Gears that need clutch C are unavailable; Limp mode in a fixed gear. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0969 – Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0969: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance. Performance fault of pressure control solenoid C. Publicly documented only for GM's front-drive six-speeds: on the Saab 9-4X 6T70, clutch pressure solenoid 3 feeds the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches through the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve. If measured current differs from the commanded current for 5 s, the module stores a Type C code and freezes the adaptations of both clutches. GM's 2016 table (C456/CBR1 solenoid) sets it after an invalid feedback for 4.4 of 5 s, also without MIL. Other GM users such as the 8- to 10-speeds list only open, low and high for C, and Ford does not use C. Drivers rarely notice more than gradually rougher 4-5-6 or reverse engagements. Electrical faults: P0968, P0970, P0971. Common causes: Solenoid 3 with internal fault, current no longer matches the command (high likelihood); Debris sticking the solenoid or the R1/4-5-6 regulator valve (medium likelihood); High resistance in the internal connection to the module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Usually no warning light; Rougher shifts into 4th, 5th, 6th or reverse over time; Shift adaptation stops learning. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0970 – Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
text: P0970: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit Low. Pressure control solenoid C circuit low, a short to ground in the driver. On GM's six-speeds C is the C456/CBR1 solenoid; on the Saab 9-4X 6T70 it is clutch pressure solenoid 3 for the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches. A short for 1 s (Saab) or 0.3 s (GM 2018 table) sets a Type A code: only reverse and 5th gear, no converter lock-up, maximum line pressure. GM's 8-speed uses C for clutch 3 (C13567), the 9- and 10-speeds for CB38 or C23457910 with less than 0.5 ohm counting as a short; GM's dual-clutch gearbox uses it for the odd-clutch shutdown valve. Siblings: P0968 open, P0971 high, P0969 performance. Since the solenoid sits in the valve body, repairs often mean the control solenoid valve assembly. Common causes: Internally shorted solenoid in the control solenoid valve assembly (high likelihood); Chafed control wire touching ground (medium likelihood); Fluid or moisture in the connector (medium likelihood); Faulty output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on immediately; Limp mode in reverse and one forward gear; Weak acceleration from standstill. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0971 – Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit High
text: P0971: Pressure Control Solenoid C Control Circuit High. Pressure control solenoid C circuit high: a short to voltage, and on GM six-speeds also an open, as there is no separate open code there. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 (clutch pressure solenoid 3, low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutches) and GM's 2018 six-speed table set it after 1 s or 0.3 s as Type A, with limp mode in reverse and 5th gear at maximum line pressure. GM's 8-, 9- and 10-speeds use the code for their clutch solenoid C; GM's dual-clutch gearbox for the redundant odd-clutch shutdown valve, where too high a voltage at the sense pin with the output switched on counts as a short. Ford does not use C codes. Siblings: P0968 open, P0970 low, P0969 performance. A loose connector can make the fault come and go. Common causes: Open coil or poor connection (reported as high on GM six-speeds) (high likelihood); Control wire shorted to a supply voltage (medium likelihood); Damaged or loose transmission connector (medium likelihood); Faulty output stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, limp mode in a fixed gear; Harsh engagements at maximum line pressure; Fault comes and goes with temperature or vibration. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0972 – Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0972: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Range/Performance. Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A: the circuit is not plainly shorted, yet its electrical behaviour does not fit what the module commands. Today's large makers rarely use the code. GM's 2007 table for the Allison 1000 six-speed used it for an open SS1 circuit: after three hardware fault samples the module opens the low-side driver as an intrusive test and reports P0972 if four more samples show no short to ground (400 ms, Type A, MIL at once). Newer GM Allison tables move that open to P097A. Ferrari's DCT bulletin reuses P0972 for a missing signal from the actuator 1 engage position sensor, not a solenoid. Ford and GM six-speeds report opens elsewhere. Shorts are P0973/P0974. Common causes: Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid A (Allison-type usage) (high likelihood); Loose or corroded terminal at the transmission connector or internal harness (medium likelihood); Chafed or broken wire between module and solenoid (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL or transmission warning on; Transmission falls back to a fixed default gear; Missing or abrupt shifts. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0973 – Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Low
text: P0973: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit Low. Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A, usually a short to ground. Ford lists it as SSA short to ground beside P0750 (open) for the 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140, checked by a driver feedback line within 0.5 to 5 s. GM six-speeds (6L/6T) call SS A the mode 2 solenoid and set P0973 after 1.2 of 1.5 s, MIL after one trip. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 needs 2 s, Type A, then only reverse and 5th remain. GM's 2016 Allison 1000 table folds ground short (0.42 ohm or less) and open (200 kOhm or more) into this code over 10 counts. Saab's Aisin gearbox in the 9-5 (2010) maps it to shift solenoid valve 2. High side is P0974. Common causes: Control wire to solenoid A chafed through and shorted to ground (high likelihood); Internal short in solenoid A or the control solenoid assembly (medium likelihood); Fluid or metal debris bridging pins at the transmission connector (medium likelihood); Faulty low-side driver in the transmission or powertrain module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on after the first faulty trip on many vehicles; Limp mode with only a few gears, often reverse plus one forward gear; Harsh engagements due to maximum line pressure; Torque converter lockup and manual shifting disabled. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0974 – Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit High
text: P0974: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit High. High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid A. What it covers depends on the maker. Ford reserves it for a short to power on SSA, because an open SSA circuit sets P0750. GM six-speeds put both an open and a power short of the mode 2 solenoid here: 1.2 of 1.5 s, MIL only after two trips. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 waits 2 s, Type B, and then blocks 1st gear. GM's Allison 1000 tables of 2016 and 2023 treat it as a pure power short (0.39 ohm or less, 3 samples, 75 or 60 ms) and report opens separately. Saab's Aisin gearbox in the 9-5 (2010) sets it when solenoid valve 2 reads off while commanded on, 100 ms five times, Type A. Ground-side faults are P0973. Common causes: Open coil or broken wire where the maker reports opens under the high code (GM six-speed) (high likelihood); Control wire shorted to a supply voltage (medium likelihood); Spread or corroded pins at the transmission connector (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, on GM six-speeds only after a second faulty trip; First gear locked out, start-off in a higher gear; Missing or wrong shifts, possibly limp mode. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0975 – Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0975: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Range/Performance. Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Three documented uses differ widely. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS2 circuit, confirmed by an intrusive low-side test (400 ms, Type A). FCA's 2016 recall for the 9-speed front-drive transaxle (Cherokee, 200, Renegade, 500X, ProMaster City) names P0975 with P0978, P0981 and P0984 as the codes set by intermittent high resistance from poorly crimped terminals in the range sensor harness under old TCM software; updated software reports that case as P0901 instead. Ferrari's DCT uses P0975 for a missing actuator 2 position signal. Low/high are P0976/P0977. Common causes: Poorly crimped terminals causing intermittent high resistance (FCA 9-speed recall) (high likelihood); Open or high-resistance coil of shift solenoid B (medium likelihood); Outdated transmission software that misreads harness resistance (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL or transmission warning on; Unexpected shift to neutral or loss of drive (FCA 9-speed); Fixed default gear or harsh shifts. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0976 – Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Low
text: P0976: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit Low. Low-voltage fault, normally a ground short, in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. On GM six-speeds SS B is the mode 3 multiplex valve; the 2016 table sets P0976 after 1.2 of 1.5 s without lighting the MIL, while the Saab 9-4X 6T70 version needs 2 s, is Type B and raises line pressure. Ford uses it for SSB short to ground, with P0755 for an open; on the 2023 Super Duty diesel SSB is fed by solenoid supply TSPC2, so a P2669 supply fault disables this check. GM's Allison 1000 merges ground short and open into it in 2016, but from 2022 reports opens as P097B and keeps P0976 for ground faults found by an intrusive test (120 ms, MIL after one trip). High side is P0977. Common causes: Solenoid B control wire shorted to ground or housing (high likelihood); Internal short in solenoid B or its valve body assembly (medium likelihood); Moisture or debris bridging pins at the connector (medium likelihood); Faulty driver in the transmission control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light or stored code, on some GM six-speeds without MIL; Firm shifts due to raised line pressure; Gears missing or limp mode. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0977 – Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit High
text: P0977: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit High. High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid B. GM six-speeds put an open or a power short of the mode 3 multiplex valve here, 1.2 of 1.5 s; the 2016 table sets it without MIL, the 2019 table with MIL after one trip. The Saab 9-4X 6T70 treats it more severely than P0976: 2 s, Type A, high-side driver off, only reverse and 5th gear left, no converter lockup. Ford uses it strictly for SSB short to power, as in its 2012 and later summaries. GM's Allison 1000 checks for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three samples (75 ms in 2016, 60 ms in 2023). FCA 9-speed and Aisin uses are not documented for this code. Ground-side faults are P0976. Common causes: Open solenoid B coil or wire on GM six-speeds, where opens report as high (high likelihood); Control wire shorted to battery or a switched supply (medium likelihood); Damaged pins or seals at the transmission pass-through connector (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Limp mode with only reverse and one high forward gear; Weak acceleration from rest; MIL or transmission warning, depending on calibration. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0978 – Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0978: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Range/Performance. Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM's 2007 Allison 1000 table used it for an open SS3 circuit, but only while the commanded gear is not reverse trim, 5th or 6th; the table even prints the label Circuit Low beside an open-circuit test, an apparent typo. FCA lists P0978 among the four codes that the 2014–2016 9-speed transaxle set under old software when the range sensor harness had poor crimps. Ferrari's DCT bulletin uses it for a missing signal from the actuator 4 engage position sensor. Ford and GM six-speeds do not use it. Low/high are P0979/P0980, the current open code P097C. Symptoms: MIL or transmission warning on; Sudden neutral or default gear while driving; Erratic or missing shifts. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0979 – Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Low
text: P0979: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit Low. Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid C. GM uses it mainly on the Allison 1000 six-speed of its heavy pickups and chassis cabs: in 2016 a ground short of 0.22 ohm or less, stricter than the 0.42 ohm for SS1 and SS2, or an open of 200 kOhm or more counts after 10 samples (250 ms, Type A). From 2022 the open moves to P097C and P0979 needs an intrusive low-side test (120 ms, MIL after one trip). The Allison PS3 pressure switch test (P0872) also points to P0979 when its fault is electrical. Ford uses it for SSC short to ground beside P0760 open; on 6R80 and 6F, SSC drives the CB26 clutch. High side is P0980. Common causes: Solenoid C control wire shorted to ground (high likelihood); Internal short of solenoid C inside the valve body (medium likelihood); Open coil on GM 2016 Allison calibrations, which report opens under this code (medium likelihood); Faulty low-side driver in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on after the first faulty trip; Transmission holds a default gear; Rough or delayed shifts involving the affected clutch. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P097A – Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open
text: P097A: Shift Solenoid A Control Circuit/Open. Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid A, a code that later J2012 editions added; older lists still show P097A as reserved. GM is the only maker found that documents it: the 2022 to 2025 tables for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its heavy-duty trucks call it Shift Solenoid 1 Control Circuit Open. After one hardware fault the module flags pending, and after three samples it opens the low-side driver as a test; three more open readings at 9 to 18 V set the code (120 ms, MIL after one trip). The same gearbox once used P0972 for this and P0973 in 2016. Ford reports an open SSA as P0750, GM six-speeds as P0974, and Genesis folds all electrical faults of A into P0753. Common causes: Open coil of shift solenoid 1/A (high likelihood); Unplugged, corroded or pushed-out pin at the transmission connector (high likelihood); Broken wire in the internal or external transmission harness (medium likelihood); Faulty low-side driver in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on after one faulty trip; Transmission in a fixed default gear; Shifts involving solenoid A missing. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P097B – Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit/Open
text: P097B: Shift Solenoid B Control Circuit/Open. Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid B. Public use is again limited to GM's Allison 1000 six-speed in heavy-duty trucks, where the 2022 to 2025 tables label it Shift Solenoid 2 Control Circuit Open. SS2 shares high-side driver 2 with SS1 and SS3, so the open test only runs while that supply is on and free of P2669, P2670 or P2671. It confirms an open by switching the low-side driver off and needs three samples, 120 ms, MIL after one trip. Allison's 2007 table filed the same check as P0975, the 2016 table under P0976. Ford reports an open SSB as P0755, GM six-speeds as P0977. Low/high are P0976/P0977. Common causes: Open coil of shift solenoid 2/B (high likelihood); Loose or corroded terminal on the solenoid B circuit (high likelihood); Wire broken by vibration or heat near the transmission (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on after one faulty trip; Default gear operation, some ranges unavailable; Harsh or missing shifts. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P097C – Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open
text: P097C: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit/Open. Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid C. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed in its 2022 to 2025 heavy-duty tables as Shift Solenoid 3 Control Circuit Open, with the same intrusive low-side test as SS1 and SS2: three samples, 120 ms, battery 9 to 18 V, MIL after one trip. It is the youngest of three codes for this one fault on that gearbox: 2007 used P0978, only outside reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear, 2016 merged it into P0979 with a 200 kOhm limit. Ford reports an open SSC under P0760, and no other maker was found using P097C. A related pressure switch code may set too, because SS3 strokes the S3 valve that switch PS3 watches. Common causes: Open coil of shift solenoid 3/C (high likelihood); Loose, wet or corroded pin in the transmission connector (high likelihood); Broken wire between module and solenoid C (medium likelihood); Faulty low-side driver in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on after one faulty trip; Upper gears unavailable or fixed default gear; Possible additional pressure switch code. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P097D – Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit/Open
text: P097D: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit/Open. Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. No maker documents this code publicly. GM's Allison tables that use P097A to P097C stop at shift solenoid 3, and Ford, which has a solenoid D in its 5R110W, 6R80, 6F and 6R140 gearboxes, reports an open SSD under the base code P0765, with P0982/P0983 for ground and power shorts. Any use would follow the CARB rule that every transmission output must be checked for lack of circuit continuity, plus the pattern of the A to C codes: a high-impedance reading confirmed by switching the driver. On Ford's 6R80 and 6F, SSD feeds either CBLR or C456 through a multiplex valve, so an open there would disturb first and upper gears alike. Common causes: Open coil of shift solenoid D (high likelihood); Disconnected or corroded terminal in the solenoid D circuit (medium likelihood); Broken wire in the transmission harness (medium likelihood); Faulty driver in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light or MIL on; Missing gears that depend on solenoid D; Limp mode in a fixed gear. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P097E – Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit/Open
text: P097E: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit/Open. Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid E. No manufacturer was found that documents this code. Ford, the main user of an SSE, still reports an open SSE under P0770; its 2023 diesel summary pairs that with P0985 for ground and P0986 for power shorts, and powers SSE from supply TSPC1 together with SSA and SSC. In the 6R80 and 6F, SSE is an on/off solenoid that switches the multiplexing of SSD, while the 6R140 uses a variable force SSE for clutch C456. Without a public owner the code rests on the CARB demand for circuit continuity checks on transmission outputs and on GM's A to C pattern. Opens in shared supply wiring usually set P0657 first. Common causes: Open coil of shift solenoid E (high likelihood); Poor contact at the solenoid E terminal or lead frame (medium likelihood); Broken signal wire to solenoid E (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light or MIL on; Gears using solenoid E unavailable; Default gear operation. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P097F – Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit/Open
text: P097F: Shift Solenoid F Control Circuit/Open. Open-circuit fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid F. It is the only code in its family for letter F, since J2012 has no range/performance, low or high codes for F in this block. No maker was found to document it. Hyundai's Genesis bulletin for the eight-speed (2017–2018 G80 and G90) shows how F is handled in practice: an electrical fault of shift control solenoid F (labelled 8LR) is reported under P2709 and fixed by replacing the solenoid. Other makers with six or more clutches use their own codes. A P097F would follow the CARB requirement to test every transmission output for circuit continuity, by analogy with GM's open tests for solenoids 1 to 3. Common causes: Open coil of shift solenoid F (high likelihood); Loose or corroded terminal at the valve body connector (medium likelihood); Broken wire between module and solenoid F (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light or MIL on; Gears that need solenoid F unavailable; Limp mode. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0980 – Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit High
text: P0980: Shift Solenoid C Control Circuit High. High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid C, meaning a short to supply. GM documents it for the Allison 1000 six-speed: the 2007 table wants four consecutive power-short samples (100 ms, Type A) and skips the check in reverse trim, 5th and 6th gear; later tables (2016, 2018) look for 0.39 ohm or less to a supply over three counts within 75 ms, and from 2022 within 60 ms, MIL after one trip. Ford uses it for SSC short to power in all its listed gearboxes, with P0760 for an open. Neither GM's 6L/6T six-speeds nor Saab's documented gearboxes use P0980. The ground counterpart is P0979, the open code for the Allison is P097C. Common causes: Solenoid C control wire shorted to a supply voltage (high likelihood); Shorted turns in solenoid C lowering its resistance (medium likelihood); Adjacent pins bridged by fluid or debris in the connector (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on after the first faulty trip; Solenoid C stuck energized, wrong gear or default gear; Harsh shifts. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0981 – Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0981: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Range/Performance. Range/performance fault in the drive circuit of shift solenoid D. GM's Allison tables end at solenoid C, and Ford checks SSD only with P0765, P0982 and P0983, so the large North American users skip it. Two codegenau sources exist. FCA's recall S55 (NHTSA 16V-529) covers about 323,400 vehicles with the 9-speed front-drive transaxle; with old TCM software, intermittent high resistance from weak crimps in the range sensor harness could set P0981 or its siblings, and the remedy is new software plus, if a code is present, a new harness. Ferrari's DCT bulletin uses P0981 for a missing signal from the actuator 3 position sensor. Low/high for D are P0982/P0983. Common causes: Weak terminal crimps causing intermittent resistance (FCA recall S55) (high likelihood); Transmission software not yet updated by the recall (medium likelihood); Solenoid D coil resistance out of range (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Unexpected shift to neutral while driving (FCA 9-speed); MIL or transmission warning on; Default gear or harsh shifts. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0982 – Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Low
text: P0982: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit Low. Low-voltage fault, in practice a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford is the documented user: its summaries list SSD with P0765 open, P0982 short to ground and P0983 short to power, checked continuously through the driver feedback within 0.5 to 5 s. Which clutch this hits depends on the gearbox. In the 6R80 and 6F, SSD is a variable force solenoid feeding CBLR or C456 via the SSE multiplex valve; in the 6R140 it drives CBLR alone. In the 2023 diesel summary SSD is fed from supply TSPC2 with SSB, the converter clutch and line pressure solenoid. GM's six-speed and Allison tables do not use P0982. Ferrari reuses it for an actuator 3 sensor reading too low. Common causes: Solenoid D control wire shorted to ground (high likelihood); Internal short in solenoid D or the main control assembly (medium likelihood); Damaged internal lead frame or connector inside the transmission (medium likelihood); Faulty driver in the powertrain or transmission module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on and default gear operation; No engine braking in first or no reverse, depending on gearbox; Harsh shifts into upper gears. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0983 – Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit High
text: P0983: Shift Solenoid D Control Circuit High. High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid D. Ford defines it narrowly as SSD short to power; the open circuit stays with P0765. On the 6R140 the solenoid outputs are run by a smart driver chip (ADLER) that does the open and short checks itself, while older units use a feedback line from the output stage; both need 0.5 to 5 s. Since SSD on Ford six-speeds controls the low/reverse clutch, either alone or through the multiplex valve, a constant power short can apply that clutch at the wrong time. The 2020–2023 gasoline summary keeps the same assignment. GM documents no P0983 for its geared automatics, and Ferrari uses it for an actuator 3 sensor reading too high. Ground faults are P0982. Common causes: Solenoid D control wire shorted to a supply (high likelihood); Solenoid D with shorted windings (medium likelihood); Conductive contamination between neighbouring pins (medium likelihood); Faulty smart driver or output stage in the module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, default gear; Clunk or tie-up feel if the low/reverse clutch applies unintentionally; Upper gears blocked. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0985 – Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Low
text: P0985: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit Low. Low-voltage fault, usually a short to ground, in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. title: P0986 – Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit High
text: P0986: Shift Solenoid E Control Circuit High. High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid E. Ford means a short to power on SSE; an open sets P0770 and a ground short P0985. On the 6R140 SSE is a variable force solenoid for the C456 clutch, so a short to power can hold that clutch on. Saab's 2010 9-5 with the Aisin six-speed instead assigns P0986 to shift solenoid valve 1 and sets it when the circuit reads off although it is commanded on, which also catches an open coil: 100 ms, five times, Type A, all solenoids then switched off. GM's published transmission tables do not use the code. Because makers split opens differently, check the maker's table before replacing parts. Common causes: Solenoid E control wire shorted to a supply voltage (high likelihood); Open coil or wire where the maker reads it as high (Saab/Aisin) (medium likelihood); Bent or corroded terminals at the solenoid E connector (medium likelihood); Faulty driver stage in the control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, transmission in fail-safe gear; Tie-up or harsh shift if the controlled clutch stays applied; Adaptation frozen, shift quality worsens. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0987 – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit
text: P0987: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit. General circuit fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The only public user of switch E found, GM's 6T70/6T75 family (Saab 9-4X: switch 5 on the low/reverse and 4-5-6 clutch regulator valve), reports only P0989 and P0990 for it, both as plausibility counts. P0987 is the slot for a module that sees a generic circuit fault on a fifth pressure sensor or switch, for example an open or out-of-range signal, without separating low from high. CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs. Range/performance is P0988, low and high are P0989/P0990; switches A to D use P0840 to P0878. Typical effects are frozen shift adaptations and harsher shifts. Common causes: Failed pressure sensor or switch E (high likelihood); Open or shorted signal wire or poor connector contact (medium likelihood); Faulty input stage in the transmission control module (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light depending on manufacturer; Harsher or less consistent shifts; Possible limp mode. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0988 – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0988: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Range/Performance. Range/performance fault of transmission fluid pressure sensor or switch E: the signal is electrically valid but does not fit the commanded clutch state or the pressure expected from other inputs. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's 6T70/6T75 family, the one public user of switch E (switch 5 on the low/reverse and 4-5-6 regulator valve), folds such plausibility checks into P0989 and P0990; its switch logic table shows which gears should pressurise the switch. Sonnax describes how these normally closed film switches in the valve body module fail through debris or delaminated films. CARB requires rationality checks of transmission inputs. Siblings: P0987 circuit, P0989 low, P0990 high. Common causes: Damaged or delaminated switch film, switch reacts late or not at all (high likelihood); Debris in the fluid holding the switch or its regulator valve (medium likelihood); Low fluid level or real pressure deviation in the clutch circuit (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Often no noticeable symptom at first; Shift quality worsens because adaptation stops; Warning light depending on manufacturer. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0989 – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low
text: P0989: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Low. Pressure switch E reads low, meaning no pressure, when it should show pressure. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; the normally closed switch sees pressure while both the low/reverse and the 4-5-6 clutch are released. The module counts clutch releases after which the signal stays low, checked with commanded clutch pressure at 50 kPa or less: 18 counts in GM's 2011 tables and on the Saab 9-4X, 17 in the 2016 table. It is a Type C or Special No Trip code without MIL, and the adaptations of both clutches are frozen. Sonnax lists P0989 among typical switch failures in this valve body module. P0990 is the stuck-high counterpart; switches A to D use P0840 to P0878. Common causes: Damaged or delaminated film in switch 5 of the valve body module (high likelihood); Debris keeping pressure away from the switch (medium likelihood); R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve sticking (medium likelihood); Low fluid level (low likelihood). Symptoms: No warning light, code stored only; Shifts into 4th to 6th or reverse gradually less smooth; Occasional limp mode if the fault persists. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0990 – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit High
text: P0990: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit High. Pressure switch E reads high, meaning pressure, when it should be vented. GM's 6T70/6T75 family uses E for switch 5 on the R1/4-5-6 clutch regulator valve; applying the low/reverse or 4-5-6 clutch moves that valve and should exhaust the switch. If the signal stays high after such an apply, with commanded clutch pressure at 700 kPa or more, the module counts it: 15 counts on the Saab 9-4X, 30 in GM's 2016 table. It is a Type C or Special No Trip code, so no MIL, and the adaptations of both clutches are frozen. According to Saab, normal debris in the fluid can set it intermittently without noticeable symptoms. A short to voltage on the signal wire has the same effect. P0989 is the stuck-low case. Common causes: Switch 5 stuck open by a damaged film or debris (high likelihood); R1/4-5-6 regulator valve not moving, switch stays pressurised (medium likelihood); Signal circuit shorted to voltage or open inside the module (low likelihood). Symptoms: No warning light, code stored only; Intermittent occurrence without noticeable symptoms; Shift quality declines over time. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0991 – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Intermittent
text: P0991: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch E Circuit Intermittent. The module has seen the signal of the fifth transmission pressure sensor or switch drop out or jump briefly, without a steady low or high reading. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. The only switch E found in public sources is GM's TFP switch 5 in the 6T70/6T75 valve body module (Saab 9-4X 2011), a normally closed switch that GM monitors only through P0989 and P0990: signal stuck low at commanded pressure of 50 kPa or less, or stuck high, counted over clutch releases and logged as Special No Trip without MIL. An intermittent check would follow the CARB rule that transmission inputs be monitored for circuit faults. Steady faults are P0987 to P0990. Expect frozen shift adaptation and the odd harsh shift. Common causes: Loose or corroded contact at the valve body module connector (high likelihood); Debris or damaged diaphragm film making the switch contact flicker (medium likelihood); Chafed internal harness that shorts or opens under vibration (medium likelihood); Fault in the transmission control module input stage (low likelihood). Symptoms: Stored fault, often without warning light; Occasional harsh or flared shift; Shift adaptation frozen. Repair difficulty: hard.

title: P0992 – Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit
text: P0992: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor/Switch F Circuit. General circuit fault of a sixth transmission pressure sensor or switch, labelled F. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and no gearbox with a switch F was found. GM's six-speeds stop at TFP switch 5 (letter E, P0989/P0990), and Mitsubishi's 2019 six-speed monitors its 2-6 brake, high clutch and low-reverse brake switches under P0846, P0876 and P0988, which are letters B, D and E. Pressure switches like these sit in the valve body module and tell the module which clutch is applied; Sonnax describes them as normally closed film-and-piston switches. P0992 would be the code for an open or implausible circuit without a low/high split, as CARB requires circuit checks on transmission inputs. Range/performance, low, high and intermittent are P0993 to P0996. Common causes: Open or damaged signal wire or connector to the switch (high likelihood); Pressure switch or sensor failed inside the valve body module (medium likelihood); Transmission control module input fault (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning light depending on manufacturer calibration; Harsh or delayed shifts; Possible limp mode with a fixed gear. Repair difficulty: hard.
