title: P0B37 – High Voltage Service Disconnect Open
text: P0B37: High Voltage Service Disconnect Open. P0B37 means the controller sees the service disconnect as open, either because the plug is really removed or because its detection loop is broken. Ford uses the code in the battery energy control module of the 2013-2016 C-Max Energi: bulletins SSM 46108 and TSB 17-0015 describe intermittent stalls or no crank with a Stop Safely Now message and MIL, stored with U3012 and, in another module, the interlock code P0A0A. The cause was an intermittent short to ground in the low-voltage interlock wiring, found by inspecting the harness for chafing. P0B33 to P0B36 cover circuit, performance, low and high faults. For the driver: the car shuts down or will not start. Common causes: Low-voltage interlock wiring chafed with intermittent short to ground (Ford C-Max) (high likelihood); Service disconnect plug removed, loose or not locked (medium likelihood); Open terminal in the plug base or interlock connector (medium likelihood); Battery energy control module fault (low likelihood). Symptoms: Intermittent stall or no crank; Stop Safely Now message and MIL; High-voltage interlock code stored in another module. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B38 – Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
text: P0B38: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit/Open. Hybrid and electric drives cool the inverter and motor electronics with electric coolant pumps; J2012 numbers them A, B and C. P0B38 sets when the controller detects an open or general fault in the control line of pump B, typically by checking the driver output for missing load current. No manufacturer documents P0B38 publicly. FCA uses a pump B on the Jeep Compass and Renegade 4xe, where bulletins name its performance code P0C74, and Mercedes uses the pump A code P0A05 for an open control circuit of the low-temperature circuit pump on M264 engines. CARB requires output components of inverter thermal management to be monitored. Expect a coolant or hybrid warning and power reduction if electronics overheat. Common causes: Pump connector loose, corroded or terminal pushed out (high likelihood); Open control wire between controller and pump (medium likelihood); Pump electronics or motor failed open (medium likelihood); Driver stage in the controlling module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: Hybrid system or coolant warning, MIL on; Reduced electric drive power when electronics get hot; Pump not running audibly after switch-on. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0B39 – Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
text: P0B39: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low. P0B39 sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B is lower than the controller expects, usually a short to ground on the command line or a pump input that pulls the line down. On a low-side switched or PWM line the module sees the voltage stuck low while it commands the pump off. No manufacturer documents P0B39 publicly. Pump B is in service at FCA (Compass and Renegade 4xe, performance code P0C74), and Ford stores the pump A codes P0A06 and P0A07 in the PCM of the 2020 Explorer and Aviator hybrids. CARB requires these inverter cooling outputs to be checked for circuit faults. Open and high faults are P0B38 and P0B3A; running faults use P0C74 and P2D05 ff. Common causes: Control wire shorted to ground, often chafed at brackets (high likelihood); Pump electronics pulling the control input low (medium likelihood); Coolant or water in the pump connector (medium likelihood); Driver stage in the controlling module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning; Pump runs permanently or not at all, depending on circuit design; Power limitation at high load or heat. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0B3A – Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High
text: P0B3A: Motor Electronics Coolant Pump B Control Circuit High. P0B3A sets when the control signal of motor electronics coolant pump B stays higher than expected, typically a short to battery voltage on the command line or, with some driver designs, an open pump input that floats high. The module then cannot switch the pump as requested. No manufacturer documents P0B3A publicly. As reference points, FCA has a pump B on its 4xe models with the performance code P0C74, and Ford lists the pump A high code P0A07 among PCM codes fixed by a battery controller update on the 2020 Explorer and Aviator hybrids. CARB requires inverter thermal management outputs to be monitored. Open and low faults are P0B38 and P0B39. Overheating protection may reduce power. Common causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage (high likelihood); Pump control input open so the line floats high (medium likelihood); Controller software misjudging the circuit, fixed by update (low likelihood); Driver stage in the controlling module faulty (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and hybrid or coolant warning; Pump cannot be switched off or on as commanded; Reduced electric power when the inverter heats up. Repair difficulty: medium.

title: P0B3B – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit
text: P0B3B: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit. Voltage sense A to Z and beyond are the cell or cell-group sense channels of the battery monitoring electronics, unlike the pack voltage sense codes P0ABA and P0B14 ff, which measure the whole pack. P0B3B is the circuit code for channel A. GM uses it in the battery energy control module as an open sense line check: neighbouring cell readings differ by 1.3 V or more, or a cell reads under 36 mV with balancing on, or a splice reads over 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V), for 0.6 s; Type A, one trip. Ford stores P0B3B with other open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV and 2023 Mach-E; Honda's 2014-2015 Accord Hybrid used it for a cell voltage sensor fault caused by inverter noise. Common causes: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack (high likelihood); Intermittent fault in the flexible printed circuit to the battery controller (Ford Mach-E) (medium likelihood); Sensor software misreading inverter noise, fixed by update (Honda) (medium likelihood); Internal failure of the traction battery requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV) (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL or powertrain warning, Stop Safely Now message possible; No start or no charging; Fail-safe EV mode with limited speed and sudden loss of power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B3C – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B3C: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Range/Performance. P0B3C flags a cell voltage channel A that reads plausible values but does not follow the other cells. GM runs this check in Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 as a stuck-in-range test: while the average cell voltage moves by at least 0.005 V in one direction between samples, channel A must move as well; 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip. FCA names the code Voltage Sense 1 Circuit Performance on the Chrysler Pacifica plug-in hybrid and fixes it, together with P0B41 and further channels, by reprogramming the battery pack control module. Circuit, low, high and erratic faults have their own codes. The system limits battery power or shuts down hybrid operation. Common causes: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica) (high likelihood); Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics (medium likelihood); High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection (medium likelihood); Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes; Reduced electric range or no electric drive; Contactor related codes stored at the same time. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B3D – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low
text: P0B3D: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low. P0B3D sets when cell voltage channel A reads below the lowest value a real cell can have, which points to the measurement rather than the cell. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, provided no open sense line, communication or balancing fault is active. FCA lists P0B3D as Hybrid Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Low on the 2019 Ram 1500 with eTorque mild hybrid, next to the pack-level code P0ABA, and cures it with a battery pack control module update. A genuinely low cell is reported with separate cell voltage codes. Expect reduced or blocked hybrid assist. Common causes: Battery pack control module software, fixed by update (Ram eTorque) (high likelihood); Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative (medium likelihood); Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on; Start-stop and electric assist unavailable; Hybrid battery power limited. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B3E – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit High
text: P0B3E: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit High. P0B3E sets when cell voltage channel A reads above any value a healthy lithium-ion cell reaches, so the reading is treated as a sensing fault. GM sets it in the battery energy control module when cell voltage A is 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip. FCA uses the code on the 2021 Jeep Wrangler 4xe as Voltage Sense 1 Circuit High and on the 2019 Ram 1500 eTorque as Voltage Sense A Circuit High; in both cases a battery pack control module update removes a false MIL. A truly overcharged cell sets separate cell voltage high codes such as P0DE7 instead. Low, range and open faults are P0B3D, P0B3C and P0B3B. The car limits battery use. Common causes: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA) (high likelihood); Open sense line letting the input float high (medium likelihood); Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, possibly without noticeable drivability change; Electric drive or start-stop disabled; Charging limited. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B3F – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B3F: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B3F is reserved for a cell voltage channel A that jumps or drops out briefly instead of failing steadily. No manufacturer documents P0B3F publicly. GM's 2019 tables show how the siblings on the same channel work: an open line test (P0B3B), a stuck-in-range test against the other cells (P0B3C) and fixed limits of 0.2 V and 4.8 V (P0B3D, P0B3E); an erratic test would watch for implausible jumps between samples. CARB requires battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system to be monitored as input components, with fault codes pinpointing the smallest replaceable unit. Loose connections at the cell taps or the monitoring board are the usual suspects. Hybrid power may be limited. Common causes: Loose or cracked cell tap connection (high likelihood); Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector (medium likelihood); Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines (medium likelihood). Symptoms: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes; Occasional loss of electric drive or assist. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B40 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit
text: P0B40: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit. P0B40 is the circuit code of cell voltage sense channel B, the second cell or cell group the battery monitoring electronics measures; pack-level voltage uses P0ABA and P0B14 ff instead. GM applies the same open sense line test as on channel A: a 1.3 V jump between neighbouring cells, under 36 mV with balancing on, or splice voltage above 0.1 V (bus bar 0.5 V) for 0.6 s, Type A, one trip. Ford lists P0B40 among the open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV, where the fix is a new traction battery, and on the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and e-Transit, where an intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller is to blame. Expect no start or no charging. Common causes: Open cell sense line, splice or bus bar connection inside the pack (high likelihood); Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable in the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, e-Transit) (medium likelihood); Internal traction battery failure requiring replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV) (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Wrench indicator or MIL, Stop Safely Now message possible; No start condition; Battery cannot be charged. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B41 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B41: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Range/Performance. P0B41 reports that cell voltage channel B gives values inside the normal range that fail a plausibility check against the other cells. In GM's 2019 tables Hybrid Powertrain Control Processor 2 compares sample-to-sample changes: if the average cell voltage trends by at least 0.005 V while channel B stays unchanged, a failure is counted, and 35 of 40 samples at 100 ms set the code, Type A, one trip, with system voltage above 10.2 V. FCA calls it Voltage Sense 2 Circuit Performance on the Pacifica plug-in hybrid and lists it with P0B3C and further channels in battery pack control module update bulletins. Circuit, low, high and erratic faults of channel B are P0B40, P0B42, P0B43 and P0B44. Common causes: Battery controller software, fixed by reprogramming (FCA Pacifica) (high likelihood); Cell voltage measurement channel frozen inside the monitoring electronics (medium likelihood); High resistance in the cell sense line or its connection (medium likelihood); Cell monitoring board failure inside the pack (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, often with several voltage sense codes; Electric drive reduced or unavailable; Contactor related codes stored at the same time. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B42 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Low
text: P0B42: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Low. P0B42 sets when cell voltage channel B reads implausibly low, below what any usable cell would show. GM's battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, and only when no open sense line, slave communication or balancing fault is present. FCA uses P0B42 as Voltage Sense 2 Circuit Low on the 2022 Grand Wagoneer and Wagoneer with the 5.7 L eTorque mild hybrid; its bulletin calls the MIL false, mentions inoperative start-stop and a car that seems to run on fuel only, and prescribes a battery pack control module update. Cells that are actually weak set separate cell voltage codes. High and range faults are P0B43 and P0B41. Common causes: Battery pack control module software causing a false MIL (FCA eTorque) (high likelihood); Sense line shorted to the adjacent line or to the cell negative (medium likelihood); Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on; Start-stop inoperative; Vehicle behaves as if running on the engine only. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B43 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit High
text: P0B43: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit High. P0B43 sets when cell voltage channel B reads higher than a lithium-ion cell can physically reach in service, so the controller blames the measurement path. GM documents the criteria for its battery energy control module: cell voltage B at 4.8 V or above for 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A, one trip, with open sense line, communication and balancing faults ruled out first. Beyond GM, no manufacturer documents P0B43 publicly; FCA's sister code P0B3E for channel A shows that software in the battery controller can cause such readings. CARB treats battery voltage sensors as monitored input components. Overcharged cells use separate cell voltage codes. Low, range and open faults of channel B are P0B42, P0B41 and P0B40. Common causes: Open sense line letting the input float high (high likelihood); Battery controller software misreading the channel (medium likelihood); Measurement input of the cell monitoring chip failed (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning on; Charging or electric drive limited. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B44 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B44: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B44 is the J2012 slot for a cell voltage channel B whose reading jumps or drops out for short moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents P0B44 publicly. CARB requires the storage system's voltage sensors to be monitored as inputs and faults to be pinpointed to the smallest replaceable unit. Typical causes are vibration-loosened cell taps and connectors on the monitoring board. Warnings may come and go with driving conditions. Common causes: Loose or cracked cell tap connection (high likelihood); Fretting or vibration damage at the monitoring board connector (medium likelihood); Electrical noise from inverter or motor coupling into the sense lines (medium likelihood). Symptoms: MIL or hybrid warning that comes and goes; Occasional loss of electric drive or assist. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B45 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit
text: P0B45: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit. Voltage sense C is the third cell or cell-group measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics, not a pack voltage input like P0ABA. P0B45 reports an electrical break in that channel. GM's battery energy control module sets it when its open sense line test fails for 0.6 s: adjacent cell readings at least 1.3 V apart, a cell below 36 mV while its balancing switch is on, or a splice above 0.1 V (bus bar splice 0.5 V); Type A, one trip. Ford lists P0B45 with the other open-line codes on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid, fixed by a new traction battery, and on the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit, where an intermittent BECM flexible printed circuit is blamed. Expect no start or no charging. Common causes: Open cell sense tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel C (high likelihood); Intermittent flexible printed circuit between cells and battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit) (medium likelihood); Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV) (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Vehicle does not start or does not become ready to drive; High-voltage battery no longer charges; Powertrain warning (wrench) and Stop Safely Now message. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B46 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B46: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Range/Performance. With P0B46 the channel C wiring is intact; the value on it looks plausible but no longer behaves like a real cell. The 2016 Chevrolet Volt uses a window of 7 out of 8 seconds instead. Chrysler calls the code Voltage Sense 3 Circuit Performance on the 2020 Pacifica plug-in hybrid and cures it by reflashing the battery pack control module. So before opening the battery, check the controller software level. Common causes: Battery controller software misjudging the channel, fixed by reflash (Chrysler Pacifica PHEV) (high likelihood); Measuring chip input for channel C stuck at a constant value (medium likelihood); High-resistance cell tap damping the channel C signal (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on without noticeable driving fault; Reduced electric power or hybrid assist; Contactor or precharge codes stored at the same time (Pacifica). Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B47 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Low
text: P0B47: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Low. P0B47 is stored when channel C delivers a voltage too low to come from a working cell or block, so the controller blames the measurement rather than the battery. GM documents two implementations. On lithium-ion packs the battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, one trip, unless an open sense line, communication or balancing fault is already active. On the 2012 Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado and Sierra two-mode hybrids channel C is nickel-metal hydride block 3; there block 3 and block 4 must both read under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips. Shorted sense lines or a failed measuring input are the usual suspects. Common causes: Sense lines of channel C shorted to each other or to a neighbouring tap (high likelihood); Failed measuring input in the battery monitoring module (medium likelihood); Loose or corroded block connector shared by blocks 3 and 4 (GM two-mode) (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL; Electric drive or engine start-stop no longer available; Battery power limited, sluggish acceleration. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B48 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit High
text: P0B48: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit High. No healthy lithium-ion cell reaches 4.8 V, which is why GM's battery energy control module treats a channel C reading of 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within a 2 s window as a sensing fault and stores P0B48, Type A, one trip. On the 2012 two-mode full-size hybrids the threshold is scaled to a nickel-metal hydride block: block 3 above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B, two trips. Because the controller cannot trust the reading, it usually narrows the allowed charge and discharge power to protect the cells. For the driver this means less electric assist and possibly no plug-in charging. A cell that is really overcharged triggers separate cell voltage codes, not this one. Common causes: Channel C sense line touching a tap of higher potential (high likelihood); Failed measuring input or reference in the monitoring electronics (medium likelihood); Monitoring software fault, check for controller updates (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning; Reduced charge and discharge power; Plug-in charging refused. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B49 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense C Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

title: P0B4A – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit
text: P0B4A: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit. P0B4A is the open-circuit code of cell sense channel D, the fourth measuring channel of the battery monitoring electronics. For diagnosis, the pattern matters: if P0B4A stands alone, inspect the channel D tap and its connector; if Ford's whole open-line group from P0B3B upwards is set, as on the 2019-2020 Fusion PHEV or the 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit, a common cause such as the BECM flex cable or the battery itself is more likely. Common causes: Open channel D sense tap or connector (code set alone) (high likelihood); Faulty BECM flexible printed circuit affecting several channels (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit) (medium likelihood); Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV) (medium likelihood). Symptoms: No start or vehicle will not go into ready mode; Charging not possible; Several sense channel codes stored together. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B4B – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Range/Performance

title: P0B4C – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Low
text: P0B4C: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Low. From the driver's seat P0B4C looks like a battery problem: the hybrid warning comes on and electric power is cut back. title: P0B4D – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit High
text: P0B4D: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit High. P0B4D sets when cell sense channel D reports more voltage than the cell or block behind it can deliver. title: P0B4E – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B4E: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense D Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B4E completes the five-code set of cell channel D. Where P0B4A means a lasting open circuit, P0B4B a frozen or implausible value and P0B4C or P0B4D a reading beyond fixed limits, this code is meant for short, irregular dropouts and spikes. No manufacturer documents P0B4E publicly, and GM's published hybrid tables, which cover the other four, contain no such test. CARB obliges manufacturers to monitor the storage system's voltage sensors as input components. In practice, intermittent sense faults trace back to vibration, thermal cycling and connectors that only lose contact on rough roads, which is why the fault often cannot be reproduced in the workshop. Common causes: Connector or tap losing contact under vibration (high likelihood); Solder joint or crimp cracked by thermal cycling (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Intermittent hybrid warning, often on rough roads; Fault not reproducible during workshop test. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B4F – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit
text: P0B4F: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit. Symptoms: No start; Battery cannot be charged; Stop Safely Now message while driving. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

text: P0B51: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit Low. P0B51 tells that cell sense channel E reads near zero. title: P0B52 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit High
text: P0B52: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense E Circuit High. The threshold behind P0B52 is chosen so that only a measurement error can reach it. title: P0B5E – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit
text: P0B5E: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit. P0B5E flags a broken measuring path on voltage sense H, the eighth cell tap channel read by the battery monitoring electronics. In GM's 2019 tables the battery energy control module runs an open sense line test within a 0.6 s window: neighbouring cells diverging by 1.3 V or more, a cell under 36 mV while its balancing switch is on, or a splice above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a bus bar splice) sets it as Type A. Ford names P0B5E in two bulletins: a no-start on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid, repaired with a new traction battery, and the 2023 Mustang Mach-E and E-Transit, where H is the last code of the affected range and an intermittent flexible printed circuit at the BECM is blamed. Starting and charging may fail. Common causes: Intermittent flexible printed circuit cable at the battery controller (Ford Mach-E, E-Transit 2023) (high likelihood); Open cell tap, splice or bus bar connection on channel H (medium likelihood); Internal traction battery failure requiring pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV) (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Powertrain malfunction (wrench) indicator and Stop Safely Now message; Vehicle does not start or does not become ready to drive; High-voltage battery cannot be charged. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B5F – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B5F: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Range/Performance. With P0B5F the channel H wiring is intact, but the value it delivers does not fit the rest of the battery. GM runs two quite different plausibility tests. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids (Tahoe, Yukon, Escalade, Silverado, Sierra) channel H is nickel-metal hydride block 8 of 20; the battery pack control module multiplies blocks 8 and 9 by twenty and fails the test when both differ from the measured pack voltage by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B, two trips, with active pack voltage codes P0ABB to P0ABD blocking it. Lithium-ion systems in the 2019 tables look for a frozen reading instead: if H stays put while the average cell voltage trends, 35 of 40 samples set the code, Type A. Common causes: Block or cell voltage input for channel H drifting away from the true value (high likelihood); Measuring chip input stuck at a constant value (medium likelihood); Faulty pack voltage reference distorting the comparison (low likelihood). Symptoms: Hybrid system warning with MIL; Reduced electric assist or regeneration; Inaccurate state-of-charge display. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B60 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Low
text: P0B60: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Low. P0B60 means channel H reports less voltage than any healthy cell or block could hold, so the measurement itself is suspect. GM publishes three variants. Lithium-ion packs with a battery energy control module (2016 and 2019 tables) trip at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A, provided no open-line, communication or balancing fault is already stored. The BAS Plus mild hybrid in table 13OBDG05C uses a cell sense line threshold of 1.4 V and needs 7 failures out of 10, Type B. The 2012 two-mode trucks compare blocks 8 and 9, both under 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Typical culprits are a sense lead shorted to ground or a failed input on the monitoring board. Common causes: Channel H sense lead shorted to ground or to the next lower tap (high likelihood); Failed measuring input on the cell monitoring board (medium likelihood); Cell or block on channel H actually collapsed (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and hybrid or EV system warning; Electric drive power limited or switched off; Charging interrupted. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B61 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit High
text: P0B61: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit High. A lithium-ion cell cannot sit much above about 4.2 V, so when channel H reads 4.8 V or more the GM battery energy control module concludes the sense circuit is wrong and stores P0B61 after 1.4 s within a 2 s window, Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets the same code at more than 4.65 V on the cell sense line in 7 of 10 samples, Type B, while the 2012 two-mode hybrids treat H as nickel-metal hydride block 8 and only object above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. A high reading usually comes from a sense lead touching a higher potential or from a monitoring input that floats when a reference connection is lost. Unlike P0B60 the controller here suspects overvoltage, so charging is typically blocked. Common causes: Channel H sense lead in contact with a higher cell tap (high likelihood); Lost reference connection letting the measuring input float (medium likelihood); Internal fault of the cell monitoring chip (low likelihood). Symptoms: Charging refused or stopped early; MIL with reduced electric power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B62 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B62: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense H Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B62 describes a channel H signal that jumps or cuts out for moments rather than failing permanently. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. It is worth noting that Ford's 2023 Mach-E and E-Transit bulletin attributes an intermittent flexible printed circuit fault to the open-circuit code P0B5E, not to P0B62, and GM's published tables contain no erratic monitor for channel H at all. The code is therefore defined by SAE J2012 but appears to remain unused in practice. CARB demands that battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system be checked like every other input. If it ever appears, logging channel H next to channels G and I while moving the harness is the sensible first step. Common causes: Intermittent contact at the channel H connector or flexible circuit (high likelihood); Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board (medium likelihood); Inverter noise coupling into the sense line (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning appears occasionally and clears after a restart; Short interruptions of electric drive. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B63 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit
text: P0B63: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit. Channel I is the ninth sense input of the battery monitoring chain, and P0B63 reports that its circuit is open. GM shows how differently this can be detected. The BAS Plus mild hybrid (table 13OBDG05C) watches the voltage of line N and its neighbour N-1: if both drop under 1.4 V and change by more than 0.5 V within 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples set the code, Type B. The newer battery energy control module of the 2019 tables relies on neighbouring cells drifting 1.3 V apart, a balancing test below 36 mV or a splice voltage, all within 0.6 s, Type A. Ford lists P0B63 among the open-line codes behind a no-start on the 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid and replaces the traction battery. Common causes: Broken channel I sense wire, crimp or cell tap (high likelihood); Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV) (medium likelihood); Corroded or loose connector at the cell monitoring board (low likelihood). Symptoms: Vehicle will not start or enter ready mode; Service hybrid or EV system warning; Electric mode unavailable. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B64 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B64: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Range/Performance. P0B64 is a rationality fault: channel I is connected and reads a believable number, yet it does not move with the other cells. GM's 2016 Chevrolet Volt compares the movement of each cell with the average; if channel I does not follow when the average moves by more than 0.022 V, 7 out of 8 seconds fail the check, Type A. The 2019 hybrid powertrain control processor 2 tables keep the idea but count samples, 35 failures out of 40 at 100 ms. On the 2012 two-mode trucks the same code belongs to nickel-metal hydride block 9, whose scaled value must stay within 70 V of the pack voltage. Because the input is alive but stuck or drifting, a software update or the monitoring board is a likelier fix than wiring. Common causes: Channel I measuring input frozen at a constant value (high likelihood); Battery controller software misjudging the channel (medium likelihood); High-resistance cell tap damping the signal (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, vehicle drives normally; Reduced hybrid assist or electric range. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B65 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Low
text: P0B65: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Low. The 2012 GM two-mode hybrids show a detail worth knowing for P0B65: their battery pack control module only declares channel I, nickel-metal hydride block 9, too low when block 9 and its neighbour block 10 both read under 2 V, and only after 15 of 20 samples at 100 ms; the fault is Type B and needs two trips. A single weak block alone therefore does not set it. GM's lithium-ion controllers judge each cell on its own, setting P0B65 at 0.2 V or less held for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A, as long as no open-line or communication fault has priority. The BAS Plus mild hybrid uses 1.4 V and 7 of 10 samples. In all cases the reading is too low to be a real cell. Common causes: Channel I sense lead shorted to ground or a lower tap (high likelihood); Connector fault affecting adjacent blocks 9 and 10 (two-mode) (medium likelihood); Failed measuring input in the battery controller (low likelihood). Symptoms: Hybrid system warning and MIL; Engine runs more often, electric assist reduced; Limited power in limp mode. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B66 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit High
text: P0B66: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit High. When channel I claims a voltage above what its cell or block can physically reach, the controller stores P0B66. The thresholds GM publishes depend on chemistry and architecture: lithium-ion packs with a battery energy control module set it at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A, one trip; the BAS Plus mild hybrid at above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B; the 2012 two-mode trucks, which measure nickel-metal hydride block 9 rather than single cells, above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Every limit sits clearly above normal full charge, so a real overcharged cell is unlikely. Look first for a sense lead touching the next tap up or for a measuring input that has lost its reference. Common causes: Channel I lead touching a higher-potential tap (high likelihood); Open reference or ground of the measuring chip (medium likelihood); Genuinely overcharged cell after a charging control fault (low likelihood). Symptoms: Charging stops or is refused; MIL and reduced power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B67 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B67: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense I Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. SAE J2012 reserves P0B67 for an unsteady signal on channel I, meaning readings that spike, drop and recover. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the GM tables that define the other four channel I codes includes an erratic test. The fault picture would sit between an open circuit (P0B63) and a frozen value (P0B64): the line works most of the time but loses contact under vibration, heat or current load. CARB requires battery voltage sensors to be monitored as inputs of the energy storage system, which explains why the code exists at all. For diagnosis, record cell voltage I with a scan tool during a drive and compare its noise with neighbouring channels H and J. Common causes: Sense contact on channel I opening under vibration or heat (high likelihood); Corroded terminal in the module connector (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Sporadic warning without a reproducible pattern; Momentary drop in electric power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B68 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit
text: P0B68: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit. For owners of a 2019 or 2020 Ford Fusion plug-in hybrid, P0B68 is best known from bulletin 23-2039: the car will not start, the battery energy control module stores one or more open sense line codes from P0B3B to P0B7C, and the prescribed repair is a complete high-voltage traction battery. Technically the code says that the tenth measuring channel, J, has lost its connection to the cells. GM describes the test in detail for its lithium-ion packs: within 0.6 s it looks for adjacent cells 1.3 V apart, a cell under 36 mV while being balanced, or splice voltages above 0.1 V or 0.5 V, and sets P0B68 as Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid uses a 1.4 V and 0.5 V rate-of-change test, Type B. Common causes: Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020) (high likelihood); Open sense wire or cell tap on channel J (medium likelihood); Bad bus bar or splice connection near channel J (low likelihood). Symptoms: No start, vehicle does not become ready; Hybrid system warning on the cluster; Plug-in charging unavailable. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B69 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B69: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Range/Performance. P0B69 is set when channel J is electrically present but its readings do not behave plausibly. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid explains the logic most clearly: once the average cell voltage moves by more than 0.045 V, the cell under test must move in the same direction and by at least half as much; 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, two trips. The 2019 lithium-ion tables use a tighter trigger of 0.022 V and 35 of 40 samples, Type A. On the 2012 two-mode trucks the code belongs to nickel-metal hydride block 10 and compares its scaled value with the pack voltage. Neither Ford nor Chrysler publishes this channel; Chrysler's Pacifica bulletin stops at sense 6. Common causes: Channel J input reacting too little to real voltage changes (high likelihood); Corroded or high-resistance cell tap (medium likelihood); Calibration error in the battery controller (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL without obvious driveability problem; Hybrid assist reduced. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B6A – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Low
text: P0B6A: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Low. A reading of almost zero on channel J points to the measurement, not to the cell, and that is what P0B6A records. In GM's lithium-ion systems (2016 and 2019 tables) the battery energy control module sets it at 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A. The interesting part is what it ignores: while a module communication loss, an open sense line code, a balancing fault or an internal module fault is active, P0B6A stays silent so that the root cause is stored first. The 2012 two-mode hybrids look at nickel-metal hydride block 10 together with block 11, both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. Expect reduced or no electric drive until the circuit is repaired. Common causes: Channel J lead chafed through and shorted to ground (high likelihood); Damaged measuring input on the monitoring board (medium likelihood); Cell on channel J internally shorted (low likelihood). Symptoms: Electric drive limited or unavailable; MIL and battery warning message. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B6B – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit High
text: P0B6B: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit High. On GM's 2012 two-mode hybrid trucks the battery is divided into 20 nickel-metal hydride blocks, and channel J is block 10. The battery pack control module samples it every 100 ms while the 12 V supply is between 9 and 18 V; if block 10 reports more than 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, P0B6B is stored as Type B, so the MIL comes on after the second trip. Lithium-ion GM packs check single cells instead and set the code at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A; the BAS Plus mild hybrid uses 4.65 V. Since these limits lie well above any real charge level, a wiring short to a higher tap or a faulty sense input is the expected finding, not an overcharged battery. Common causes: Channel J lead shorted to a higher block or cell tap (high likelihood); Faulty measuring input in the battery pack control module (medium likelihood). Symptoms: MIL after the second drive (Type B systems); Charging or regeneration restricted; Reduced electric power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B6C – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B6C: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense J Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. No manufacturer documents P0B6C publicly. The code stands for a channel J signal that is unstable, with brief jumps or dropouts, as opposed to the steady faults covered by P0B68 to P0B6B. CARB section 1968.2 requires that the individual electronic inputs of a hybrid energy storage system, battery voltage sensors expressly included, be monitored for circuit and rationality faults; erratic behaviour is one way such a fault can show. GM, which publishes tests for the other four channel J codes, lists none for this one. For the driver it would mean a warning that comes and goes, possibly with short power cuts. A cable or connector with marginal contact is the most plausible cause. Common causes: Marginal contact in the channel J harness or connector (high likelihood); Cracked solder joint on the monitoring electronics (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Intermittent warning light; Brief power reductions while driving. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B6D – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit
text: P0B6D: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit. P0B6D marks an open circuit on voltage sense K, the eleventh cell measuring channel. GM has used the code since its first published hybrid tables: in 2011 the open-line test already checked bus bar voltages, flagging more than 0.7 V. The 2019 battery energy control module refines it into seven cases, among them adjacent cells 1.3 V apart, a cell under 36 mV with balancing active and splice voltages over 0.1 V, all judged in a 0.6 s window and set as Type A. Ford counts P0B6D among the open sense line codes that leave a 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrid unable to start and fixes it by replacing the traction battery. Before any pack work, the high-voltage system has to be disabled by trained staff. Common causes: Loose or corroded bus bar connection at the channel K tap (high likelihood); Internal traction battery fault, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV) (medium likelihood); Broken sense wire between cells and monitoring board (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Vehicle not ready to drive; Hybrid or EV system warning with MIL; Charging not possible. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B6E – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B6E: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Range/Performance. In a nickel-metal hydride pack with 20 equal blocks, twenty times one block voltage should roughly equal the whole pack voltage. GM's 2012 two-mode hybrids use exactly this for P0B6E, assigned to block 11: the battery pack control module checks blocks 11 and 12, and if both scaled values deviate from the pack voltage sensor by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, the code is set, Type B. The test only runs with the contactors closed for over 200 ms and no pack voltage fault active. GM's lithium-ion controllers judge channel K differently, as a frozen value that fails to follow the average cell voltage (35 of 40 samples, Type A, in the 2019 tables). No other manufacturer publishes it. Common causes: Block or cell voltage measurement of channel K out of calibration (high likelihood); Pack voltage sensor reading off, distorting the comparison (medium likelihood); Measuring input stuck at one value (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL after two trips; Less electric assist, more engine running. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B6F – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Low
text: P0B6F: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Low. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid, the eAssist system in table 13OBDG05C, gives P0B6F a simple rule: if the cell sense line for channel K measures below 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples at 200 ms while the 12 V supply is above 8.8 V, the code is stored as Type B, two trips. Since a lithium-ion cell in use never falls that low, the value must come from a short or a failed input. GM's later battery energy control modules work with 0.2 V and a 1.4 s window, Type A, and the 2012 two-mode trucks with nickel-metal hydride blocks 11 and 12, both under 2 V. The driver typically sees a hybrid warning and loses electric assist; the engine takes over more of the work. Common causes: Channel K sense line shorted to ground or a lower tap (high likelihood); Failed measuring input in the battery interface module (medium likelihood); Blown protective element in the sense line (low likelihood). Symptoms: Hybrid warning and MIL after the second trip; Auto stop and electric assist disabled. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B70 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit High
text: P0B70: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit High. P0B70 says that cell voltage K reads too high to be genuine. GM's 2019 battery energy control module sets it at 4.8 V or more, held for 1.4 s within 2 s, as a Type A fault with immediate MIL, and only when no communication loss, open sense line or internal module fault takes precedence. The same principle appears with other numbers elsewhere at GM: 4.65 V and 7 of 10 samples on the BAS Plus mild hybrid, 23 V for nickel-metal hydride block 11 on the 2012 two-mode trucks. The difference to P0B6F is the direction, not the location: a high reading typically comes from a lead touching a higher potential, a low one from a short to a lower one. Charging is usually blocked while it is active. Common causes: Channel K lead in contact with a higher tap (high likelihood); Floating measuring input after loss of its lower reference (medium likelihood); Cell monitoring chip fault (low likelihood). Symptoms: Charging blocked; MIL and power limitation. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B71 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B71: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense K Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B71 belongs to the unsteady fault type: the channel K reading flickers or drops out momentarily without staying beyond a fixed limit. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Neither GM's hybrid tables from 2011 to 2019 nor the Ford and Chrysler bulletins on cell sense codes mention it, although they cover the open, plausibility, low and high codes of neighbouring channels. Its basis is the CARB requirement to monitor battery voltage sensors of the energy storage system as input components. In a workshop the approach would be a wiggle test on the module harness while watching cell voltage K live, plus a check of the connector terminals for fretting corrosion. Common causes: Fretting corrosion on channel K connector terminals (high likelihood); Sense harness under strain losing contact with movement (medium likelihood). Symptoms: Warning that comes and goes; Occasional short loss of electric power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B72 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit
text: P0B72: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit. P0B72 reports an open circuit on voltage sense L, the twelfth channel. One detail sets it apart from its neighbours: GM's 2011 hybrid tables list every open sense line code from P0B3B upward except P0B72 (and P0B90), so the early system did not use it, while L's range, low and high codes were present. Later GM tables include it. The BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it when lines N and N-1 fall below 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B; the 2019 battery energy control module uses its adjacent-cell, balancing and splice tests within 0.6 s, Type A. Ford's Fusion plug-in hybrid bulletin for 2019-2020 includes P0B72 and replaces the traction battery. Common causes: Open sense lead, crimp or cell tap on channel L (high likelihood); Internal traction battery failure, pack replacement (Ford Fusion PHEV) (medium likelihood); High-resistance splice or bus bar joint (low likelihood). Symptoms: No start or no ready mode; Battery or hybrid system warning; Charging aborted. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B73 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B73: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Range/Performance. Channel L delivers a value, but P0B73 tells you that the value is not credible. GM checks this in three ways. The 2016 Chevrolet Volt and the 2019 lithium-ion systems test whether cell L moves in the same direction as the average once that average changes by more than 0.022 V, failing 7 of 8 seconds or 35 of 40 samples respectively, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid demands at least half of the average movement, 20 of 40 samples, Type B. The 2012 two-mode trucks treat L as nickel-metal hydride block 12 and compare blocks 12 and 13, scaled by twenty, with the pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. A battery controller reflash or measuring board repair is the usual remedy. Common causes: Channel L input not following real cell voltage changes (high likelihood); Battery controller software or calibration issue (medium likelihood); Corroded cell tap slowing the signal (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL with normal driving behaviour; Reduced electric range or assist. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B74 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Low
text: P0B74: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Low. P0B74 is set when channel L reads implausibly low. A short of the sense lead to a lower potential, a defective monitoring input or, more rarely, a cell that has really collapsed are the candidates. The vehicle will normally restrict electric operation. Common causes: Channel L sense lead shorted to a lower potential (high likelihood); Defective measuring input in the battery controller (medium likelihood); Cell or block on channel L actually failed (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and hybrid system warning; Electric operation restricted; Engine runs continuously on hybrids. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B75 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit High
text: P0B75: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit High. With P0B75 the battery controller rejects channel L because it reads above any value a real cell or block can reach. While it is active, charging and regeneration are normally limited to protect the pack. title: P0B76 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B76: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense L Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B76 closes the channel L group and covers an erratic signal: values that jump or vanish briefly while the circuit otherwise works. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, the only maker with public tables for L, defines open, plausibility, low and high tests for this channel but no erratic test, and the Ford bulletins name only the open-circuit code P0B72. CARB obliges manufacturers to monitor the battery voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system, which is the regulatory background of the code. Practically, an intermittent contact at the channel L tap, a fatigued harness or a cracked board joint would produce this picture. Warnings may disappear after a restart and return. Common causes: Intermittent contact at the channel L cell tap (high likelihood); Fatigued sense harness wire (medium likelihood); Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning clears after restart and comes back; Momentary power reduction. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B77 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit
text: P0B77: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit. P0B77 flags an open or high-resistance tap on voltage sense M, the thirteenth cell channel. GM's 2019 battery energy control module checks seven cases: adjacent cells differing by 1.3 V or more, a balancing gate reading below 36 mV, or splice voltages above 0.1 V (0.5 V at a busbar splice). M is the last channel there with the short 0.6 s window, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid instead needs lines N and N-1 both below 1.4 V plus a jump over 0.5 V within 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Ford's TSB 23-2039 names P0B77 for 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids that no longer start and prescribes a new traction battery. Range, low and high faults on M carry their own codes. Common causes: Open or corroded tap of sense lead M at the cell connector (high likelihood); Fault inside the traction battery (Ford Fusion PHEV TSB 23-2039) (medium likelihood); High resistance at a splice or busbar joint in the sense path (medium likelihood); Defective cell monitoring board input (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL with hybrid or EV system warning; Vehicle may not start or go into ready mode; Charging blocked or limited. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B78 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B78: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Range/Performance. With P0B78 the controller doubts the reading of channel M rather than its wiring. GM's 2019 hybrid powertrain processor watches for a frozen value: whenever the average of all cells moves by more than 0.022 V, cell M must follow by at least 0.005 V in the same direction, and 35 failures in 40 samples at 100 ms set a Type A fault. The 2012 two-mode trucks map M to nickel-metal hydride block 13 and multiply blocks 13 and 14 by twenty; if that estimate misses the pack voltage by more than 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, the code is stored as Type B. The BAS Plus mild hybrid wants at least half the average movement, 20 of 40 samples, Type B. A plausible but wrong value is often a controller or measuring board issue. Common causes: Measuring channel M stuck at a fixed value (high likelihood); Battery controller software needing an update (medium likelihood); Block 13 voltage drifting from the pack on two-mode NiMH packs (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on, often without noticeable driving change; Reduced electric assist or regeneration. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B79 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Low
text: P0B79: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Low. P0B79 means that the voltage reported for sense M is too low to be real. GM's lithium-ion battery controllers of 2016 and 2019 set it at 0.2 V or less, held for 1.4 s inside a 2 s window, Type A, and only while no open sense line fault is active, so a broken lead is reported by P0B77 first. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids M is block 13: the battery pack control module needs block 13 and block 14 both below 2 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. The BAS Plus mild hybrid uses 1.4 V, 7 of 10 samples, with the 12 V supply above 8.8 V. Typical sources are a sense lead shorted towards ground or a lower cell, a failed measuring input, or rarely a cell that has truly collapsed. Common causes: Sense lead M shorted to ground or a lower cell potential (high likelihood); Failed measuring input on the monitoring board (medium likelihood); Cell or NiMH block on channel M actually collapsed (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and service hybrid or EV system message; Electric drive or assist disabled; Engine runs continuously on hybrids. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B7A – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit High
text: P0B7A: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit High. A reading on channel M above what any healthy cell can deliver produces P0B7A. For lithium-ion packs GM sets the line at 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in a 2 s window and treats it as Type A, illuminating the MIL on the first trip. The BAS Plus mild hybrid already reacts above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Where M stands for NiMH block 13, as on the 2012 two-mode trucks, a block voltage above 23 V for 15 of 20 samples is the trigger, again Type B, with the 12 V system between 9 and 18 V. Because a cell itself rarely climbs that high, a sense lead touching a higher potential or a faulty measuring input is far more likely than overcharging. The vehicle will usually limit charging and electric drive. Common causes: Sense lead M in contact with a higher cell potential (high likelihood); Measuring input of channel M reading high (medium likelihood); Real overvoltage of the cell after a balancing fault (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL on from the first trip (GM lithium-ion, Type A); Charging stopped or limited; Reduced electric power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B7B – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B7B: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense M Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B7B is reserved for a sense M signal that flickers: short dropouts or jumps while the circuit is otherwise intact. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's tables for channel M contain open, plausibility, low and high tests but no erratic test, and Ford's Fusion bulletin lists only the open-circuit code P0B77. The legal footing is CARB 1968.2, which requires the battery voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system to be monitored as electronic components and demands fault codes that point to the smallest replaceable unit. In practice a loose crimp at the M tap, a chafed lead in the sense harness or a cracked solder joint on the monitoring board would cause such a signal. Expect warnings that come and go. Common causes: Loose crimp or connector at the channel M tap (high likelihood); Chafed wire in the cell sense harness (medium likelihood); Cracked solder joint on the monitoring board (low likelihood). Symptoms: Hybrid warning appearing and clearing again; Brief drops in electric power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B7C – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit
text: P0B7C: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit. Voltage sense N, the fourteenth channel, reports a broken or high-resistance sense lead with P0B7C. It is the last code in Ford's TSB 23-2039: 2019-2020 Fusion plug-in hybrids that fail to start with any open-circuit code from P0B3B up to P0B7C get a replacement traction battery; the bulletin names no channel beyond N. In GM's 2019 battery controller tables N is the first channel whose open test runs 0.8 s within a 1.6 s window instead of 0.6 s, while the criteria (1.3 V adjacent-cell difference, 36 mV balancing gate, splice limits) stay the same, Type A. A second GM program of 2016 closes the balancing gates in a test pattern, turns the voltage drop into a sense-line resistance and fails above 30.00 in 7 of 9 samples, Type A. Common causes: Internal traction battery fault (Ford Fusion PHEV 2019-2020) (high likelihood); Sense lead N broken or with excessive resistance (medium likelihood); Fault on the cell monitoring board (low likelihood). Symptoms: No start or vehicle does not become ready; MIL and stop-safely or service message; Plug-in charging unavailable. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B7D – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B7D: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Range/Performance. P0B7D concerns a channel N value that stays inside its limits yet does not behave like a real cell. GM's 2016 tables show how the same check is tuned per vehicle: the Chevrolet Volt fails when cell N does not move with the average for 7 of 8 seconds, while the Cadillac ELR counts 20 of 40 samples at 200 ms once the average shifts by more than 0.006 V; both are Type A. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids N corresponds to NiMH block 14, and blocks 14 and 15 scaled by twenty must agree with the pack voltage within 70 V, otherwise 160 of 170 samples set a Type B code. The 2019 processor uses its 0.005 V trend test, 35 of 40 samples. Often a battery controller reflash or a board repair is the fix. Common causes: Channel N value not tracking the other cells (high likelihood); Outdated battery controller calibration (medium likelihood); Block 14 or 15 voltage mismatch on two-mode NiMH packs (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL with hybrid service message; Shorter electric range or less assist. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B7E – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Low
text: P0B7E: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Low. P0B7E sets when channel N reads below the lower plausibility limit. GM's 2016 program with a separate battery sense module uses less than 0.20 V and needs 14 failures in 18 samples, about 1.8 s at 100 ms each, before a Type A fault; the open-circuit test must not be failing at the same time. The other GM lithium-ion controllers use 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s in 2 s, also Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid works with 1.4 V and 7 of 10 samples, Type B. On 2012 two-mode trucks N is NiMH block 14, and blocks 14 and 15 must both drop under 2 V. A low reading usually comes from the measuring path, not from the cell: a lead shorted to a lower potential or a damaged input stage. Common causes: Sense lead N shorted to a lower potential (high likelihood); Damaged input stage in the sense module (medium likelihood); Deeply discharged or failed cell on channel N (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL from the first trip on lithium-ion GM systems; Hybrid system limits power; Combustion engine does not shut off at standstill. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B7F – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit High
text: P0B7F: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit High. Channel N reporting more voltage than a cell can hold leads to P0B7F. GM uses three thresholds depending on the system: 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s on most lithium-ion battery controllers, above 4.90 V in 14 of 18 samples on the 2016 program with a separate sense module, both Type A, and above 4.65 V in 7 of 10 samples on the BAS Plus mild hybrid, Type B. The 2012 two-mode trucks treat N as NiMH block 14 and set the code above 23 V in 15 of 20 samples, Type B. The low counterpart is P0B7E, an open lead is P0B7C. Before suspecting the cell, a technician checks whether the N lead touches a neighbouring higher potential or whether the measuring input has drifted. Common causes: Sense lead N touching a higher potential (high likelihood); Drifted measuring input in the battery controller (medium likelihood); Real overvoltage of the cell on channel N (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and warning in the instrument cluster; Regenerative braking and charging limited. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B80 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B80: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense N Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B80 describes an unsteady channel N signal: the voltage drops out or jumps for moments, then looks normal again. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Ford's Fusion plug-in bulletin, which reaches exactly up to channel N, cites only the open-circuit code P0B7C, and GM's tables give channel N open, rationality, low and high diagnostics without a separate erratic test. Background is CARB 1968.2, under which battery voltage sensors in a hybrid energy storage system count as monitored components with their own fault codes. If a vehicle does store it, the trigger would be a contact that opens under vibration or temperature change, for example at the N tap, in the harness connector or at a board joint. Restarting may hide the fault for a while. Common causes: Contact at the N tap opening under vibration (high likelihood); Fretting corrosion in the sense harness connector (medium likelihood); Solder joint cracking with temperature cycles (low likelihood). Symptoms: Intermittent hybrid warning; Fault not present after restart; Occasional loss of electric power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B81 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit
text: P0B81: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit. P0B81 stands for an open sense lead on channel O, the fifteenth cell tap. GM has used it from the start: the 2011 Volt battery tables already list P0B81 among the open sense line codes and detect, among other cases, a busbar connection voltage above 0.7 V. In the 2019 battery energy control module the test needs 0.8 s within a 1.6 s window, with adjacent cells 1.3 V or more apart or a balancing gate below 36 mV, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid compares lines N and N-1, both under 1.4 V with a change above 0.5 V in 200 ms, 7 of 10 samples, Type B. Unlike channels M and N, P0B81 does not appear in Ford's Fusion plug-in bulletin. With the lead open, the controller loses sight of that cell and limits operation. Common causes: Loose or high-resistance busbar joint at the O tap (high likelihood); Broken sense wire O in the battery harness (medium likelihood); Faulty cell sense module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and propulsion system warning; Reduced power or no electric drive. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B82 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B82: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Range/Performance. P0B82 is a plausibility verdict on channel O. GM's 2016 program with a battery sense module asks cell O to trend at least 0.002 V in the direction of the average whenever the average moves by more than 0.022 V; 35 failed evaluations out of 40 set a Type A code. The 2019 controllers use the same logic with 0.005 V. Where O is NiMH block 15, on the 2012 two-mode hybrids, the battery pack control module multiplies blocks 15 and 16 by twenty and compares the result with the pack voltage, failing beyond 70 V in 160 of 170 samples, Type B. The BAS Plus mild hybrid needs half the average movement, 20 of 40, Type B. Low, high and open faults on the same channel are reported separately as P0B83, P0B84 and P0B81. Common causes: Channel O reading frozen in the monitoring electronics (high likelihood); Battery controller software fault (medium likelihood); Rising resistance in the O sense tap distorting the reading (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL with otherwise normal driving; State of charge display jumps or is inaccurate. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B83 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Low
text: P0B83: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Low. P0B83 reports that channel O reads implausibly low. It is not the same as an open lead: GM's lithium-ion controllers run this check only while no open sense line fault is present, so a broken wire shows as P0B81 instead. The low limit there is 0.2 V or less for 1.4 s within 2 s, Type A. The BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it below 1.4 V in 7 of 10 samples, Type B. On the 2012 two-mode trucks, where O is NiMH block 15, block 15 and block 16 must both be under 2 V for 15 of 20 samples, Type B, with the 12 V supply between 9 and 18 V. Short circuits in the sense path towards ground or a lower cell are the main suspects; a genuinely dead cell is the exception and usually brings neighbouring codes as well. Common causes: Short in the O sense path towards ground or a lower cell (high likelihood); Monitoring input reading low (medium likelihood); Dead cell or NiMH block 15 (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and hybrid warning lamp; Electric operation switched off. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B84 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit High
text: P0B84: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit High. P0B84 is stored when channel O sits above the upper limit of a credible cell voltage. For GM lithium-ion packs that limit is 4.8 V, held 1.4 s in a 2 s window, Type A; the 2016 program with a separate sense module tolerates up to 4.90 V and counts 14 failures in 18 samples, also Type A. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid uses a lower ceiling of 4.65 V and a Type B rating. On the 2012 two-mode hybrids the reading belongs to NiMH block 15, which must exceed 23 V in 15 of 20 samples. For the driver the effect is a warning and a battery that is no longer charged fully or used for electric drive. Since true overvoltage is rare, the measuring lead and the input of the monitoring electronics are checked first. Common causes: Sense lead O shorted to a higher cell tap (high likelihood); Monitoring input of channel O reading too high (medium likelihood); Cell overcharged because balancing failed (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and battery warning; Charging ends early; Less electric assist. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B85 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B85: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense O Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B85 would mark a channel O signal that is present but unsteady, with spikes or brief gaps. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; even GM, whose public tables cover channel O in detail from 2011 onward, defines only the open, rationality, low and high tests for it. The requirement behind the code family comes from CARB 1968.2: voltage sensors of a hybrid energy storage system must be monitored like other electronic components, with fault codes that identify the part to replace. A plausible cause for such a signal is a contact resistance that changes with movement, heat or moisture, typically at the cell tap, the busbar screw or the connector of the sense harness. A fault that vanishes and returns calls for wiggle testing with live data. Common causes: Loose busbar screw changing contact resistance at tap O (high likelihood); Moisture or corrosion in the sense harness connector (medium likelihood); Cracked joint on the monitoring board (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning that comes and goes; Short-term power reduction during driving. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B86 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit
text: P0B86: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit. P0B86 belongs to channel P, the sixteenth sense lead, and indicates that this lead has lost its connection to the cell. Comparing GM's tables shows how the timing evolved: the 2016 Volt battery controller decides within 0.6 s, the 2019 version waits 0.8 s in a 1.6 s window; both use the 1.3 V adjacent-cell, 36 mV balancing gate and splice criteria and are Type A. GM's 2016 program with a separate sense module measures the sense line resistance instead, failing above 30.00 in 7 of 9 samples. On the BAS Plus mild hybrid the code is Type B after 7 of 10 samples showing lines N and N-1 below 1.4 V with a step over 0.5 V. Ford's public bulletins do not list P0B86. The pack usually has to come out for repair. Common causes: Sense lead P open at the cell tap or connector (high likelihood); Excessive resistance in the sense line (corrosion, loose screw) (medium likelihood); Defective input of the sense module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and hybrid system fault message; Vehicle runs only on the engine or with reduced power. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B87 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Range/Performance
text: P0B87: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Range/Performance. P0B87 says channel P is delivering numbers that do not fit the rest of the battery. On GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid the cell under test must move at least 50 percent as far as the average cell voltage; if not, 20 failures in 40 samples set the code as Type B, i.e. MIL after two trips. GM's 2019 lithium-ion processor is stricter in its rating, Type A after 35 of 40 samples, and looks for a value that stays flat by less than 0.005 V while the average moves more than 0.022 V. The 2012 two-mode trucks check NiMH block 16, together with block 17, against the pack voltage with a 70 V window, 160 of 170 samples, Type B. Since wiring faults have their own codes (P0B86, P0B88, P0B89), this one points towards measuring electronics or software. Common causes: Measuring electronics for channel P out of tolerance (high likelihood); Software or calibration of the battery controller (medium likelihood); NiMH block 16 or 17 out of balance with the pack (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL after two trips on Type B systems; Engine start-stop or electric assist less frequent. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B88 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Low
text: P0B88: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Low. A too-low value on sense P, the sixteenth channel, is what P0B88 records. GM's BAS Plus mild hybrid sets it at a cell sense line below 1.4 V for 7 of 10 samples, sampled every 200 ms and only with the 12 V battery above 8.8 V; it rates the fault Type B. The full lithium-ion systems in GM's 2016 and 2019 tables react at 0.2 V or less after 1.4 s in a 2 s window and set it as Type A. In the 2012 two-mode NiMH pack, P is block 16; blocks 16 and 17 must both stay below 2 V for 15 of 20 samples. A collapsed reading usually traces back to a short between the P lead and a lower potential, sometimes to a defective input; it is rarely the cell itself. The open-circuit condition is reported separately with P0B86. Common causes: Lead P shorted to a lower potential or chassis (high likelihood); Defective input in the battery interface module (medium likelihood); Weak cell or NiMH block 16 (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and reduced propulsion power; Auto stop no longer active. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B89 – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit High
text: P0B89: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit High. P0B89 covers the opposite case to P0B88: the voltage reported on channel P is above the plausible range. In lithium-ion systems GM sets 4.8 V or more for 1.4 s in 2 s as the limit, Type A, while the BAS Plus mild hybrid reacts above 4.65 V. GM's 2016 program with a separate sense module allows up to 4.90 V. Overcharging is unlikely to be the cause because the controller stops charging well below these values; a sense lead reaching a higher tap or an input fault is the usual explanation. Expect restricted charging. Common causes: Lead P in contact with a higher cell tap (high likelihood); Input fault in the cell monitoring electronics (medium likelihood); Genuine overvoltage of the cell or block (low likelihood). Symptoms: Charging restricted; MIL and hybrid warning. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B8A – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B8A: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense P Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B8A is the erratic-signal member of the channel P group. There is no public manufacturer documentation for it: GM describes open, rationality, low and high diagnostics for sense P in its 2016 and 2019 tables, but none for an intermittent signal, and the Ford bulletins stop at channel N. The code exists because CARB 1968.2 requires the voltage sensors of a hybrid battery to be monitored and malfunctions to be stored under distinct codes. If set, the picture would be a channel P value that briefly drops out or spikes, for instance through a fatigued wire near a bend in the sense harness or a connector that loses contact when the pack warms up. Readings in live data may look normal between the events. Common causes: Fatigued wire at a bend of the sense harness (high likelihood); Connector losing contact as the pack warms up (medium likelihood); Sporadic fault in the cell monitoring chip (low likelihood). Symptoms: Warning lamp that goes out again; Occasional engine start without demand on hybrids. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B8B – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit
text: P0B8B: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit. P0B8B marks an open circuit on voltage sense Q, the seventeenth channel. The two-mode NiMH trucks have no circuit code for block 17. Ford does not list it. Typically the vehicle restricts or blocks electric operation until repaired. Common causes: Sense lead Q open between cell tap and module (high likelihood); Loose or corroded connector at the second measuring group (medium likelihood); Fault in the battery interface module (low likelihood). Symptoms: MIL and service vehicle message; Electric operation blocked or limited; Fuel consumption rises on hybrids. Repair difficulty: shop_only.

title: P0B8C – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Range/Performance

title: P0B8F – Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
text: P0B8F: Hybrid/EV Battery Voltage Sense Q Circuit Intermittent/Erratic. P0B8F closes the channel Q group and stands for a sense Q signal that is erratic rather than absent or out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. GM's tables for sense Q, from the 2011 Volt to the 2019 battery controllers, list circuit, range, low and high monitors only, and the Ford Fusion bulletin ends four channels earlier at N. CARB 1968.2 forms the basis: it calls for monitoring of the battery voltage sensors in a hybrid energy storage system and for codes that lead a technician to the faulty part. Physically, an erratic Q reading would point to an unstable connection between tap and measuring chip, such as a cracked crimp, a damaged flexible circuit or a cold solder joint. The next channel, R, starts at P0B90. Common causes: Cracked crimp at the channel Q tap (high likelihood); Damaged flexible circuit between cells and monitoring board (medium likelihood); Cold solder joint at the measuring chip (low likelihood). Symptoms: Sporadic hybrid or EV warning; Power briefly reduced, normal after restart. Repair difficulty: shop_only.
